News.title: Attack mum's trauma of fighting early release plan
News.content:
Reacting to the announcement, Emma Webber said: "I'm glad it has happened, it is the right thing.

"But I'll tell you what wasn't the right thing, the trauma of victims, who have been through so much already, have had to go through to fight for this.

"Petitions, doing news interviews, having to talk about the terrible losses we have suffered and there are dozens of us that have had to do this.

"I try not to be always confrontational and always fighting but as much as I try not to, it seems to be the only way that things are getting done.

"Everything we have done as families in the Nottingham attacks has come at such great cost and yes we are getting results but we shouldn't have had to do any of it at all."

She said the controversy reflected wider problems with funding across the justice system.

"The fact that we were even having to consider releasing people who had taken lives and destroyed families and communities early from their sentences is abhorrent.

"I stand by what I said yesterday - it is morally bankrupt."

She also confirmed after making a call to meet ministers some weeks ago, they had now received an invitation to meet with Justice Secretary Alex Norris, where their concerns would be raised.

News.title: Third murder charge over Brent Council HQ stabbing
News.content:
A total of three people have now been charged with murder over the fatal stabbing of a 17-year-old boy at Brent Civic Centre in Wembley.

David Wynter died after he was attacked on Engineers Way at about 14:30 BST on 25 August.

A 15-year-old boy was charged with murder two days later, and two more teenagers - a 17-year-old boy and 18-year-old Jahquarn St Hillaire - were charged with murder and possession of an offensive weapon on Saturday.

The 15-year-old was remanded in custody and is due to appear at the Old Bailey on 24 September, with the other pair due at Willesden Magistrates' Court on Monday.

News.title: Dementia patient's deportation from Sweden delayed
News.content:
A man with dementia will be able to remain in Sweden while a legal bid to delay his deportation is considered.

The Swedish authorities said they wanted George Mason, originally from Hinckley in Leicestershire, to leave the country by midnight on 20 August, after his application for permanent residency was rejected.

Mason's daughter, Michelle Torossian, said the family had been told an injunction to halt his deportation would be decided by Swedish authorities in a timeframe of two weeks to six months.

Torossian said she was told by the British Embassy in Stockholm that the original deportation decision would not be enforced by the authorities while the injunction order was considered.

The BBC has contacted the Swedish Migration Agency, which said it was unable to comment on individual cases.

News.title: Girl faces six-month recovery after 'freak accident' bus crash on holiday
News.content:
After eight days in hospital, Greta was transported back to the UK for treatment with Williams in an air ambulance which their Â£106 travel insurance policy covered.

"They [the pilots and medics] told me it cost â¬50,000 just for the flight. That was quite scary, Â£106 paid for that. Anything can happen."

Williams said Jet2, which sold them the package holiday, waived the cost of changing Len and Eiry-ana's flights back to the UK.

Greta was admitted to The Grange University Hospital in Cwmbran and had physiotherapy, and will find out on 2 September whether she can return to school.

"We can't do anything until that assessment. It's strict bedrest at the minute.

"She's not allowed to do much, she's not allowed to walk loads or do much which is a massive shame. Her friends have been fantastic."

Williams added: "She was petrified when it happened. All she wanted was reassurance from me. We tried to keep it as positive as we could in the circumstances.

"She was phenomenally strong. I'm so proud of how she coped."

"This is something that's going to haunt us forever," added Williams.

"It's going to take a long time to get over it all. We need normality to hit first, as we're in the summer holidays, before we can process it properly.

"You can see the accident has impacted them, and being in a foreign country has escalated their fears.

"We were trying to fill it in with so many experiences and memories as possible to make it fun-filled.

"They don't want to go on holiday ever again. We're going to try and take them somewhere - probably not on an excursion - to ease their mind. It was a one-off freak accident, and these things don't generally happen."

Graeme Buck from the Association of British Travel Agents said travel insurance was "one of the must-haves whenever you travel overseas".

"While most holidays go ahead without any problems, accidents and unexpected events can happen, and the costs of medical treatment and getting home can be significant.

"Cheap isn't always the best, and it's important not to choose a policy based on price alone. Holidaymakers should check what their policy covers and make sure they have comprehensive cover that is appropriate for their trip, including any activities they plan to take part in, such as winter sports."

News.title: Two murder arrests after balcony fall man dies
News.content:
Two men have been arrested on suspicion of murder after a man who fell from a balcony died.

Officers were called to reports that the man had fallen at flats on Liverpool Street in Salford shortly after midnight on Saturday, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said.

The force said the man died later that night. A man arrested on suspicion of attempted murder has now been arrested on suspicion of murder.

A second man has also been arrested on suspicion of murder.

The incident has been referred to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) because the men had earlier contact with police, GMP said.

An IOPC spokesperson said: "After being notified by the Greater Manchester Police of the previous police contact with the parties involved in this incident, we sent investigators to the police post-incident procedures in Manchester in assessment mode to gather further information.

"We continue to remain in assessment mode and will assess a GMP referral in due course."

News.title: Swimmers told to avoid beauty spot as 'hidden hazards' revealed by drought and fires
News.content:
People have been warned to stay away from a popular beauty spot pond used for swimming and other water sports due to "hidden hazards" exposed by reduced water levels.

Keepers Pond in Abergavenny poses "serious safety risks" with levels dangerously low, according to Bannau Brycheiniog National Park, also known as the Brecon Beacons.

It said that along with the prolonged dry spell, the water had been used to tackle recent wildfires.

"As the water has receded, previously hidden hazards and unknown objects have been exposed on the pond bed, creating serious safety risks. For your own safety, you must not enter the water under any circumstances," the park authority said in a Facebook post, external.

Border czar Tom Homan defended the Trump administration’s recent deportations to Haiti on Sunday, even as the State Department warns Americans not to travel to the Caribbean nation “for any reason.”

During an interview on CNN, host Dana Bash asked Homan about two deportation flights to Haiti over the past two weeks. The flights came after the Supreme Court allowed the administration to end Temporary Protected Status for Haiti in June, making roughly 350,000 Haitians who were permitted to live and work in the U.S. vulnerable to arrest and removal from the country.

Bash noted that Ambassador Jennifer Locetta, a Trump administration official and the U.S. emissary to the United Nations for political affairs, had described conditions in Haiti as “dire” earlier this week.

“Why is the Trump administration knowingly sending Haitians, including many who’ve lived in the U.S. legally under Temporary Protected Status, into the danger that they describe?” Bash asked Homan.

“We’re returning deportees to their home country,” Homan replied. “I’m not in the loop on this specific incident ... but when people are deported, they can’t stay here, they’re gonna go home.”

open image in gallery Border czar Tom Homan said he is unaware of 'the conditions in Haiti' after the Trump administration deported hundreds of Haitians to the country, which the State Department has described as plagued by crime, terrorism and unrest ( CNN, State of the Union )

Bash noted that the administration is moving to end TPS — a decades-old program that allows eligible nationals of certain countries to remain in the U.S. — even while conditions in immigrants’ home countries are still unsafe.

Homan complained that TPS appeared to be “never temporary” and noted that the Supreme Court had allowed termination in June.

In a third attempt to elicit a different response, Bash asked whether Homan, “as a human,” felt comfortable sending people back to a country ravaged by violence.

“Look, the bottom line is they’ve been ordered removed,” Homan replied. “I don’t know the conditions in Haiti. I’ve never been to Haiti. I don’t know if you have. But look, the judge made a decision ... and they need to go home.”

“We’re just enforcing the law,” Homan added. “And we’re doing it in a way that the American people voted for.”

Conditions in Haiti

The State Department currently lists Haiti under a Level 4 travel advisory, warning Americans not to travel there “for any reason.”

“U.S. citizens are at risk due to crime, terrorism, kidnapping, unrest, and limited health care,” the department says on its website.

Haiti, which shares the Caribbean island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic, is in the midst of a severe political and humanitarian crisis. Armed gangs control or contest large parts of Port-au-Prince, the capital, while the government struggles to maintain order.

open image in gallery Recently, 47 people were killed in a gang attack outside Port-au-Prince. Pictured: Women mourn next to the covered body of a person killed during the overnight attack ( Reuters )

open image in gallery Pictured: People walk past the remains of a charred vehicle following overnight violence in Kenscoff, a neighborhood near Port-au-Prince, Haiti, on August 24 ( AFP via Getty Images )

Recently, 47 people were killed in a gang attack in Kenscoff, a farming community. Among those killed was a 70-year-old man whose body was set alight by gang members.

Nearly 1.5 million people have been displaced across Haiti in recent years, in a country with a population of about 12 million. More than 3,000 people were killed between January and June, according to the United Nations.

Deportations set to ramp up

Amidst the unrest, deportations to Haiti are expected to increase, with flights scheduled to expand from once a month to once a week, The New York Times reported this week.

About 200 people were deported to Haiti on two separate flights over the past two weeks, according to the Trump administration and a human rights group.

“We are deeply concerned about the safety of Haitians in Haiti and those being returned to a country where the government cannot currently guarantee their protection,” Guerline Jozef, executive director of Haitian Bridge Alliance, said in a statement shared with The Independent last week.

“The Haitian government must explain clearly what measures it has put in place to protect people across the country, including those being deported back to Haiti,” she added. “If the government cannot provide that protection, it must engage its U.S. counterparts and request an immediate moratorium on deportations. The United States must halt deportation flights to Haiti and provide protection for Haitians in the United States until it is safe for people to return.”

open image in gallery Deportation flights to Haiti are expected to expand from once a month to once a a week after the Trump administration revoked TPS for the country, making thousands of Haitian immigrations with humanitarian protections vulnerable to removal ( AFP via Getty Images )

The Department of Homeland Security, meanwhile, has promoted the deportation flights.

In a recent update headlined “HOME SWEET HAITI,” the agency said a flight on August 20 carried 162 immigrants — including “pedophiles, gang members, drug traffickers, and violent assailants” — back to Haiti.

“TPS was never designed to be permanent, yet previous administrations have used it as a de facto amnesty program for decades,” Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in a press release. “Under the strong leadership of President Donald J. Trump, we are putting America first again.”

Multiple recent polls indicate that many Americans oppose Trump’s handling of immigration, once one of his strongest issues.

A YouGov survey conducted this month found that 53 percent of respondents disapproved of the administration’s handling of immigration, while 40 percent approved — Trump’s lowest-ever rating on the issue, according to the pollster.

NASA has embarked on an ambitious new endeavour to probe some of the most profound puzzles of space following the launch on Sunday of the US space agency's latest flagship observatory—a repurposed spy satellite designed to capture panoramic views of the cosmos.

Lifted into clear blue skies from NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida, the roughly $4 billion Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope was launched aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket shortly after sunrise.

Its primary mission is planned to last five years, though NASA indicated the spacecraft may hold enough fuel for another five years.

Positioned in an orbit beyond the moon, the telescope is engineered to investigate cosmic enigmas including dark energy and dark matter, while testing gravity across vast scales and searching for exoplanets, the term given to planets outside our solar system.

Sunday's launch marked "an endpoint for the engineers, but it's a starting point for the scientists," Julie McEnery, Roman telescope senior project scientist, told reporters at a post-launch news conference. "It feels like I'm on the edge of a precipice, and we're just about to set a foot off into the unknown."

open image in gallery A SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket carrying the Nancy Grace Roman space telescoe lifts off from Launch Complex 39A at the Kennedy Space Center in Florida ( AFP/Getty )

The observatory was originally designed for a spy satellite program under the National Reconnaissance Office, a part of the U.S. intelligence community that manages the most powerful American spy satellites. That program was over budget and terminated, and the NRO in 2012 donated it to NASA, which repurposed it for cosmic exploration.

Roman will travel through space toward an orbital location called Lagrange Point 2 about a million miles (1.6 million km) from Earth.

Mission scientists will spend the next 90 days commissioning it and preparing for its science operations. Roman is expected to beam back its first high-resolution images "before the winter holidays," Roman telescope project manager Jackie Townsend said.

A household name

Roman will build on the capabilities of other orbiting observatories such as the James Webb Space Telescope, launched in 2021, and the Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990.

"I have no doubt that Roman will become a household name alongside those great instruments of discovery," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman told reporters.

McEnery has said that Roman possesses broadly the same sensitivity and sharpness of vision as Hubble, but will survey the cosmos more quickly. Roman can survey our entire Milky Way galaxy in a month while Hubble would need a century, according to McEnery.

During Sunday's news conference, Isaacman took a call from President Donald Trump and put the phone speaker up to his microphone. Trump said the launch "looked beautiful on television."

"You are doing a fantastic job, and I'm supplying you all that money," Trump said, referring to NASA's approximately $24 billion 2026 budget, which survived an earlier White House proposal to cut the agency's funding by about $6 billion.

open image in gallery Space X is owned by Elon Musk ( Getty )

Trump's administration tried during both his first and second terms as president to cancel Roman or reduce its funding, but Congress preserved it. Its launch came nine months ahead of schedule, according to NASA.

Exquisite sensitivity

Webb has provided a new understanding of the universe's early history, finding among other things that primordial galaxies formed sooner and were bigger than previously known. Webb can look across vast distances and back into deep time, because of the time it takes light to travel.

Roman instead is able to take panoramic views. NASA likens Roman to a camera's wide-angle lens and Webb to a zoom lens.

"Webb is designed to be able to probe very deeply and with exquisite sensitivity into the universe, so we can find rare things in the early universe," McEnery told an earlier briefing, while Roman offers "the large vision that complements the deep views that Webb provides."

Roman will help in the understanding of two mysterious cosmic components — dark energy and dark matter — by creating the most comprehensive 3D map of the universe to date. Its main survey, to take more than a year to complete, will cover more than two billion galaxies.

open image in gallery A SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket lifts off carrying NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope ( Reuters )

The Big Bang event roughly 13.8 billion years ago initiated the universe, and it has been expanding ever since. This expansion is accelerating, with an invisible force called dark energy as the hypothesized reason.

The universe's contents include ordinary matter — stars, planets, gas, dust and all the familiar stuff on Earth — as well as dark matter and dark energy. Ordinary matter represents perhaps 5 per cent of the contents. Dark matter, known through its gravitational influences on galaxies and stars, may represent about 27 per cent. Dark energy may represent about 68 per cent.

Using Roman to gauge dark matter's pull and dark energy's push across the universe will bring scientists closer than ever before to solving both mysteries, according to NASA.

Roman also will conduct one of the most comprehensive searches ever for exoplanets. It is expected to discover thousands of new ones and provide the first statistical census of planetary systems similar to our own.

The U.S. military attacked Iranian rocket launchers positioned in the Strait of Hormuz, marking its first offensive operation in a month, a U.S. official told The Associated Press on Sunday.

Explosions were heard near Larak Island — which lies in the waterway — Iranian media outlets reported.

Iranian forces had been preparing to launch rockets carrying mines into the strait, the unnamed U.S. official said. The waterway, a vital trade route, has emerged as a major flash point in the war, which had largely settled into a stalemate in recent weeks.

In response, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said in a statement that the U.S. offensive “will be answered by the sons of Iran and will result in the punishment of the aggressor,” Axios reported.

Last week, the U.S. completed an operation to clear mines from shipping lanes in the strait, which carried about 20 percent of the world’s oil before the war began.

open image in gallery The US military attacked Iranian rocket launchers positioned in the Strait of Hormuz, marking its first offensive operation in a month, a US official told The Associated Press on Sunday ( Getty Images )

“I have just been informed by the United States Navy that all mines have been removed and/or detonated from within the International Waters of the Strait of Hormuz,” President Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social on August 25. “Iran has been notified that any ship or boat placing new mines will be immediately and systematically destroyed.”

When reached for comment, a Pentagon spokesperson referred The Independent to U.S. Central Command, which oversees U.S. operations in the Middle East.

This is a breaking story...

The Republican who won Texas’s Senate primary with Donald Trump’s backing is now hoping the president and Senate Republicans will help him keep the seat from falling into Democratic hands in the midterms.

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton won a contentious primary against the incumbent senator, John Cornyn, and secured the GOP nomination in May. Since then, he’s been running neck and neck with Democratic state Rep. James Talarico, who led Paxton by six points in a poll from a Democratic-linked polling firm published on Thursday. And he says he needs Trump’s cash to put him over the finish line.

Paxton said in an interview Sunday that his campaign’s own internals showed the race to be a different picture, but conceded that it was a close fight.

“I don’t trust all these polls. We have our own polling that suggests maybe a little different result, but we definitely have a close race,” he told The Sunday Briefing on Fox News.

He added that he needed a cash infusion from Donald Trump’s MAGA Inc. PAC, which has a war chest of more than $800 million but has been sparing in doling out funds this cycle.

open image in gallery Ken Paxton is trailing James Talarico by millions of dollars in cash on hand but is hoping for a boost from Donald Trump, who has been sparing in doling out dollars from his significant war chest ( Getty )

“I know that they are going to be a part of this,” Paxton said. He declined to say whether he has spoken with the president about fundraising during Trump’s campaign stop to Texas last week, though he said he expected money to come in from Senate Republicans to help keep the seat from becoming “California’s third senator.”

But that cavalry might not be coming.

Senate Republicans aren’t coming out in waves to support Paxton, who ousted one of their own closely tied to leadership and whose scandal-plagued background has already been the target of millions in negative ad spending by their campaign arm as they sought to protect Cornyn from his challenger.

open image in gallery James Talarico led Ken Paxton by eight points in a recent poll from a Democratic-linked outfit ( AFP/Getty )

Cornyn himself has signaled that there’s no love lost between the two men, telling reporters repeatedly that he won’t campaign or raise money for Paxton.

“Paxton’s a poor campaigner,” the Republican senator told The Texas Tribune last week. “He’s lazy and doesn’t raise money. And he basically is not offering a very compelling case for his election.

Cornyn said Paxton is “making this harder than it needs to be.”

On Sunday, Republican Sen. John Kennedy stressed that the Senate GOP’s campaign arm — the National Republican Senatorial Committee — didn’t have any money budgeted to protect the Texas Senate seat as Republicans find themselves fighting off a number of credible Democratic challenges.

open image in gallery Sen. John Kennedy says Senate Republicans have no money budgeted for the Texas race ( AFP/Getty )

"We in the senate don’t have the money budgeted for Texas. We need help from the president,” Kennedy told The Sunday Briefing on Fox News.

“The president says he has $850 million in his campaign accounts. That’s a lot of jack. I’m hoping that the president’s gonna spend $100 or $200 million in Texas. But he hasn’t committed to it yet,” Kennedy said. “But in the meantime, we’ve got a race, and I’m not going to play-act and say that we don’t.”

Fox’s interviews with Paxton and Kennedy came as the network highlighted the massive advantage Talarico currently has over Paxton in available cash, which Paxton credited to the expensive runoff against Cornyn.

Talarico won significant national support and saw a fundraising surge after former CBS host Stephen Colbert said that his network banned an interview with Talarico from the airwaves in February. His own primary did not go to a runoff, sparing the Democrats a second costly battle.

open image in gallery John Cornyn has refused to fundraise or campaign for his onetime opponent ( Getty )

Republicans are optimistic that Trump’s support and Texas’s strong Republican voting base will push Paxton over the finish line, but the president’s sinking approval ratings and Talarico’s popularity compared to Paxton’s are making that a tough argument to make.

A former top aide to Cornyn made headlines earlier this month when it was reported that he accepted a senior position on Talarico’s campaign, a sign of the work the Talarico campaign has done to win over Republicans averse to supporting Paxton.

The Texas attorney general was investigated by the FBI and accused of misusing his office, and faced an impeachment trial led by Republicans in the state legislature. In 2024, he accepted a deal to avoid charges on securities fraud by paying restitution of $300,000. The Department of Justice declined to bring charges against him in a decision made just weeks before Trump was set to take office.

Texas is just one of several red-purple states where Republicans are defending Senate seats this year and Democrats believe they have a chance to reverse the GOP’s gains made in the last election cycle, potentially even securing a majority. Such a possibility was considered far off just last year.

Democrats are also mounting serious challenges in Iowa and North Carolina, where retiring Republican senators have left their seats open, as well as in Alaska, Maine and Ohio where Democrats are challenging incumbent Republicans.

News.content:

Olivia Rodrigo and Stevie Nicks performed a moving rendition of “Landslide” at the pop singer’s inaugural Daisy Chain Fields festival, as it was announced that the event had raised $20m for women-focused organisations – aided by a donation from Melinda French Gates.

Rodrigo, 23, put on the star-studded event on Saturday (29 August) in Irvine, California, with performances from artists including Nicks, Karen O, Chappell Roan, Doechii, Bikini Kill, Rachel Chinouriri, Garbage, The Breeders and Mitski.

The festival was inspired by Lilith Fair, which was co-founded by Sarah McLachlan in 1997 in response to the misogyny she and her peers were facing in the music industry.

McLachlan was a special guest at Rodrigo’s festival; the “Drop Dead” star brought her out during her headline set and said without Lilith Fair, “there would be no Daisy Chain”.

They performed two of McLachlan’s songs – “Building a Mystery” and “Angel” – and dedicated them to Dolly Parton following the country music icon’s death aged 80.

Rodrigo then invited out Alanis Morissette for a singalong to her 1996 hit “Ironic”, after which Nicks joined her onstage for Fleetwood Mac’s 1975 song “Landslide”.

open image in gallery Rodrigo performing at Daisy Chain Fields ( Getty )

During her set, Rodrigo performed a number of tracks from her latest album, You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love, and debuted her new single “Serena Joy”, which was inspired by Margaret Atwood’s novel The Handmaid’s Tale.

Before she began her performance, Rodrigo thanked all of the musicians who took part in the festival: “The fact that they took the time out of their insanely busy schedules to come and do this festival for free is something I’m so grateful for,” she said.

“Because of that, and because of all of you who came to hang out today, I can stand on the stage and say we are donating $10m to 10 incredible charities. I really believe that giving women the tools to decide their own futures and live healthy lives free of violence and discrimination is the most effective tool we have at changing the world for the better.”

open image in gallery Rodrigo with Melinda French Gates at Daisy Chain Fields festival ( Getty )

Rodrigo then introduced Melinda French Gates, praising her as “one of the most inspiring women I’ve ever met”.

“She’s devoted her life to empowering women and girls that might have otherwise been forgotten,” Rodrigo said.

“She’s generous and brave and has done so much good in this world, and I’m totally floored because as well as being in attendance here tonight, she’s pledged to double every dollar that we made here today to a grand total of funds being donated to $20m. I’m so grateful!”

For her part, Gates called Rodrigo “a force” and praised her for “showing a new generation how much their voices matter”.

The funds raised will be split equally among 10 beneficiary organisations: Baby2Baby, Black Mamas Matter Alliance, Center for Reproductive Rights, FreeFrom, Jhpiego, John Hopkins Center for Indigenous Health, National Domestic Workers Alliance, National Institute for Reproductive Health, National Women’s Law Center, and Planned Parenthood.

open image in gallery Kate Halter of Die Spitz performs at the Daisy Chain Fields Music Festival ( AP )

It comes as President Donald Trump attempts to overhaul family planning grants that reproductive health clinics use to provide birth control and treat sexually transmitted infections. His administration paused $27.5 million last year for such organizations, including some Planned Parenthood affiliates, before officials agreed to restore the money.

Rodrigo and her festival co-organisers have hinted that the event will return, as a post to its Instagram page showed the huge crowds in attendance with the caption: “One year down, and we’ll just keep growing.”

On the eve of the festival, she shared a statement that said Daisy Chain Fields was created “to celebrate the power of what can happen when we come together to support one another”.

“The organisations we’ve partnered with are doing incredibly important work every single day in the US and globally,” she continued. “I’m so grateful to every person who bought a ticket, every artist who waived their fee, every sponsor for signing onto a brand new festival, and every donation that helped get to $10m dollars to support women and girls.”

Additional reporting by Associated Press

News.content:

PC Andrew Harper’s killers will remain in prison after the prime minister announced changes to the early release scheme that will keep anyone convicted of unlawful killing behind bars.

Andy Burnham said “hundreds” of people will be excluded as part of the changes, including prisoners convicted of historic child sex offences or manslaughter.

The prime minister previously promised to do “everything possible” to ensure Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole were not released under the scheme designed to ease prison overcrowding.

Extra prison space will now be created by deporting foreign offenders and ending indefinite jail terms, which The Independent has relentlessly campaigned on for more than two years.

Mr Burnham said: “I know how strongly people feel about this issue. I understand the concern and anger because I share it.

“That’s why I took action during my first weeks as prime minister to block some of the very worst in society being released before they should.

“We moved quickly to block vile criminals who commit rape, sexually abuse children and groom vulnerable young people.”

open image in gallery PC Harper was killed in 2019 and his three killers convicted of manslaughter ( PA Media )

He continued: “But I always said I wanted to do more. We will now not only be keeping offenders serving time for indecent assault locked up, but also those in prison for manslaughter and death by dangerous driving.

“This means that the awful criminals responsible for the killing of PC Andrew Harper will not have their sentence shortened.”

He said he “couldn’t have pushed the system any further” as he confirmed changes to the prison early release scheme.

Prisoners convicted of manslaughter, indecent assault and death by dangerous driving will now be exempt from the scheme, designed to ease pressure on the prison system – and Mr Burnham said he can now look victims “in the eye”.

He told BBC Breakfast: “I can look them in the eye now and say, I have turned over every stone, working with the Justice Secretary, over the summer, we have worked hard to look at everything.

“But at this point in time, there is no further that we can go without risking new offenders coming through the court system.

“Those guilty of the most serious offences, not being able to be sent to prison because the prisons are full, and I can’t allow that situation to arise either.”

open image in gallery PC Harper’s killers Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers were initially eligible for early release under the government’s planned sentencing changes ( Thames Valley Police )

He told the programme around 1,000 prisoners will remain in prison because of his initial changes, while “hundreds more” will stay behind bars because of the extra exemptions he announced on Sunday.

The prime minister had ordered a review of the changes to the Sentencing Act, which is being undertaken by justice secretary Alex Norris and is set to be published when parliament returns from summer recess this week.

It came after widespread condemnation of the scheme when it emerged that Bowers and Cole could be released halfway through their 13-year sentences.

They were passengers in the car that dragged PC Harper down a country road after he got caught in a strap attached to the vehicle as they fled the scene of a quad bike theft in Sulhamstead, Berkshire, in 2019.

open image in gallery PC Andrew Harper’s mother Debbie Adlam said she was ‘grateful’ her son’s killers would not be freed early ( PA Archive )

PC Andrew Harper’s mother said she is “grateful” her son’s killers will not be released early, but they “are only back at where we were to start with”.

Debbie Adlam told BBC Breakfast: “It’s a really mixed bag of emotions, though, because on the one hand we are glad, but we’ve been brought through the mill, and we are only back at where we were to start with. You know, go back a few months, this is where we were – so we’re not making any headway or anything. We are just literally fighting to get back to where we were.

“I just hope that what Andy Burnham says there, that they will be going into a further overhaul over the next few years – it really needs to happen for our sakes.”

She said she hopes there is a way to increase sentences in the justice system “because our country seems to be going downwards”.

Asked if she thinks the country is getting it wrong, if a sentencing says that a particular crime gets 10 years then the person gets out at half or two-thirds, she said: “I really think we’re getting it wrong. When you look at what starting point we had for our sentences in this case, they started off as a decent amount, really, and then they were sliced away and sliced away, and the years came off for various things.

“You know, we’re actually feeling, I think most public would say to you, ‘I feel like we’re going downhill as a country, and I think it needs some serious work’.”

Aileen O’Connor, the chairwoman of Thames Valley Police Federation said: “PC Andrew Harper made the ultimate sacrifice for the job that he loved, serving communities, serving society.

“His killers should never have been considered for early release. It remains shocking that they were.”

Paul Williams, acting deputy national chair, said: “The voice of policing and the policing family across the country has been heard loud and clear.”

Mr Norris is expected to reveal full details of the latest changes when parliament returns on Tuesday.

open image in gallery (Top) Wayne Williams and Leroy Douglas (Bottom) Abdullahi Suleman, Shaun Anton Lloyd and Thomas White ( The Independent )

Mr Burnham’s scrapping of Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) sentences could now mean thousands of people stuck in prison will finally be given a release date.

The controversial open-ended punishments were given to offenders considered a significant risk to the public between 2005 and 2012.

The Independent has campaigned for the past two years alongside the families of those affected to call for all IPP prisoners to have their sentences reviewed. Despite 96 people taking their own lives in custody after losing hope of release, successive governments have refused.

Among those trapped inside are Leroy Douglas, 43, who has served almost 20 years without release for street robbery of a mobile phone, Abdullahi Suleman, 42, who is still in jail 20 years after he was handed an IPP for a laptop robbery and Shaun Anton Lloyd, 39, who has been hauled back to prison four times and served 12 years for two street robberies committed when he was 18.

News.title: Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season
News.content:
Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season, then?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick amidst another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

News.title: Robinson’s Victorian-style bowling figures secure series victory over Pakistan
News.content:
The only missing aspect was a five-fer which would have brought a 100th Test wicket. Even so, his career average is now 19.53, the best for England since Frank Tyson of those with 50 or more wickets.

Mr Nude Nuts, as Matthew Hayden called him, could be devastating against Australia and, like Root the captain, deserves to be judged on what happens in his second incarnation rather than what went before.

Robinson’s pace has lingered around the 79mph mark and inevitably that throws up Rob Key’s assertion you cannot succeed in Test cricket bowling in the 70s with the keeper standing up. Key was referring to county bowlers pitching it up and relying on the Dukes ball to do the rest.

It was thrown in his face in Australia but Michael Neser and Scott Boland are not county trundlers: they extract more energy off the pitch than that.

Robinson is also no dobber. His high release point combined with a mastery of length means he is always threatening the top of off stump. He also knows which way the ball is going to nip, giving no clues to the batsmen due to his sleight of hand skills.

With Jamie Smith improving under the tutelage of Sarah Taylor, he can operate with the keeper standing up which pins batsmen in the crease, bringing all modes of dismissals into play. Robinson was as effective with the new ball as the old: his two seven-over spells were two for 13 and two for 11.

How snarling Robinson adds edge and precision

At 32, he has become a combination of Stuart Broad and James Anderson, although down on their pace with the height and bounce of the former, and tricks of the latter. He can move the new ball further either way than Anderson or Broad but the question is whether he has their durability and sheer competitiveness.

He has not been tested this summer by pitches or opponents. He has not bowled more than 18 overs in an innings and was injured when England played on the best batting pitch at the Oval. He was not trusted at Trent Bridge because the old management had burned their fingers before. That decision may well have cost the coach his job.

Like Broad and Anderson he has a snarl too, sending Abdullah Shafique on his way with a word or two. There was no need for that but maybe it was just a carried away reaction to bowling an absolute beauty that angled in, seamed away and hit the top of off.

News.title: Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness
News.content:
Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

“It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso said. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”

Brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

“We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

News.title: Moses Itauma lifted out of ring after losing IBF title bout to Filip Hrgovic
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the heavyweight clash between Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic.

Itauma is on the cusp of becoming a British boxing star, but for now there remain questions. It is not that people doubt his talents, more that he needs to prove them emphatically to the wider boxing world.

At just 21, Itauma has been creating rumblings since 2023. He has 10 straight knockouts. He is undefeated. His last two wins were against Dillian Whyte and Jermaine Franklin, but he is yet to beat a fighter you might regard as a gatekeeper to a title fight.

Hrgovic might normally be seen as that gatekeeper. At 34, the Croatian has plenty of experience in the ring, with 21 fights bringing 20 wins, 15 of them by knockout. His only loss was against Daniel Dubois in 2024, but his wins since then have been against Joe Joyce, David Adeleye and Dave Allen. Not the highest quality, by any means. Hrgovic, then, has something to prove to us too.

However, this is no eliminator, this is for the full IBF world heavyweight championship. A win for Itauma would see him become the second-youngest world heavyweight champion in boxing history.

As Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury circle one another, threatening to never fight at all, Itauma looks set to be Britain’s next heavyweight star. All he has to do is win at the O2 Arena tonight. If he does that, he could then be a fixture at the top of the sport for a decade, perhaps more.

Ringwalks are expected at around 10.30pm for the main event. So if men in dressing gowns is your thing, get ready.

News.title: £380m = zero points: Big-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle
News.content:
“After the first goal we lost confidence,” said De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”

To be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the new signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

Of the five new arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

News.title: Lawrence seizes his opportunity on rain-ruined day at Lord’s
News.content:
On a bleak day for batting, Dan Lawrence seized an opportunity that he must have feared had passed him by.

Lawrence was one of the victims of Bazball excess, shoved up to open in place of Zak Crawley two years ago in a punt that backfired and could have ended his Test career.

It took the sudden retirement of Ben Stokes and an injury to first-choice replacement Sam Curran to open up a position at No 6, Lawrence’s natural home, and it has come at just the right time.

At 29 he is a much more rounded cricketer than the one who debuted in Sri Lanka under Joe Root in 2021 and he showed it here with a hard-fought half-century on a gloomy, dank Saturday when only 25 overs were possible between the frequent drizzly showers, forcing MCC into a 50 per cent ticket refund.

It was a second fifty in three innings since his recall and he will not have faced many tougher conditions than this, with the ball seaming around on a spiteful pitch. With Mohammad Abbas teasing the ball off the surface and the athletic Mohammad Rizwan snaffling everything up to the stumps, this was a real challenge of mind and technique.

Lawrence will never win awards for aesthetic beauty but he chose the right balls to put away in a 66-ball unbeaten 50 that stretched England’s lead to 357 at 177 for seven in their second innings. Lawrence settled any wobbles about Pakistan pulling off a miracle recovery.

News.title: Springboks level Greatest Rivalry series with blood-and-thunder victory over All Blacks
News.content:
South Africa aim to bounce back from losing the first game of the Greatest Rivalry Tour as they take on New Zealand in game two from Cape Town. The All Blacks claimed an impressive 33-16 win in game on in Johannesburg last weekend, outscoring South Africa five tries to one. That victory takes New Zealand above South Africa in the world rankings into top spot.

The Springboks know that a defeat today will mean they cannot win the series. They have not lost two consecutive Tests since November 2022. Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu has been given the nod to start at fly-half but Handre Pollard has pulled out of the matchday squad due to a calf injury.

“There were a handful of positives and negatives last week, but the main thing that let us down was that we created so many chances, but mistakes at crucial times cost us,” South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus said.

“We will put in a lot of work this week to ensure that we are sharp in that regard this weekend because if we had used even some of those chances, the result could have been completely different. That said, we know New Zealand will be charged up after winning last week, and they will want to build on that. But the key for us will be to focus on our game and ensure that we are as effective as possible all around.”

News.title: Iraola fumes at bungling fourth official for costing Liverpool a penalty
News.content:
He did know, though, why Liverpool had needed to drag themselves off the deck again for the second week in a row. Iraola has shown in his opening weeks on Merseyside that he is not someone who seeks excuses.

“A lack of intensity hurt us,” Iraola said with obvious disdain and it was only down to a show of character in the second period that a slovenly first half did not enable Forest to win at Anfield for the third consecutive year, for all that the travelling fans thought it was “happening again!”

Forest, bruised after two defeats in four days to Leeds, looked like an Oliver Glasner side. They were aggressive and well organised, the only failing was that physically they could not see the job through, but the Austrian insisted that will change in due course.

Once Glasner is settled in and he gets his transfer business done – “definitely one, possibly two and probably three,” was his mischievous reply to how the window will unfold – Forest will be a formidable proposition, especially if the first 45 minutes are a barometer.

They had been knocking on the door before Dan Ndoye eventually broke the deadlock, sweeping a left-footed drive past Alisson after Igor Jesus had won a header from a long clearance. It was a simple goal, marginally onside, but it was absolutely deserved.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta reveals he’s ‘BEGGING’ Premier League chiefs to make major rule change to overhaul matchday squads
Sports.content:
MIKEL ARTETA has been “begging” Premier League officials to expand matchday squads for the “welfare of the players”.

Rules currently allow managers to name nine substitutes on the bench, an increase from the seven permitted before the Covid-19 pandemic.



But Arteta wants Prem chiefs to increase that so he does not have to leave anyone at home.

The Arsenal boss, whose side go to Aston Villa tonight, has had to leave stars like Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus out of his matchday squad this term and feels it leads to a number of issues — that duo are now both set to leave.



Arteta said: “That’s why I have been begging the Premier League to extend those numbers just for the welfare of the players, which is the most important thing.

“I think every squad needs more than 20 outfield players, ideally, to sustain the level of demand in international games that we have.



“But these are the rules, and within the rules, we have to play.

“We need to be very close to the players to explain those situations in the right way, for everybody to feel important, because they will be.”

The Gunners chief revealed last week that Gabriel Jesus was not part of Arsenal training because of the “numbers in the squad”.

And Arteta does not want to continue having “tough” conversations with players who would rather be with the squad than at home watching on TV.

Sports.title: Mario Balotelli slams ‘phones & PlayStations’ for ‘ruining’ football and reveals advice he’d tell his 16-year-old self
Sports.content:
MARIO Balotelli has slammed the impact of mobile phones and video games on football.

The 36-year-old explained that the current crop of young stars coming through have experienced a vastly different upbringing to himself.



Balotelli has noted that he no longer sees young children playing football in the streets in Italy, like when he was a youngster.

He has suggested that modern mobile phone and video game culture is to blame for this shift in entertainment.



The Italian star told The Guardian that the shift now sees young footballers playing less football than previous generations.

Balotelli said: “Computers, phones, and PlayStations have ruined a lot.



“Above all, the parents’ mentality has changed. A seven‑year-old kid today might play football for two hours every three days.

“We had the same structured training sessions, plus three hours of playing at the park every day, which felt like fun but was actually extra training.

“I truly believe talents were born on the street and in the parks.”

He explained that playing against older children helped to raise his game in a way that is less common in the modern age.

The striker claimed that “it’s very different” because he would learn skills on the streets, rather than just watching videos online.

This upbringing seemed to serve Balotelli well as he went on to score 14 goals in 36 caps for Italy between 2010 and 2018.

Even 20 years after coming through at Lumezzane, Balotelli is continuing to ply his trade professionally for Al-Ittifaq in the UAE First Division.

But it has not been a straight-forward career for the controversial star.

Former Scotland midfielder Scott Brown, 41, even recalled being threatened on the pitch by the striker during a game.



Balotelli’s wild side even threatened to re-emerge after falling out of favour at Genoa last year.

But the Italian has explained that there are lessons he wished he could tell his 16-year-old self.

Balotelli continued: “I’d tell him not to make certain choices and to listen to certain people at specific times.”

Sports.title: Michael Carrick gives Man Utd transfer update as he hails ‘new signing’ Marcus Rashford
Sports.content:
MICHAEL CARRICK insists Manchester United could still be active in the transfer market before Tuesday’s 11pm deadline.

United recovered from an opening weekend defeat at Hull City to hammer Ipswich Town 5-2, despite going 1-0 down.



The £155million trio Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba have bolstered the midfield but United have conceded four goals in two games and look vulnerable in defence.

Left back Luke Shaw was culpable for Leif Davis’ opening goal and United have been on the lookout for a new left back.



Shaw admitted he was “disappointed and angry with myself” over his defending against Abdul Fatawu before he crossed for Davis, but it is unclear whether United will bring in competition for the 31-year-old.

United wanted Newcastle left back Lewis Hall but their new manager Matthias Jaissle said there was “no chance” of the England international leaving.



When asked about the possibility of any more incomings, Carrick replied: “It’s always difficult to say, to be honest, when there’s so little time left.

“I think the situation that we’re in, I think the business that we’ve managed to do, I’m pleased with.

“I think we’re a better group, a better squad, potentially a better team. Adding Marcus (Rashford) into that feels like a new signing.

“So, in that respect, we’re quite happy. We’re always open to if there’s something else to be able to add, so I wouldn’t shut that down.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“But as it stands, we’ll have to wait and see.”

Rashford was sharp on his first United start since December 1, 2024 and chief executive Omar Berrada all but confirmed the 28-year-old would stay in his programme notes.

Carrick said: “[I’m] really pleased with Marcus. I thought he dealt with the whole day as normal, really.

“I’m sure it was nice for him to be back and starting games here and enjoying being involved in a good performance.

“I thought he did particularly well in not easy circumstances, particularly as the game was going through the cycle.



“And then second half, it all clicked. So, I thought he did very good all-round and he’ll only get better.

“So, I was really pleased with him.

“He’s adding to the group for us, for sure, because it’s pretty obvious. But I’ve known him for a while, and then he wasn’t here when I’ve come back, and now he is.

“So, I think he’s making the most of that for us and for him as well to have the opportunity to be here.

“He’s one of our own, you know. He’s living his dream, playing here now and trying to be successful and win.



“So, whatever’s gone on, I think part of this club, there’s players that have come and come back sometimes, or players that maybe were going to leave, didn’t leave.

“It’s always about what you do next and what your intentions are.

“He’s been fantastic since he came back, I have to say, and it was great to see him on the pitch today for us.”

Sports.title: Man Utd spent £155m creating midfield for future… but Kobbie Mainoo proves his new contract was biggest deal of summer
Sports.content:
THE Old Trafford stadium announcer introduced one of the starters as “Manchester born and bred”. It was not Marcus Rashford.

That was Kobbie Mainoo’s privilege. Mainoo, recalled after the aberration at Hull, underpinned United’s recovery against Ipswich Town with a performance worthy of the man of the match.



For all the three midfielders United have signed for £155million this summer, their biggest midfield signing this year was Mainoo’s five-year contract.

On the one occasion Mainoo was unavailable for Michael Carrick last season, United lost to Leeds. Against Ipswich, he outshone new partner Youri Tielemans with a fleet-footed performance that blew away any World Cup cobwebs.



The Stretford End serenaded Mainoo loudly as United homed in on victory. There is a particular fondness for an academy graduate born in the City stronghold of Stockport.

Marcus Rashford used to be the Mancunian reds’ poster boy. He may adorn the bedroom walls of young United supporters again.

This was Rashford’s first United start in 637 days. He emerged for the Premier League anthem with his niece in his arms, a reminder of how much of a family affair United is for the Rashfords of Wythenshawe.

Benjamin Sesko’s handful of minutes since he aggravated a shin injury on May 3 ensured Rashford was first in line to replace the unconvincing Patrick Dorgu. United got an immediate upgrade.

Rashford and Matheus Cunha, handed the No.10 when Rashford was still at United last year, quickly struck up a promising rapport.

Cunha high-fived Rashford for teeing him up for an early sighter and the link-up play between United’s new ‘9’ and ‘10’ was encouraging.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Rashford was impressively denied twice by Ipswich ‘keeper Kjell Scherpen yet his most profound impact came in his own half.

With the game 15 minutes old, Rashford regained the ball inside his own half. The rapturous reaction rivalled Rashford’s last goals at Old Trafford almost 21 months ago. Any lingering friction between player and matchgoers was extinguished.

Rashford’s work ethic was certainly questionable during his 18 months at United before Ruben Amorim ostracised him.

Rashford was so switched on that Bruno Fernandes granted him the privilege of a free kick that was blazed into the protective netting.

United only confirmed Rashford’s new squad number last week, which may have accounted for the lack of ‘Rashford 9’ shirts inside or outside Old Trafford.



Cannily, Carrick substituted Mainoo and Rashford at the same time with the game won. Supporters were already on their feet, putting their hands together for Mainoo, and the applause continued for Rashford’s admirable shift.

Having two Mancunian academy graduates in the United starting XI cannot be underestimated when rookies were occasionally its only representative in squads last year.

The United fans’ favourite remains their best player. Fernandes’ name was chanted more often and more loudly than any of his teammates.



The August date for the PFA Player of the Year awards is illogical and there was a risk of United already dwelling on the past with more recognition for Fernandes.

As if to remind everyone he was the deserving recipient, Fernandes hit a third hat-trick for the club and his second in the opening Old Trafford fixture of a season.

His goals – the equaliser and clincher – were more leverage for Fernandes to be put on a salary that trumps Rashford’s. For now, United’s best player is not the best paid.

The attack was always bound to be untouched by United in the event that there were no takers for Rashford. The clamour for a reinforcement at the other end will intensify, though.

Yesteryear, a player who had served United for 12 years would have contributed to a period of success. Luke Shaw defies that assumption.



Shaw’s approval ratings were high after he started every Premier League game in 2025-26 yet the reality is he has entered the final year of his contract and United want a new left back.

Recruiting one is more urgent after the livewire Abdul Fatawu sped past Shaw and stayed ahead of him. Shaw will not forget Fatawu’s name after he crossed for Leif Davis to put Ipswich ahead.

The issue United have is they have dawdled for so long over whether to recruit a new left back that even if they do so before Tuesday’s 11pm it will look reactionary.



They must also ensure if they do bring in anyone it does not compromise a move for a more esteemed left back next year. Lewis Hall, their preferred target, may be easier to prise from Newcastle in 2027.

Shaw started the second half with a firm and fair tackle on Fatawu, who milked its force. Lisandro Martinez, sensing fragility, high-fived him.

It is not particularly progressive for United that they have settled with Shaw as a certain starter devoid of competition for now.

Shaw avoided celebrating the Jacob Greaves own goal – not out of uncertainty VAR would chalk it off – and received a sympathetic arm around the shoulder from Carrick.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

When Shaw was removed with United’s comeback complete, Noussair Mazraoui – a right back – replaced him.



The applause was not as loud as it was for Mainoo and Rashford.

Sports.title: Ollie Watkins shares emotional video after completing £51m Al Hilal move with Arsenal ace to follow & Benzema to be axed
Sports.content:
OLLIE WATKINS has said an emotional farewell to Aston Villa after completing his controversial move to Al Hilal.

The striker, 30, refused to play in Villa’s Premier League opener last weekend away at Brighton as the team lost 4-0 in a disastrous start on the south coast.



But he returned to apologise to manager Unai Emery before his switch to Saudi Arabia was confirmed.

And Watkins, a modern day Villa great with 278 appearances and 108 goals (91 in the Prem) shared a sad goodbye with fans online.



Sat down in a plush Villa chair, Watkins speaks into the camera and talks over some of his best moments during his time after joining from Brentford in 2020.

With slow music playing in the background, he said: “Hi Villans. Firstly, I’d like to say never did I intend, nor did I imagine, my time at Aston Villa would end this way.



“With that being said, I am eternally grateful for the last six years.

“Not only has it shaped me as a player, but as a person.

“We’ve been through so many ups and downs during my six seasons here.

“But one thing that has never changed is that I’ve given everything for this club.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“From my first goals in the 7-2 win against Liverpool, getting the club back into Europe, the Champions League nights at Villa Park, to that unforgettable night in Istanbul.

“And becoming Villa’s record Premier League goalscorer is an achievement I never thought would be possible when I signed for the club.

“I want to thank everyone who has contributed to my time here.

“Dean Smith, Steven Gerrard, and especially Unai Emery, for always believing in me.

“For me personally, my two children were born here in Birmingham.



“And to see them walk on the pitch and you fans singing my name in the Holte End, in front of them and my family, is something that will always stay with me forever.

“Birmingham will always be home and so will Villa.

“After six years, it’s time to say goodbye. It’s time for a new chapter that I’m excited about.

“However, I close this chapter with a heavy heart.

“Villa will always mean so much to me.



“Thank you guys, from the bottom of my heart. Ollie.”

England forward Watkins is set to join up with Arsenal winger Gabriel Martinelli, who will be signed for around £50million.

And they are trying to replace Real Madrid legend Karim Benzema, who ripped up his contract at the Middle Eastern side.

It is reported that the Frenchman could retire.

Al-Hilal still have Kalidou Koulibaly, Theo Hernandez, Yassine Bounou, Ruben Neves, Sergej Milinkovic-Savic, Crysencio Summerville, and Darwin Nunez in their squad.

Watkins, who tried to force his Villa exit as chiefs held out for a bigger fee, has been replaced by Nicolas Jackson.

Rashford's impact on Man Utd transfer deadline day plan as 'new signing' hailed

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford has returned to Man Utd to give them even more attacking depth

Michael Carrick admitted Marcus Rashford’s return to the Manchester United starting line-up has eased the need for last-minute business in the transfer window.

‌



Carrick gave Rashford his first United start in 626 days and while he did not get on the scoresheet in the 5-2 win over Ipswich at Old Trafford, the 28-year-old England attacker impressed his manager.

‌



And Rashford’s return to United’s squad has clearly influenced their transfer window policy. With the clock ticking down to the window’s close, Carrick said: “I think the situation that we're in, I think the business that we've managed to do, I'm pleased with.

‌



“I think we're a better group, a better squad, potentially a better team, you know. Adding Marcus into that feels like a new signing. So, in that respect, we're quite happy.”

Carrick, though, did not rule out any eleventh hour deals. He went on: “It's always difficult to say, to be honest, when there's so little time left. I think the situation that we're in. We're always open to if there's something else to be able to add, so I wouldn't shut that down, but as it stands, we'll have to wait and see.”

The United boss said: “I've known him for a while, and then he wasn't here when I've come back, and now he is. So I think he's making the most of that for us and for him as well - to have the opportunity to be here. He's one of our own.

“He's living his dream, playing here now and trying to be successful and win. There are players that have come back sometimes or players that maybe were going to leave, who didn't leave. It's always about what you do next and what your intentions are. He's been fantastic since he came back, I have to say, and it was great to see him on the pitch today for us.”

‌



View 2 Images Michael Carrick has not totally ruled out any late business

And Carrick also had special praise for Kobbie Mainoo, who did not see a minute’s action at the World Cup but was outstanding for United against Ipswich.

Carrick said: “I thought Kobbie was pretty much all-around very, very good for a first start back. We kind of managed him a little bit, and we've got good midfielders, so it's about trying to make the best of the combinations.

Article continues below

“I understand Bruno will get a lot of credit today, and he deserves that as well, but I thought Kobbie was immense in the middle of the pitch for us and underpinned the performance of the team.”

Sports.title: Neville Southall supported after Everton icon's social media post as fans rush to help
Sports.content:
Neville Southall has received swathes of support after sharing a health update on social media. The former Everton goalkeeper revealed that he was taking a leave of absence from X due to ill health.

The Welshman, 67, offered the news on Sunday morning, much to the concern of his fans. Southall, who also turned out for Bury and Torquay United during a distinguished career spanning three decades, took to X on Sunday morning to share the concerning news.

After working as a binman and waiter during his teenage years, Southall went on to win 92 Wales caps and win the FWA Footballer of the Year in 1985. But the love of football fans has been inspired by more than his stellar achievements on the pitch, having become an advocate for LGBT rights among a range of political causes.

The MBE holder posted: "Won't be on here for a bit not well."

‌



That message prompted a wave of warm wishes from across the footballing world. Southall quickly received messages from fans, and former colleagues.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Former Wales team-mate Iwan Roberts added: "Bless you Nev get better soon big man." Wales fan group The Barry Horns posted: "We love you Nev."

BBC colleague Marc Webber said: "Get well soon, fella." Journalist Daniel Storey added: "Keep well Nev, look after yourself x."

‌



"Wishing you well, Neville, the best goalkeeper in the world when I was growing up, but far more importantly, a really good, kind person and a voice of reason on here these days," said Dan Harvey.

View 2 Images Neville Southall remains a Wales and Everton icon (Image: Offside, Offside via Getty Images)

Anthony Robbins said: "Best of luck big man, we are all with you, we are one, we are Everton.

Paul Steer added: "Get well soon Nev! Absolute legend and I say that as someone who never supported any of the clubs you played for."

‌



Amàdan said: "Best wishes, Neville. A hero to many Evertonians. The best to ever do it. Look after yourself big man"

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Southall racked up well over 500 league appearances for Everton, remaining at Goodison Park from 1981 to 1998. During that time he twice won the first division with the Toffees, in addition to two FA Cups and the European Cup Winners' Cup.

The Llandudno-born shotstopper started his career at Bury before representing Stoke City, Bradford City and several other clubs, eventually bringing the curtain down on his playing days at Dagenham and Redbridge.

‌



Since hanging up his boots, he has been a passionate champion of mental health awareness and LGBT rights, though concerns over his well-being have grown in recent times. Southall was taken to hospital last summer after contracting an infection, which resulted in him being placed on an intravenous drip.

"Not talking a break from here in hospital with a couple of drips due to bad infection sorry any I was supposed to meet and work for this weekend," he posted at the time.

The details surrounding his latest health scare have yet to be revealed, but there is little doubt he will be inundated with well-wishes from throughout the football community.

Sports.title: Why Harry Maguire goal was allowed to stand despite refs seeing Man Utd handball
Sports.content:
Why Harry Maguire goal was allowed to stand despite refs seeing Man Utd handball

Manchester United's second goal against Ipswich Town was allowed to stand after an initial VAR check as Harry Maguire's shot found the bottom corner

View 2 Images Harry Maguire's goal for Manchester United against Ipswich Town was allowed to stand despite a handball in the build up

Manchester United's second goal against Ipswich Town was allowed to stand despite the ball hitting Harry Maguire's HAND in the build-up.

‌



Maguire, 33, fired United into a 2-1 lead in the 57th minute at Old Trafford after controlling the ball on the edge of the box before drilling a low shot that was deflected home by Jacob Greaves for an own goal.

‌



However, the ball appeared to hit Maguire's hand when he won it back, leaving the Ipswich players incensed that the goal should be disallowed. But, because he was not the actual goalscorer, the goal is allowed to stand.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

If Maguire had directly benefited from the handball and been the scorer, a free-kick would have awarded to Ipswich. As he was not, United were given a second goal and took the lead for the first time in the game.

"The referee's call of goal for Manchester United was checked and confirmed by VAR – with it deemed that Maguire was not the immediate goalscorer after an accidental handball," the Premier League said.

‌



VAR added: "It's an own goal and the accidental handball is not punishable, so we recommend you award the goal."

Gary Neville delivered his verdict on the incident and repeated what was said by VAR when they were discussing about disallowing the goal. "If that shot had been on target it wouldn't have been a goal," Neville told Sky Sports.

View 2 Images Harry Maguire puts Manchester United ahead against Ipswich Town (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"VAR say to the referee 'hear me out and listen to me' because they know it's going to be complicated."

United had fallen behind in the 29th minute as Ipswich took a shock lead. Abdul Fatawu went past Luke Shaw with ease on the right-hand side before pulling the ball back for Leif Davis to smash home.

But the Reds responded 11 minutes later as Matheus Cunha pounced on an error from Marcelino Nunez to slide a pass through to Bruno Fernandes and he did the rest, slotting the ball beyond the Ipswich goalkeeper.

‌



Although Ipswich hadmade a bright start to the second half, United were ruthless in attack. After Greaves' own-goal put them ahead, Fernandes scored from the spot soon after to make it 3-1 to the Reds.

Fernandes wrapped up his hat-trick in the 68th minute, tucking the ball into the bottom corner after the ball fell into his path, before Bryan Mbeumo made it 5-1 to United with a well-taken lobbed effort.

There was still time for Ipswich to reduce the deficit to three and make it 5-2, however, as Julio Enciso robbed Lisandro Martinez before squaring to substitute Chuba Akpom to prod home from close-range.

Article continues below

That is how it ended in Manchester as the Reds secured their first win of the season and bounced back from last weekend's dismal opening defeat at Hull City.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso opens the door for Enzo Fernandez to join Man City in double transfer update
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso opens the door for Enzo Fernandez to join Man City in double transfer update

Chelsea continued their perfect start to the Premier League season with a win over Brighton - but there could be major changes to the squad ahead of Tuesday's deadline

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso has hinted that Enzo Fernandez could leave Chelsea in the next 48 hours (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso has shown the exit door to Enzo Fernandez - and admitted Pedro Neto could still leave too.

‌



Argentina midfielder Fernandez is desperate to join Manchester City before Tuesday’s transfer deadline and was left out of Chelsea ’s squad again for their win over Brighton.

‌



City are lining up a £130m British record deal and Alonso admitted he made the decision because it was “best for the team.”

‌



Alonso also left the door open for Neto to go before Tuesday’s deadline as the Portugal winger has been attracting interest with Liverpool, one of the teams linked with him.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Chelsea expect more arrivals before the window - they have been linked with Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara - and Fernandez appears to be on his way out as long as the money is right and the Blues sign a replacement.

‌



Chelsea boss Alonso said: “We'll see. We want the best for the team and that's why we made the decision against Luton and today and anything that happens before Tuesday evening, we need to be aware of what is going to develop.

“We are not sure, we are preparing for all the scenarios but I am sure that whatever happens from Wednesday we will have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games.”

Neto is also an interesting story for Chelsea because the winger is playing as a wing back and his future looks uncertain - but equally he played well against Brighton and could stay.

‌



View 2 Images Alonso has admitted that Pedro Neto could still leave before the window closes

But asked whether he could guarantee Neto would stay, Alonso said: “No, in football I don't guarantee anything, not anyone. But I was very happy with Pedro. He did really well, he played with a lot of energy.

“He is going to be very important for the team for the whole season because he has different special qualities. He is a threat in one-v-one, he attacks very well in the space, he is strong, he is competitive.

Article continues below

“I am happy that he scored, he was really close to scoring another one. I am very happy with Pedro.”
