Sports.title: Man Utd told Victor Osimhen is 'waiting' for transfer as Benjamin Sesko plan tipped
Sports.content:
Man Utd told Victor Osimhen is 'waiting' for transfer as Benjamin Sesko plan tipped

Former Manchester United striker Louis Saha has claimed that Victor Osimhen is still waiting for the Red Devils to make their move before the September 1 deadline

View 2 Images Victor Osimhen has been linked with a move to Manchester United this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Victor Osimhen is still holding out for Manchester United to come calling before the end of the transfer window, given his well-known affection for the club. That is according to ex-United forward Louis Saha, who believes the Nigeria international is waiting for the Reds to make a move in the next 48 hours.

‌



Osimhen, 27, has been linked with a move to United for a number of years, but that opportunity now appears to have passed. Galatasaray are paying him enormous wages, which stretch even further due to Turkey's top tax rate of just 40 per cent, with half of that absorbed by Super Lig clubs, effectively reducing it to 20 per cent, compared to 45 per cent in the United Kingdom. Any potential deal would require an equally substantial fee for the Turkish champions to even contemplate selling. As such, it is not particularly financially feasible for United to make a move.

‌



Saha, however, has told MrGamble via Metro that Osimhen remains hopeful of a United move before the end of the window. He said: "All United have to do is make the connection, but that's why it hasn't happened yet.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"Osimhen is still waiting. United missed out on signing Harry Kane, and that was one of their biggest mistakes in the transfer market. But they can correct that mistake by signing Osimhen.

"I think Osimhen is a better fit for United now than Kane because of Benjamin Sesko. Osimhen can teach Sesko about movement and being a striker, but they could also play together and combine better than Kane and Sesko could."

‌



Saha added: "I know for a fact that Victor Osimhen is a Manchester United fan. He loves Man United. I have seen it in his eyes: the impact the club has on him, and he sees the impact he could have on this team."

View 2 Images Galatasaray striker Victor Osimhen has been linked with a move to Man United this summer (Image: Cemal Yurttas/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Saha is not the only former United player to have voiced his support for signing Osimhen this month. Patrice Evra told GOAL in association with Stake that they need "a striker, someone who scores a goal, I think that's what I'm looking at."

‌



He added: "That's why for me, Osimhen is the best, he's a perfect example."

Osimhen has netted five goals and laid on a further three across the opening three Super Lig fixtures of this campaign. The striker has therefore had a direct hand in all but two of their nine league goals.

He is already a third of the way to matching his tally of 15 from last season's Super Lig and just three short of his domestic assists tally. It was in the Champions League where Osimhen truly caught the eye, netting seven goals and contributing a further assist across ten outings. His current form mirrors that of his loan spell. The striker found the net 37 times in 41 appearances across all competitions.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso has Chelsea looking like genuine title challengers - no wonder fans are happy
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso has Chelsea looking like genuine title challengers - no wonder fans are happy

Xabi Alonso is already proving a hit with the Chelsea fans and the Blues made it two wins from win against Brighton as Emi Martinez debuted in goal after his move

View 3 Images Xabi Alonso has kept up his perfect Chelsea start

Chelsea fans are notoriously hard to please. But no wonder Xabi Alonso has won them over already.

‌



This was a brilliant, entertaining and terrific seven-goal contest which had the Stamford Bridge faithful singing the new manager’s name.

‌



Let’s not forget they did not sing Enzo Maresca’s name or Liam Rosenior. And Alonso is a former Liverpool player so it could easily have been a hard sell.

‌



But not with Chelsea playing like this. Yes, they conceded three and look shaky at the back but they are also the great entertainers. Joao Pedro was electric, scored and played comedy villain with an own goal in front of the Brighton fans who gave their former striker pelters all afternoon.

Predictably, Cole Palmer stole the show with the all-important fourth goal to seal victory as he looks rejuvenated after his summer break through missing the World Cup.

Xabi Alonso speaks after axing Enzo Fernandez again and hints at Chelsea exit READ MORE :

Aston Villa and Chelsea relationship as Emi Martinez becomes EIGHTH transfer READ MORE :

Emiliano Martinez made his debut for Chelsea and, even though they concede far too many goals, at least they have top quality keeper behind their rather unreliable defence.

‌



Pedro Neto shone in his new role as right wing back and Chelsea look as if they could be realistic title challengers this season. Chelsea’s trip to reigning champions Arsenal next Sunday already looks like a blockbuster.

But really it is the flair, the movement and skill of Chelsea’s front three. Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers are as good as any forward line in the Premier League. Certainly no-one missed Enzo Fernandez who was missing again as he waits on a mega last-minute move to Manchester City while the only real concern was Moises Caicedo limping off just 14 minutes after coming on as a substitute.

View 3 Images Chelsea have scored seven goals in their opening two games

‌



But it is the entertainment value which gets Chelsea fans off their seats. They were ahead after just four minutes. Joao Pedro’s header was cleared off the line, but Mats Wieffer got in a horrible mix-up with keeper Bart Verbruggen and Chelsea midfielder Romeo Lavia pounced to squeeze home.

Incredibly, that was Lavia’s first goal in four very injury disrupted years. His last goal was on August 30, 2022, for Southampton against Chelsea. Maybe this season maybe the year where the talented midfielder’s luck changes.

Chelsea made it 2-0 after just 14 minutes. Jorrel Hato’s throw-in found Morgan Rogers and his low cross was swept in by Pedro Neto. Brighton’s bench were furious because Hato’s throw was so obviously taken from the wrong place.

‌



Joao Pedro missed a sitter to the delight of the Brighton fans. But their glee did not last long. Hato showed great strength to hold off Wieffer and then put over a low cross for Joao Pedro to score. It was 3-0.

View 3 Images Emiliano Martinez made his debut after joining from Aston Villa

Just three minutes later, Brighton gave themselves a glimmer of hope. Brighton striker Charalampos Kostoulas went through, Chelsea new boy Martinez saved bravely at his feet but Malick Yalcouyé smashed the loose ball in off the far post.

‌



Chelsea have not kept a clean sheet in the Premier League since last January. And worse was to follow. Martinez can expect to be busy. Then the comedy punchline. Pascal Gross’s low cross was deflected in off Joao Pedro. The Brighton fans were lapping it up and, from 3-0 down, the fightback was on. This had turned into a sensational game at 3-2.

But Brighton could not seize the opportunity. It was left to Palmer to steal the show again. Palmer strode forward from midfield, had time to pick his spot and fired into the bottom corner to make it safe at 4-2.

Still there was time for one more goal as Gross got a third for Brighton in the 96th minute. Clean sheets are a worry but who cares when you play such great attacking football? Chelsea fans don’t seem bothered.

Sports.title: Arsenal set to smash transfer record as Gabriel Martinelli closes in on Gunners exit
Sports.content:
Arsenal set to smash transfer record as Gabriel Martinelli closes in on Gunners exit

Arsenal have spent a considerable amount this summer as they attempt to defend their Premier League crown but a few title winners could potentially be on the way out of the Emirates over the coming days

View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli is set to earn Arsenal a record amount (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal star Gabriel Martinelli is set to leave the Emirates and join Al-Hilal for a record £55m. The Brazilian winger has been linked with a move away from North London throughout the summer.

‌



Saudi side Al-Hilal had emerged as suitors over recent days and had been holding talks with the Gunners in an effort to secure a deal. And it appears that they have done just that.

‌



According to reports, Martinelli is set to fly over to the Middle East over the next few days to undergo a medical and complete a move worth around €65m (£55.7m) ahead of Tuesday's deadline.

‌



Should the move go through as expected, it would see Arsenal bank their highest fee ever for a sale, smashing the £35m that they received from Liverpool for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain back in 2017.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Asked about Martinelli's future in his pre-match press conference, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said: "That's another personal situation that we're dealing with. I think everybody knows and recognises how much we love Gabi. Whatever the outcome is, it will be because everybody agrees to that."

‌



Martinelli joined Arsenal from Brazilian side Ituano in 2019 and he has gone on to score 62 goals in 278 appearances in all competitions. He helped the club win the Premier League last season.

Martinelli is not the only league winner set to leave the club over the coming days. Striker Gabriel Jesus is anticipated to complete a switch to Barcelona.

Asked why the forward was not in training, Arteta said: "It's something to do with the numbers that we have in the squad at the moment and the way we're managing that kind of situation individually with all the players - they have some personal situations."

‌



View 2 Images Gabriel Jesus is also expected to quit Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Asked if he had held conversations with either Martinelli or Jesus, Arteta replied: "Yes, for sure. Those conversations go both ways, but I'm very satisfied with how these conversations went because I know what is in each other's hearts, and the words that come through in those conversations make me really happy.

"But it's inevitable at some point you need to have certain discussions and say certain things that sometimes are tough."

‌



Along with Jesus and Martinelli, Fabio Vieira is also set to depart, with talks over an £8.6m move to Hamburg advancing.

Leandro Trossard, Christian Norgaard and Jakub Kiwior have all left North London over recent weeks, while academy graduate Reiss Nelson saw his deal cancelled by mutual consent. Arsenal have refreshed their side with a number of big-money signings including Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis, Ezri Konsa and Piero Hincapie.

Sports.title: Julian Alvarez makes Atletico Madrid decision after Arsenal transfer call with Mikel Arteta
Sports.content:
Julian Alvarez makes Atletico Madrid decision after Arsenal transfer call with Mikel Arteta

Julian Alvarez has missed three training sessions this week and did not feature in his side’s trip to Sevilla on Saturday as his transfer standoff continues

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez during a Atletico Madrid training session (Image: (Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press via Getty Images))

Julian Alvarez has returned to Atletico Madrid training after Diego Simeone vowed to welcome him back into his squad. Alvarez missed three training sessions this week and did not feature in his side’s 3-1 victory over Sevilla on Saturday night due to what the club said was a stomach bug.

‌



Atletico are standing firm in their refusal to sell Alvarez to Barcelona, with Arsenal leading the race to sign the forward. However, it has been claimed that the Argentine informed Gunners boss Mikel Arteta during talks that he does not want to return to England.

‌



Providing an update on Alvarez, Atletico sporting director Matheu Alemany said: "He trained yesterday, and we hope he recovers quickly and is ready for the upcoming La Liga match."

‌



He added: "We have been very clear and firm on this matter. The board issued a statement about it, and the chief executive confirmed it clearly and firmly. I refer you to that. Why should I say more?”

Simone said ahead of their 3-1 win against Sevilla on Saturday night: "I understand that all the questions will be about Julian. The club has been very clear about what will happen.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"From a sporting perspective, I hope to help him continue being as important as he still is. My focus is on Sevilla, where he won't be available.

"When he returns, we’ll give him everything he needs to feel important. In life, anything can be reversed, as long as we have our health."

‌



Atletico have issued two public statements insisting they will not sell Alvarez to Barca, with a move elsewhere now appearing to be the only realistic option. And speaking on Thursday, Atletico chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin told Spanish broadcaster Movistar Plus: "Our intention and ⁠my personal dream is for him to stay with us, to remain at Atletico.

View 2 Images Diego Simeone talks to Julian Alvarez during an Atletico Madrid Champions League game (Image: (Manu Reino/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images))

"To compete among ‌the greats, you need great players, and Julian is one. If he believes that staying at Atletico Madrid is no longer feasible, we will look for an alternative, but it will never, ever be Barcelona.”

‌



Gil Marin continued: "The truth is that it outrages us even more. We are repulsed by the dishonesty, the lack of ethics, transparency and professionalism, and we can only insist that we will not negotiate with Barcelona under any circumstances.

"I have the support of everyone working with me, from shareholders ⁠to directors, and the only certain ‌and firm decision is that we will not negotiate with Barcelona under any circumstances; you have my word – which is one of the few things I have – the ‌player will most certainly not be transferred to Barcelona.”

Sports.title: England player ratings: Seamers sizzle again as Cox impresses with the bat
Sports.content:
We rate England's players after the 194-run, series-sealing victory over Pakistan at Lord's, with the seamers once again standing out...

Ben Duckett - 4

Batting: 17 and 1

A forgettable Test which saw the England opener face only 26 deliveries across his two innings.

He was one of a number of batters who perhaps felt a touch unfortunate to be given out lbw in the first innings to deliveries that, at first glance, looked to be going over the stumps, only to be shown otherwise after a timely Pakistan review.

His second-innings failure, however, simply owed to a poor shot as he chipped one straight to mid-off.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England opener Emilio Gay was out to an unplayable delivery from Mohammad Abbas that scuttled through low

Emilio Gay - 5

Batting: 8 and 31

It's a cruel game.

Gay can count himself unfortunate in both innings, with Mohammad Rizwan claiming a terrific diving grab off little more than a leg-side strangle in the first innings, before a devastating grubber did for him lbw when batting was at its toughest on a rain-interrupted third day.

He'd batted determinedly through to stumps on the second evening, a quality that has been evident since making his debut this summer, but his place in the side is coming under increasing scrutiny with Jacob Bethell still to return after this series and others staking a claim.

Jordan Cox - 7

Batting: 55 and 11

Cox is one such player pushing for a permanent spot in the side as he registered a second fifty in as many Tests since his reintroduction in place of the injured Bethell at No 3.

Speaking to Sky Sports Cricket ahead of the Lord's Test, Cox said of the opportunity handed to him: "This could be your only shot, make sure this counts".

He's come close to doing just that, looking very assured out in the middle, just as he did at Headingley.

A century once again eluded him - this time thanks to an absolute screamer of a catch from Salman Ali Agha, one of the best slip catches you're ever likely to see.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Salman Ali Agha took this screamer of a catch at slip to remove Jordan Cox on day one at Lord's

Joe Root - 4

Batting: 4 and 24

Does Root have an lbw problem?

"It's fascinating that even a guy of more than 160 Tests, who averages over 50 - one of the greatest players England have ever produced - teams will still be looking at that developing trend," Sky Sports' Michael Atherton said as the skipper fell leg before wicket in both innings, making it seven such dismissals this summer and nine times in his last 12 Test innings'.

He's far from the only batter to succumb in such fashion this summer, with lbw dismissals on the rise as a whole in seamer-friendly conditions, but it's certainly something he'll be eager to correct with a big score in the final Test at Edgbaston.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Nasser Hussain and Michael Atherton discuss the reasons behind Joe Root's recent vulnerability to lbw dismissals in Test cricket

Harry Brook - 5

Batting: 15 and 34

Brook batted better than his run haul would suggest, particularly in the second innings where he cautiously negotiated a testing period on the second evening, before building a promising partnership with Dan Lawrence on day three - with conditions at their toughest.

Just as in the first innings, though, when bowled by a devastating Mohammad Ali in-ducker, one eventually had his name on it when grazing a faint shoulder edge to Rizwan, stood up to the stumps, off Mohammad Abbas.

Has caught pretty consistently in the slips all summer, but put down Azan Awais on eight as he went on to score 46 in the first innings.

Dan Lawrence - 7

Batting: 17 and 54

Lawrence is another staking his claim for a permanent place in the side, with the No 6 position seemingly suiting him perfectly as England look to fill the Ben Stokes-shaped hole left behind.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dan Lawrence smoked the shot of the series so far, hitting Mohammad Ali for six over extra-cover

While Lawrence could never hope to match Stokes' repeated and ridiculous feats of the past decade and more, he provides similar counter-attacking verve with the bat - which was on full display with his second-innings half century in testing conditions.

He also helps balance the side with his part-time off-spin to complement England's four-pronged pace attack, which we've admittedly yet to see a lot of.

Jamie Smith - 8

Batting: 61 and 7

There was a welcome return to form with the bat, too for Smith, as he tonked 61 off 80 deliveries in the first innings, featuring 10 boundaries.

It's precisely the sort of attacking prowess for which he made his name as he took to Test cricket like a dream in his first 18 months, only for it to then draw criticism as the runs dried up during a dismal Ashes drubbing, admitting to Sky Sports Cricket this week that "I have found it tough".

His impeccable keeping, particularly when stood up to the stumps, earns him an extra mark.

Image: Jamie Smith scored a half-century at Lord's and was immaculate with the wicketkeeping gloves

Gus Atkinson - 6

Bowling: 0-33 and 0-41

Batting: 45 and 7

Atkinson is the one to feel the pinch of England's four-pronged pace attack at the moment, being reduced to second change and rarely being afforded the end he wants to bowl from.

There simply aren't enough wickets to spread around, given Ollie Robinson and Jofra Archer's success with the new ball and Josh Tongue's taste for the tail.

Atkinson is certainly not bowling poorly, with a pacey spell prior to tea on the fourth afternoon a particular standout, but he's just bagged the one wicket so far in the series and will be eager to cash in at Edgbaston.

His batting was a positive, enjoying himself again at Lord's - the scene of his Test hundred - as he cracked 45 in the first innings.

Ollie Robinson - 9

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ollie Robinson struck twice in one over at Lord's on Sunday, removing Azan Awais and Abdullah Shafique

Bowling: 4-11 and 4-24

Batting: 0 and 8

That's three Test matches played this summer and three Player of the Match awards secured. Just let some of these numbers wash over you...

Robinson returned astonishing match figures of 8-35 across his 27 overs of supremely skilful bowling.

He now has 99 wickets in 23 Tests played, at an average of 19.53! And that average only improves to 15.45 for his five career Tests at Lord's, and an astonishing 8.34 for his three appearances this summer.

"There will be more questions asked of Robinson, on difficult pitches to bowl seam up on - his fitness will have to come into play - but in these conditions, at the moment he's England's best bowler," Sky Sports Cricket's Nasser Hussain said post-match.

"For someone who was left out of the side for quite some time, to suddenly come back and be England's best bowler is some achievement. You've got to take your hat off to him.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Robinson, player of the match at Lord's, speaks glowingly about England's bowling attack

"He now has to ask himself, the backroom staff, and people like Stuart Broad and James Anderson, 'what do I need to do to become the complete bowler?' That's how you grow as a player and a team."

Jofra Archer - 8

Bowling: 3-26 and 2-73

Batting: 14 and 2no

Deserved more than just a five-wicket haul from the match, particularly in the first innings where he could and perhaps should have taken that many alone.

According to CricViz, Archer's opening spell averaged 90.7 mph, with the odd delivery touching 94mph, as he picked up the flat-footed Shan Masood caught behind.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jofra Archer dismissed Pakistan captain Babar Azam with a brute of a short ball on day four at Lord's

He repeatedly threatened both edges of the bat thereafter but without reward - Azan playing and missing as many as 14 times to the quick - until returning to dismantle the tail late on.

He also saw off Babar Azam with a brute of bouncer in the second innings as he and Robinson reduced Pakistan to 14-3 as part of another devastating new-ball spell.

Josh Tongue - 7

Bowling: 2-27 and 3-46

Batting: 30no and 12

Tongue got Abdullah Shafique and Babar Azam nicking off either side of lunch on day two, before feasting on the tail once more in the second innings. He had also successfully set the trap for Saud Shakeel, who happily hooked into it, falling three runs short of a well-deserved hundred.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Josh Tongue and Archer put their football skills to the test with a spot of keepy-uppies at Lord's

He continues to prove his worth as part of this attack, albeit he does leak runs - particularly when bowling to left-handers, which will need to be addressed - as he went at over five an over for his 14.5 overs bowled.

He smacked a few to the fence himself at No 11, part of an impressive 47-run final-wicket partnership in the first innings as he and Atkinson had some fun on the second morning.

Sports.title: Hits and misses: Mainoo impresses as well as Fernandes
Sports.content:
Bruno stars but Mainoo impresses too

Bruno Fernandes produced yet another match-winning performance for Manchester United in their come-from-behind 5-2 win over Ipswich. The Premier League assist king could not depart without throwing one of those in too for United's fifth at Old Trafford.

"I understand Bruno will be getting a lot of the credit but [Kobbie Mainoo] was immense," said Michael Carrick afterwards. Fernandes was indeed the player of the match, but it was the performance of Mainoo against Ipswich that was most encouraging for United.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the match between Man Utd and Ipswich Town

Carrick said the efforts of the young midfielder "underpinned the result of the team" and Mainoo certainly impressed. On a pitch packed with talent, he completed more dribbles than anyone else, used the ball smartly and produced three tackles too.

Interestingly, Mainoo's physicality stood out. His robustness in this particular game, controlling midfield, serves as a reminder that he is still only 21 years old. He has been around a long time already, had his ups and downs, but this is a player who can keep developing.

What he needs is time on the pitch after a World Cup in which he was a squad member for England but remained a spectator throughout. After a watching brief under Ruben Amorim at United too, there are signs that he can grow under Carrick.

He will need to do so given the competition. Carlos Baleba was introduced to the Old Trafford crowd before the game. Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos have arrived too. That represents a major challenge for Mainoo to show that he belongs on the pitch.

"It is about trying to make the most of the combinations," said Carrick when discussing that midfield. But whatever combination works best for United in the long term, this performance from Mainoo was a step towards showing that he must be part of it.

Adam Bate

Is Chelsea's low possession a problem?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Chelsea and Brighton & Hove Albion

Chelsea supporters were thrilled by the speed and incisiveness of their side's attacks against Brighton. They scored four goals to add to their three against Fulham and could easily have had more.

But the victory also featured a record low possession share. Xabi Alonso's side only had 25.6 per cent of it. Their total of 146 completed passes was also their lowest on record since 2003/04.

It followed them only having 38 per cent of the possession in the win over the Cottagers, giving them the third-lowest average in the division at the time of writing. But does it matter? Few fans would say so, as long as the results continue to go their way.

Alonso stressed the importance of context. As against Fulham, his side spent almost the entire game leading against Brighton, meaning the attacking onus was on their opponent.

"You need to have context for every data for sure," he said. "After 30 minutes we scored the 3-0. Probably in that moment, we played too much with the result instead of keeping playing.

"But the data is not important, it is how you play and what we can do better. It is never that approach. I don't say, 'today we need to have 60 per cent or 20 cent'. I never talk about those things, it is about how to prepare, how to be more competitive."

Chelsea have shown the extent of their counter-attacking threat in their opening games. Clearly, it is going to be a major weapon for Alonso. But privately, he will also accept the need for more control, too, in the absence of the exiled Enzo Fernandez and the seemingly injured again Moises Caicedo. "It is a process," he added.

Nick Wright

Squad depth bodes well for Sunderland in Fulham win

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Sunderland’s match against Fulham in the Premier League

It is going to be a squad game for Sunderland this season as they juggle domestic and European matters.

So it bodes well for Regis Le Bris that it was two of his substitutes that settled the game against Fulham on Sunday.

Habib Diarra with the cross, Wilson Isidor the finish. Both had been introduced together 10 minutes before the goal.

Isidor, in particular, showed resolve in getting into a good position again after missing a glorious chance a few minutes earlier.

The 26-year-old had been linked with a move away this summer, but signed a new contract this week and celebrated perfectly at the Stadium of Light.

"[Isidor] has a good future," Le Bris said after the game. "He has to work hard again and again but he showed really good qualities.

"It's important and the lads are really clear now about the rotation of the squad. They all want to be a starter but it's not possible and the group is well-connected.

"You see they are frustrated when they are on the bench but they know they will have opportunities and this season is going to be really long and demanding so the roles they have are clear."

They will need him plenty this season if they are to compete.

Simeon Gholam

Leeds and Brentford show growth as Farke's changes come good

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Sunderland’s match against Fulham in the Premier League

Leeds showed their Premier League grit and manager Daniel Farke his tactical prowess in earning a point against Brentford, who are evolving under Keith Andrews.

Brentford had been by far the stronger side in the first half at Elland Road with Kevin Schade's clever finish putting them ahead as they restricted Leeds to just two shots, none on target, while having 11 of their own.

This same fixture in March ended 0-0. "The way we had to approach it was quite pragmatic," said Andrews of that day. "Today was a different mindset as a group. How we've started the season has been built on what we did last season - you could see that in the first half."

Leeds could not match Brentford's aggression, nor their quality on the ball, until Farke switched to a back four at half-time, adding Ao Tanaka into the midfield and Harry Wilson initially off the right.

It worked at first but Brentford's centre-backs Kristoffer Ajer and Nathan Collins still weren't being troubled enough and Farke brought on Lukas Nmecha to partner Dominic Calvert-Lewin in a 4-4-2.

Dan James was also introduced to provide width on the right, with Anton Stach tucked inside on the left to guard against Brentford's three-man midfield, now up against an unorthodox but fresh pairing of Tanaka and Wilson with Ethan Ampadu moved to right-back.

And Leeds' goal came when James combined with Ampadu and his low cross was controlled by Nmecha, who flashed the ball across the six-yard box to be turned in by Calvert-Lewin.

Farke's tactical flexibility and his side's determination to not fold when Brentford were on top shows how Leeds are slowly establishing themselves in the top flight.

David Richardson

Sports.title: 'Any side in world cricket would find it hard against England bowling attack'
Sports.content:
Nasser Hussain says any side in the world would find it tough against England's bowling attack in current conditions after they shredded Pakistan yet again to help Joe Root's side to a series win with a game to spare.

An inexperienced Pakistan outfit have been skittled for under 200 in all four innings so far, only batting in excess of 50 overs once, with the relentless accuracy of Ollie Robinson complemented superbly by the pace of Jofra Archer, Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson.

Thoughts have inevitably turned to how the quartet may fare in the home Ashes next summer, a series England will be looking to win for the first time in over a decade, while there is also a mouth-watering assignment in South Africa in prospect this winter.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the best of day four at Lord's as England thumped Pakistan by 194 runs to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match Test series

Speaking after Root's men rolled Pakistan for 194 on day four at Lord's to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match contest, Sky Sports pundit Hussain said: "That four-pronged attack looks really strong, offering so many different things.

"Robinson is hugely skilful, Tongue has the angle, Atkinson has his skiddy pace and Archer is just box office. When he bounced out Babar Azam it reminded me of the spell he bowled to Steve Smith in the 2019 Ashes.

"I wouldn't judge them on how they go against Pakistan but I think pretty much any side in world cricket would find it hard work against this attack, in these conditions.

"I also think this attack would have gone really well in the last Ashes and I think it will go really well in South Africa but it will be tested more."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Robinson, player of the match at Lord's, speaks glowingly about England's bowling attack

Robinson impresses - but more questions to come

The metronomic Robinson has led the way with 16 wickets across the first two Tests at an average of just 7.18, and when you add in his seven-wicket match haul against New Zealand at Lord's in June, his record for the summer is a remarkable 23 scalps at 8.34.

The 32-year-old had spent over two years in the international wilderness before his recent recall, mainly due to fitness concerns, but his return has been a raging success and highlighted just what England were missing during their Ashes drubbing last winter.

Hussain said of Robinson: "England bowled in some very useful conditions in The Ashes and kept dishing up short and wide deliveries - Travis Head could not believe the amount of cut shots he got away.

"It's been nice these last few months to see an England opening bowler using the skills he has to target the stumps and the pads, making sure he is always in the game. That's what Robinson does from the first ball to his last.

I would find Robinson a nightmare to face in these conditions as at times you are putting your bat there and guessing if you are going to hit it.

"There will be more questions asked of him, on difficult pitches to bowl seam on - his fitness will have to come into play. But in these conditions, he's England's best bowler - as good as you get

"For someone who was left out of the side for quite some time to suddenly come back and be England's best bowler is some achievement. You have to take your hat off to him.

"He now has to ask himself, the backroom staff, and people like Stuart Broad and James Anderson, 'what do I need to do to become the complete bowler?' That's how you grow as a player and a team."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Robinson struck twice in one over at Lord's on Sunday, removing Azan Awais and Abdullah Shafique

Hussain: Archer has looked fit all summer

Archer, who has deserved more than the eight wickets he has picked up in the series so far, bowled his fastest opening spell in Test cricket when he clocked an average of 90.7mph against Pakistan in the Lord's Test, according to CricViz.

Hussain added: "I spoke to Archer here during the ODI series against India this summer and he said 'I am consistently bowling well' - and not in an arrogant way.

"Everyone has also noted how fit Jofra has looked all summer.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jofra Archer dismissed Pakistan captain Babar Azam with a brute of a short ball on day four at Lord's

"People were worried when he came back from the IPL whether he had got enough overs and workload in and he was left out of the first Test against New Zealand. But he has played a lot of cricket since, playing all the time.

"Stuart Broad made the excellent point that when he worries about fitness, speeds and rhythm is when bowlers play and then don't play again for a month. Jofra playing all the time means he can sustain his speeds."

Why Root will be 'slightly frustrated'

Broad has also been enthused by England's attack and feels there is no need to break it up by introducing a frontline spinner - but he warned the bowler-friendly conditions means only so much can be gleaned from their success.

The Sky Cricket expert added: "Robinson has hit immaculate areas and moved the ball consistently. The other seamers hit 90mph consistently, so you have variety.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stuart Broad assesses Joe Root's developing England side after their brushed Pakistan aside

"My belief is that we don't have a good enough spinner so why bother when you have South Africa away and the Ashes next summer?

"Root will be delighted with what he has seen but what will frustrate him slightly is how much the ball has been doing.

"I don't think we are learning a huge amount about the bowling unit or batting unit as it has been such different conditions.

"You don't see Test match batters get bowled or lbw as much as we have seen this summer and that is due to conditions.

"I don't know if we will end the summer going, 'we have learnt so much about this team, we are positive about what's coming in the future', but two wins out of two is exactly what you'd expect and the team have delivered."

Sports.title: Fernandes fires hat-trick as Manchester United fight back to thrash Ipswich
Sports.content:
To follow the claiming of both the major footballer of the year awards by scoring a hat-trick in Manchester United’s first home game was some Bruno Fernandes act, and points to an intent to continue his stellar form of last season.

Ipswich came to scythe through Michael Carrick’s side via the pace of Julio Enciso, Issa Diop and Daizen Maeda, and when Leif Davis gave them a 29th-minute lead victory looked on. However, the contest turned with Marcelino Núñez’s slip as the break neared. Suddenly Fernandes was rifling in a left-foot bullet and from this point on United cuffed Gary O’Neil’s team aside.

In 12 second-half minutes United scored three times – the first a somewhat contentious Jacob Greaves own goal, the next a penalty and a close-range finish from Fernandes, strikes that made it three for the day for him. Bryan Mbeumo made it five from range on 82 minutes.

Carrick was emphatic that the pathetic 2-0 downing at Hull last week was “just one game” and he was proved correct – at least going forward. But Davis’s opener derived from holes being punched in the rearguard, and Ipswich’s added-time consolation came from sloppy defending by Lisandro Martínez that allowed Enciso to set up Chuba Akpom.

View image in fullscreen The Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes scored one before half-time and two after to help his team recover from going behind. Photograph: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images

But having the Professional Footballers’ Association Player of the Year and the Football Writers’ Player of the Year leading the side is a definite boon. If Fernandes shines so, too, usually do United. The Hull horror show caused Carrick to make four changes. Out went Ayden Heaven, Noussair Mazraoui, Andrey Santos and Patrick Dorgu; in came Martínez, Diogo Dalot, Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford, who was starting a United league game for the first time since 1 December 2024 when he scored twice here in a 4-0 win against Everton.

Operating in his favoured wide-left berth, Rashford took a first shot that deflected into Kjell Scherpen’s hands. Then Ipswich’s No 1 gazed skywards as Matheus Cunha’s effort sailed high, the chance made by Rashford’s dribble and lay-off.

Ipswich’s fine opening-day win against Sunderland convinced O’Neil to retain that starting XI and, after knocking Leicester out of the Carabao Cup in midweek with a much changed team, they were in a buoyant mood. Their challenge was to end a run of seven league games against United without a win; Maeda’s blistering run down the left and cross gave us a clue regarding how they planned to do so.

Enciso then careered 60 yards towards Senne Lammens in a footrace with Mbeumo and Luke Shaw. This came after Rashford’s loose ball could be hacked upfield; United’s left-back and right winger did well not to foul the Paraguayan, so, too, Lammens when saving his attempt. From the rebound United broke instantly in a foray that featured Rashford ­seeing the ball slide agonisingly past as he sought to poke home, and Fernandes’s effort being blocked. The tempo was high, the speed of thought similar. Davis’s knifing ball cut United apart, Maeda raced forward, and Lammens flew left to tip away a goal-bound shot.

Now came jubilant cries of “one‑nil to the Tractor Boys” as Ipswich scored an excellent opener that was poor from Shaw. Along the right, Diop ghosted past the defender and picked out the lurking Davis who rifled in off the bar to leave Carrick turning and shaking his head. Shaw’s sluggishness was emblematic of a soporific backline. Another example came when Davis was, again, free to take aim; Lammens saved the header but the alarm clanged.

So Ipswich, in the ascendancy, should not slip up – which is precisely what Núñez did inside United territory. Cunha put in the sprinting Fernandes, who left Scherpen a statue.

View image in fullscreen Marcelino Núñez (centre) lost his footing at an inopportune time to allow Manchester United to equalise. Photograph: MDI/Shutterstock

After half-time, United exerted control. Rat-a-tat-tat went a sequence that involved Mainoo, Youri Tielemans and Fernandes that moved them into the penalty area. This impressed, as did a leaping Rashford who turned Dalot’s diagonal back across goal only for Mbeumo to hit the bar.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Carrick’s team had transformed from a bitty side to a more flowing one. The net result: two goals that pulled them into a 3-1 lead.

A cohesive attack finished with Harry Maguire’s shot rebounding in off Greaves’s foot. Maguire’s hands touched the ball in the movement that brought it under control yet the video assistant referee ruled this legal, as it was accidental.

Ipswich, dizzied, now conceded a penalty. Slick Mainoo work released Cunha and, as he entered the area, Greaves brought him down, earning a yellow card. Fernandes swept home from the spot, beating Scherpen to the keeper’s right. Fernandes’s third arrived in the 66th minute. Mainoo and Mbeumo saw shots repelled before the captain, benefiting from a ricochet, racked up his team’s fourth – and his hat-trick – with aplomb, scoring in the far right corner.

View image in fullscreen Leif Davis gave United feelings of deja vu as they went behind to a promoted team for the second week running. Photograph: Matt West/Shutterstock

As cascading rain showed up the leak in the roof over the Stretford End, Mbeumo lobbed the on-rushing Scherpen from around 40 yards into Ipswich’s goal there - to unified home delight. Next came Martínez’s blunder, but after lightning the downpour ceased and the final whistle from the referee, Craig Pawson, was greeted by applause. United last hit five in the league in the opening game of the 2021-22 season, in a 5-1 win against Leeds at Old Trafford. What Carrick must ensure now is consistency.

Sports.title: Chelsea hold off Brighton in 4-3 win but remain chaotic under Xabi Alonso
Sports.content:
In the fullness of time Chelsea’s surrender against Brighton in April may be seen as the turning point. The humiliation accelerated Liam ­Rosenior’s demise and forced the Stamford Bridge hierarchy into a ­reckoning leading to the appointment of Xabi Alonso, a shift in ­transfer ­strategy, the birth of the JP Morgan front three and the end of ­Robert Sánchez’s time in goal.

For now, though, the argument that Emiliano Martínez is the final piece in the jigsaw seems a touch ­premature. With seven goals scored and five conceded while winning their first two league games, it is not hard to see where Chelsea need to improve in order to sustain a title challenge. They have to be savvier when ahead, and although the good has so far outweighed the bad Alonso could do with his side not dropping their guard when they have the ­opposition on the ropes.

Alonso’s cool disappeared as ­Chelsea’s focus dipped after they went 3-0 up against an injury‑hit Brighton inside 32 minutes. ­Stamford Bridge was anxious when a João Pedro own‑goal cut the ­advantage to one just after the hour. Alonso was ­shouting at his bench and it was only when Cole Palmer scored with 16 minutes left that calm was restored.

View image in fullscreen Xabi Alonso has won his first two league games as Chelsea manager, but neither have been what you would call relaxing. Photograph: David Klein/Reuters

Not for long, mind you, given that Brighton still managed to grab a consolation through Pascal Gross deep into added time.

It was that kind of game, Martínez conceding three despite playing well on his debut after joining from Aston Villa for £7.5m. “We can hurt teams,” the Argentina goalkeeper said. “At the back, we need to bring the goals down.”

Alonso agreed. Chelsea have been thrilling in transition – they beat Fulham with 37% possession last Monday and had only 26% against Brighton – but they must tighten up when they visit Arsenal next Sunday.

Equally, few sights will be more captivating this season than Palmer combining with João Pedro and ­Morgan Rogers in attack. Palmer looks refreshed after a summer off and Chelsea will be dangerous when games turn into shootouts. They have so many ways to score. The hope is that there will be more stability with Martínez in position.

Alonso did not hesitate to start Martínez, even though the ­Argentinian lacks match ­practice and joined on Friday. “He felt ready,” Alonso said of Martínez, the first 30‑something player to start for ­Chelsea since ­Thiago Silva in May 2024. “We will feel his ­presence because he has this charisma, this aura to influence.”

Chelsea, again in a 3-4-2-1 system, are getting serious. Sánchez was not even on the bench against his old side and needs to leave. There was a huge ovation for Martínez before kick‑off and it was followed by the focus switching to Brighton’s No 1 in the fourth minute, a handling error from Bart Verbruggen allowing Roméo Lavia to put Chelsea ahead after Mats Wieffer had cleared a João Pedro header off the line from a corner.

It was a lovely moment for Lavia. It was four years to the day since the Belgian’s last goal, against Chelsea coincidentally enough. His luck with injuries is hopefully turning.

View image in fullscreen Roméo Lavia was on hand to punish Bart Verbruggen’s early handling error and put Chelsea 1-0 up. Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

Lavia starting his second consecutive league game was important with Chelsea light in midfield. Moisés Caicedo limped off after coming on in the second half, Reece James started on the bench and Enzo ­Fernández was off ­pining for a move to ­Manchester City, so Malo Gusto moved in from right wing-back to partner Lavia.

Chelsea’s selection issues were nothing compared to Brighton’s problems, though. Fabian Hürzeler did not use the absence of Jack Hinshelwood, Yasin Ayari, Georginio Rutter, Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh as an excuse, but it had an impact.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Chelsea were rampant. Rogers ­continued his fine start after joining from Villa, creating the second goal with a powerful surge away from Luka Vuskovic in the 14th ­minute. Brighton were caught cold by a throw‑in and Rogers crossed for Pedro Neto to score.

Linked with a move away this summer, Neto has been repurposed by Alonso as a wing-back and was bright. João Pedro missed a chance after strong pressing from the ­Portugal international. The away end jeered but João Pedro converted his next opportunity, when a Rogers flick sent Jorrel Hato flying down the left to set the former Brighton striker up.

View image in fullscreen João Pedro rather summed up Chelsea’s start under Xabi Alonso with a goal, an assist and an own goal. Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

Chelsea’s mistake was thinking it was over. Brighton responded before half‑time, Malick Yalcouyé ­volleying in after Martínez made a brave block from ­Charalampos ­Kostoulas. “They showed belief in their quality,” ­Hürzeler said of his players.

The German thought Brighton deserved more. Chelsea were wobbling when João Pedro diverted a Gross cross past Martínez. Diego Gómez then lashed a shot wide and Martínez denied Olivier Boscagli the equaliser.

Alonso needed his big players to step up. Palmer, who had earlier sidefooted over from close range, delivered when he took a João Pedro flick and bent a shot past Verbruggen. Chelsea will be anything but dull.

Sports.title: Sunderland’s Wilson Isidor applies the finishing touch to sink Fulham
Sports.content:
At the final whistle Álvaro Arbeloa provided a study in pensiveness while Régis Le Bris simply looked relieved. For protracted periods an almost palpable fear of losing formed the subtext of a match decided when two of the Sunderland manager’s ­second-half substitutes, Habib Diarra and Wilson Isidor, combined for the latter to score.

Isidor’s goal not merely supplied Sunderland with their first win of the season while leaving Arbeloa’s side pointless, but also ended his side’s 17‑year run without a Premier League home victory against Fulham.

“It wasn’t our day for sure,” said Marco Silva’s successor, whose team were confounded repeatedly by Sunderland’s outstanding central defender Nordi Mukiele.

“We need to improve many things, for sure, especially the energy and the attitude.

“It was a tough game for us. Sunderland were better for many ­minutes. It’s not easy here. If you want to come to Sunderland and play the way you want to, then you need the right mentality. We need to show more energy and fight for every ball.”

Le Bris was a little happier, ­saying: “We didn’t create enough. Fulham were well organised but we had a good balance to manage the transitions. We had to be smart. It’s a question of balancing risk and organisation.”

The tone of a cagey, risk‑averse first half dominated by Fulham’s ­cautious low block was raised, albeit sporadically, by a typically indus­trious central-midfield performance by Sunderland’s Noah Sadiki.

The visiting gameplan seemed all about ouncing on the counterattack but the Democratic Republic of the Congo international extinguished so many potential visiting fires that Fulham’s sole real chance during the opening 45 minutes involved Josh King finding himself confounded by geometry as he miscued a tightly angled opening conjured by Alex Iwobi. Otherwise the home goalkeeper, Robin Roefs, was left pretty much undisturbed.

That apart, a slightly nervous impasse endured. Despite dominating possession, Sunderland’s attacking edge proved anything but serrated, leaving Bernd Leno severely underemployed in Fulham’s goal.

It all left both Le Bris and Arbeloa with much to ponder at the interval. If the watching Sunderland owner, Kyril-Louis Dreyfus, required a reminder as to precisely why Le Bris is so keen to sign a specialist right winger and another striker before the transfer window’s closure he received it.

View image in fullscreen Wilson Isidor salutes the fans after scoring. Photograph: Matt McNulty/Getty Images

At least Sunderland’s manager had the excellent Mukiele restored to his backline following injury. The former Paris Saint-Germain defender’s importance on Wearside was, not for the first time, underscored as, early in the second half his tremendous sliding challenge blocked Gonzalo García’s path to a near certain goal following Sander Berge’s stellar through pass.

“I was really impressed with Nordi and I told him this,” Le Bris said. “Nordi showed us today that he’s a great player.”

García, meanwhile, had scored twice in his first two games since joining Fulham from Real Madrid but found Sunderland’s rearguard difficult to decode. Nonetheless, ­perhaps sensing that the visitors were ­gaining a slight initiative, Le Bris made a ­double substitution.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

On came Diarra and Isidor for the hitherto largely ineffective Nilson Angulo and Brian Brobbey. Within minutes Sunderland should have been ahead after Enzo Le Fée played a beautiful, first-time ball across goal.

It seemed easier for the on-rushing Isidor to score than miss but, somehow, he ended up striking the base of a post and, in the technical area. Le Bris was left sinking to his knees in disappointment after making a premature celebratory leap as the delivery left Le Fée’s boot. “It was such a good chance,” he said. “It was such a shame.”

Poor Isidor looked mortified but redemption beckoned. Just moments later he surged onto another fabulous low dispatch across the box – from Diarra this time – and atonement arrived as his high-velocity shot whizzed past Leno.

Diarra and Isidor had succeeded in breathing new life into Sunderland’s suddenly much more dynamic press – not to mention capitalising on ­Fulham’s high defensive line – but the former’s cameo was to prove short‑lived after an injury necessitated his replacement by Chris Rigg.

No matter, he and Isidor, had already done just enough. “Habib is so, so intense,” Le Bris said. “He and Wilson changed our press, it was tactically the same just with 20-30% more energy. But the most important thing is, as we saw this afternoon, that the core of this group are very good.

“The players are all in. You can’t play at this level if you’re not all in and well connected with the project of the club. If we can add one or two signings that can help this group then we’ll do it. But I have trust and con­fidence in this squad.”

How Arbeloa must wish he could say the same.

Sports.title: Calvert-Lewin cancels out Schade’s opener as Leeds salvage point against Brentford
Sports.content:
These nascent moments of the new season can often provide false hope but, as both sets of players shook hands after what was indisputably the correct result at Elland Road, it was difficult not to imagine we had just witnessed a contest between two sides that should have lofty ­ambitions for the months ahead.

Leeds and Brentford were vic­torious on the opening weekend in differing circumstances. Leeds crafted a hard-earned but ultimately deserved win at Nottingham Forest, while Brentford Tottenham. Time will tell what the ceiling of both these sides is but, as they each continued their unbeaten starts here, hopes should be high.

This was a thoroughly ­entertaining game but it was also an occasion in which both managers, as well as the players, displayed their importance to their respective clubs.

Managers are scrutinised at every turn but Daniel Farke and Keith Andrews both excelled here. Both have had question marks as to whether they were the right man to take their team forward: Andrews when he was surprisingly appointed just over a year ago, and Farke in the difficult early stages of last season.

Andrews’s tactical nous was at its peak in the first half. He nullified the Leeds back five and his team led at half-time and probably should have been more than a single goal in front. Kevin Schade’s wonderful flick to turn home a Keane Lewis-Potter cross was the least the visitors deserved.

However, Farke showed his own tactical flexibility at the break. The German was under immense pressure last November and at real risk of losing his job before a move to a back five away at Manchester City proved the catalyst to transform Leeds’s season. He did the reverse here, going back to a four and matching Brentford in the second half to great effect.

Spearheaded by the impact of Ao Tanaka and Lukas Nmecha, both on as substitutes, the hosts were the stronger of the two sides after half‑time. They ultimately got the equaliser their play deserved when ­Nmecha’s shot across goal was prodded home by Dominic Calvert-Lewin to ensure it would be a point apiece, and four from the first two for both sides.

The early evidence overall? Leeds and Brentford should both be ­looking upwards this season. “It’s definitely a good point,” Farke said. “It was a very difficult and complicated game like we expected. Brentford were ­excellent in the first half and deserved to be in the lead, but I’m so proud of our reaction.”

His side struggled to get to grips with Brentford’s shape in the first half. Ethan Ampadu and Anton Stach were overrun in midfield, with the visitors’ three of Vitaly Janelt, ­Mamadou ­Sangaré and ­Mikkel Damsgaard ­running riot. James ­Trafford was called into action on multiple occasions, with smart saves to deny Igor Thiago and Schade.

Such was the strength of Brentford’s momentum that a goal felt inevitable. It duly arrived as half‑time approached when Lewis-Potter’s cross caught the Leeds backline off‑guard and Schade, with his back to goal, turned the ball home expertly to silence Elland Road.

As mentioned, perhaps the ­biggest gripe at that stage was that ­Brentford’s lead wasn’t greater. “I thought we could have done more in the first half,” Andrews said.

“We could have tested Trafford more but we were outstanding. The storm was always going to come and they were forced into ­making changes they haven’t done for quite some time.”

Those changes were pivotal. The back five was abandoned, with Leeds adding Tanaka as an extra man in midfield. It provided an instant impact, with the balance of play shifting the way of the hosts. James Justin forced a clever save from Caoimhín Kelleher before Dan James, on as a substitute, arguably could have done better after being set free on halfway.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In contrast, Brentford were struggling without as much space in the middle, with Igor Thiago cutting a slightly isolated and frustrated ­figure. The Leeds supporters, sensing the momentum was now with them, were beginning to come alive – as were their team. Just like in the first half, a goal was starting to feel more like an inevitability than a possibility.

Farke tweaked things further, with ­Nmecha pro­viding direct support for Calvert‑Lewin, and the duo combined with 11 ­minutes ­remaining. Nmecha dragged a shot across goal to leave Kelleher flat‑footed, with Calvert‑Lewin ­poking into the empty net for his first of the season.

A draw was the least Leeds deserved. Both sides showed their ambition by pushing for a winner, though they cancelled each other out in the final moments to underline further that these are two teams who should think positively about what lies ahead.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Shankland on the spot to ease pressure on McInnes and Rangers
Sports.content:
Lawrence Shankland’s second-half penalty gave Derek McInnes and Rangers some much-needed respite with a 1-0 win against Aberdeen at Pittodrie.

The tale since the Rangers manager arrived from Hearts in the summer has been one of constant change in formation and personnel amid exits from two European competitions and a poor start to the Premiership campaign. The Ibrox side turned in a better performance than many of late and in the 69th minute the captain, Shankland, a former Don, converted a spot-kick won by Djeidi Gassama.

The Aberdeen captain, Kevin Nisbet, had the ball in the Rangers net in the 81st minute but was judged to have pushed the full-back Dujon Sterling and the goal was ruled out.

McInnes has brought in 12 players including Kim Min-su, the 20-year-old South Korean winger signed from Girona on a four-year deal for a reported fee of about £8.5m, and who performed well on debut before he was replaced in the second half. Progress is proving frustratingly slow for their fans but three hard-fought points will bring some positivity to Ibrox.

“Probably for the first time this season, I’ve really enjoyed watching the team,” said McInnes. “There’s been moments of enjoyment. There’s been a couple of wins and some passages of play, but we know when you come here you can’t be sparkling for 90 minutes but you need to compete, and you need to bring quality, and I thought we did all that in abundance today.

View image in fullscreen Derek McInnes congratulates Ben Godfrey after the final whistle. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

“Strong performance, deserved win. I thought we were good in the game. I thought we looked like a team, a sense of the team that I would like us to be. I think the added bit of quality from Min-su at the top of the pitch was much needed. We’ve been looking for that for a while now, so it’s great that we managed to get him in. Any sort of win today was vitally important for obvious reasons. So the fact of the matter is we’ve won a tough away game, and deservedly so.”

The debutant Jardell Kanga scored a stoppage-time equaliser to earn Motherwell a 3-3 draw with St Mirren in a pulsating clash in Paisley. Goals from Tawanda Maswanhise, who also had a first-half penalty saved, and Regan Charles-Cook had the visitors in control in the early stages. Saints, though, recovered and scored three times before half-time through Paul Nsio, Declan John and Samuel Ramos to lead going into the closing stages. Motherwell had one final chance and the Swede Kanga, signed two days earlier from Finland’s Ilves, lashed a volley high into the net to snatch a point for his new side.

Hibernian secured a narrow but deserved victory over Dundee at Dens Park. Martin Boyle fired the visitors into the lead in the first half with Callum Wright doubling their advantage after the break. Dundee netted late on through Joe Westley but the Edinburgh side held on to take all three points, with the victory moving the capital club up to fifth as the hosts dropped down to fourth.

On Saturday, Camilo Durán, in his preferred position of centre-forward, scored both goals for Celtic in their 2-1 win over Falkirk. The Colombian hit two striker’s goals in the opening 29 minutes and set up several teammates for chances. Falkirk improved after the break and their ambition was rewarded by Colby Donovan’s own goal in the 72nd minute.

The win continued Celtic’s perfect start to the domestic season, but it was preceded by a display of frustration over the club’s inability to secure Champions League qualification after a four-goal aggregate lead was squandered in Thursday’s 5-1 defeat by Lask.

The Celtic ultras mocked the club board’s declaration that they aim to be “world class” in everything they do with banners listing the teams who have beaten Celtic in the Champions League qualifiers in the past 14 years, below one that read “‘world class’ embarrassment”.

However, fans got behind the team throughout the afternoon and one chant of “sack the board” emanating from the standing section did not take off around the rest of Celtic Park.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Fans hold up banners with the names of teams that have eliminated Celtic from Europe. Photograph: Stuart Wallace/Shutterstock

Hearts held firm at the end of a gruelling week to close out an unconvincing 2-1 home win over St Johnstone and climb to second in the table. Buoyed by their midweek Conference League playoff triumph away to Rapid Vienna Hearts were good value for their two-goal lead after James Wilson’s early strike was followed by a second that went down as an own goal from the Saints debutant Enes Alic.

But the hosts faded after the break and they were left clinging on in the closing stages after Ruari Paton pulled one back for the visitors early in the second half.

Dundee United produced a fine performance in the absence of their manager, Jim Goodwin, as they thrashed Kilmarnock 4-0 at Rugby Park. Goodwin was admitted to hospital on Thursday and the club said on Saturday morning the 44-year-old “continues to deal with an ongoing medical matter”.

His players, under the guidance of assistant Lee Sharp, did him proud as three first-half goals helped ease them to a first Premiership victory of the campaign. United, who had not scored in their previous three games in all competitions, were three up by 41 minutes thanks to Emmanuel Agyei’s opener, Zac Sapsford’s penalty and a Will Ferry beauty.

Jesse Randall added a late fourth as Killie conceded for the 13th time in three top-flight matches to remain bottom of the table without a point.

Sports.title: European football: Bellingham sparks Real Madrid’s cruise to maintain perfect start
Sports.content:
Real Madrid maintained their perfect start to the season in La Liga with a comfortable 4-0 home ⁠win over promoted Málaga on Sunday, scoring three times inside 30 minutes before adding a late fourth.

Jude Bellingham’s brilliant solo opener, an own ⁠goal by the Málaga goalkeeper ⁠Alfonso Herrero and ​a sharp Kylian Mbappé volley effectively settled the contest before half-time, with substitute Arda Guler wrapping up the victory in added time at ⁠the Bernabéu.

The win lifted Madrid to nine points from three matches, two clear of Atlético Madrid and Alavés. Barcelona, fourth on six points with a ⁠game in hand, host Rayo Vallecano on Monday.

Bellingham opened the scoring in the 19th minute ‌with a superb burst through the middle, collecting a loose ball near the edge of the area, gliding past three defenders and firing low beneath Herrero. They ​doubled their lead seven minutes later after Herrero could only palm out Mbappé’s effort. Bellingham headed the rebound back towards goal and, as Herrero and a teammate collided while trying to clear, the ball ended up in the net.

Mbappé then made it 3-0 in the 30th minute, meeting Trent Alexander-Arnold’s cross ⁠with a fine volley from the centre of the box. The second half drifted until Guler, shortly ​after coming on, started ‌and finished a ​slick move, feeding Vinícius Júnior before tapping in the Brazilian’s return pass to complete the rout.

Napoli suffered a 2-1 defeat at home to Como ⁠in Serie A, with all three goals coming in an entertaining opening half.

View image in fullscreen Tasos Douvikas scores Como’s second goal against Napoli. Photograph: Giuseppe Maffia/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

Assane Diao looked the most threatening player in the opening stages ⁠and the winger was instrumental in the visitors’ 17th-minute opening goal. Diao went past ​Mathías Olivera on the right wing ‌and played a pass ‌across to Martin Baturina whose shot on the turn from close to the penalty ‌spot found the bottom corner of the net.

Noa Lang missed an excellent chance to equalise, sending a header over from inside the six-yard box, before Napoli drew level on the half-hour mark. Rasmus Højlund collected a pass on the edge of the area, rolled the ball away from the defender Jacobo Ramón to make ‌room for the shot which he drilled low into the far corner, but Como were back in front four minutes later when Napoli ​were caught napping at the back.

André-Frank Zambo Anguissa underhit a pass back to Amir Rrahmani in his own box, allowing Baturina to nick the ball away. It fell to Tasos Douvikas and Como’s top scorer last season netted his second goal of this ⁠campaign.

Yuito Suzuki scored a hat-trick as Freiburg thumped Werder Bremen 4-1, while Schalke’s nightmare return to ⁠the Bundesliga ended in a 3-0 away defeat to Augsburg as they finished with 10 men.

View image in fullscreen Yuito Suzuki opens the scoring for Freiburg against Werder Bremen. Photograph: Thomas Kienzle/AFP/Getty Images

Schalke spent the last ⁠three seasons in ⁠the second tier ​and would have hoped for a positive result on their return, but were well beaten in a lively contest in which ⁠both sides created plenty of chances. Augsburg took the lead in the 18th minute as Michael Gregoritsch scored at the back post, the goal ⁠coming against the run of play.

The visitors’ task got harder when Ron Schallenberg received a ​straight red card in the 62nd minute ‌for a dangerous tackle ‌on Gregoritsch. The hosts doubled their advantage as Anton Kade provided a neat finish off ‌the post on 79 minutes, before Rodrigo Ribeiro scored the third in added time.

Suzuki was in superb form as Freiburg completed a rout of Werder Bremen to get their season off to the perfect start. He had never scored more than once in a Bundesliga game before but celebrated a hat-trick with some neat finishes.
