Sports.title: ‘I’ve had a very hectic career’: Mario Balotelli on Italian football’s troubles and his future
Sports.content:
Whenever the name Mario Balotelli is brought up, particularly in Italy, the conversation is almost inevitably laced with a sense of regret. There is that lingering “What if?”, a collective sigh over a player who possessed the raw, undeniable potential to be one of the best in the world, if only things had been different.

Yet being in front of him, with a smile on his face, it becomes clear the 36-year-old striker has reached an unexpected level of wisdom and maturity, traits that shine through in his lucid analysis of Italian football’s current struggles and the vanishing street culture of the sport. As Balotelli reflects on what he would tell his adolescent self, there is also a distinct feeling that he has finally made peace with his own turbulent narrative, that he isn’t chasing the ghosts of unfulfilled expectations.

Balotelli joined Al Ittifaq in the United Arab Emirates simply to enjoy the game, to find pure joy on the pitch, and to realise a long-held family dream of playing alongside his brother, Enock Barwuah. “To tell you the truth, it was an idea that came up more or less at the last minute,” he says. “The president wanted to meet me, and we talked. The project interested me. Everyone always says: ‘You go to Dubai for the money,’ but thank God, I’m not short of that. So, money wasn’t the only goal. The project was actually nice and competitive. I grew fond of the idea and decided to give it a try.”

View image in fullscreen Mario Balotelli signed for Al-Ittifaq in January 2026 on a two-and-a-half-year contract. Photograph: Al-Ittifaq

The realities of playing in the Middle East present a stark contrast to Balotelli’s past experiences. “Infrastructure-wise, it’s very good. The stadiums are beautiful. The problem is the public: there’s no crowd, which is a bit sad,” he says. “The organisation is also lacking a bit, but I think they’ll improve on that with time. I’m talking about all the teams across the board.” On linking up with his sibling, he says: “It’s beautiful. Ever since we were little, we always said we’d play together one day. He’d always ask me: ‘If you play for Inter, Milan, or [Manchester] City, how can I play with you?’ I used to tell him that when I got older, I might play in a team of a slightly lower level and maybe they’d give us that opportunity. It’s always been a dream, and now it’s coming true.”

Despite his new surroundings, Balotelli remains acutely aware of the deep-rooted problems plaguing football back home, particularly after Italy’s failure to qualify for three successive World Cups. “The problems, in my opinion, are very simple,” he says. “I prefer to give practical explanations rather than technical ones, based on everyday life and what I see in Italy.

“When we were little, we played hours and hours of football. I remember my mum getting mad at me because I’d stay out until it was too dark to see the ball. They’d threaten you that you couldn’t go out to play the next day. Now, when I walk around cities like Brescia, though I see it in other Italian cities too, the parks are empty. There’s no one around.”

Balotelli continues: “Computers, phones, and PlayStations have ruined a lot. Above all, the parents’ mentality has changed. A seven‑year-old kid today might play football for two hours every three days. We had the same structured training sessions, plus three hours of playing at the park every day, which felt like fun but was actually extra training. I truly believe talents were born on the street and in the parks. You played a lot, learned a lot, and tested yourself against older kids. If you were good, they didn’t let you play with kids your age; they made you play with the older ones. Those were tests that served me well in the long run. Playing with people older than me has always been one of the most important things in my career.

“Today, kids are on their phones. They feel like Ronaldinho because they watch his videos. I felt like Ronaldo because I could actually pull off the same tricks at the park. It’s very different.”

Despite his pessimism over the state of Italian football, Balotelli, who earned 36 caps for the Azzurri, scoring 14 goals, remains confident of a bright future. “Yes, I think so for the upcoming generations,” he predicts. “Maybe not right away, but in the next two or three generations. It’s normal for a country to have downturns but then you bounce back. Spain, France, and Germany have all had them.”

View image in fullscreen Mario Balotelli has won 36 caps for the Italian national team – the last in September 2018 – scoring 14 goals. Photograph: Luca Bruno/AP

When it comes to the national team, it’s impossible to ignore Roberto Mancini, reappointed as head coach and someone who acted as a mentor for Balotelli, as well as a defining figure throughout his most successful years. “He texted me to wish me a happy birthday, and I joked with him, saying: ‘Look, I can still play!’” Balotelli reveals. “I’m very happy he’s back with the national team; I’m very fond of him and I wish him the best. In Italy, people tend to blame the coaches a lot but, honestly, the system should take more of the blame. It’s the truth that nobody wants to say.”

As a curious footnote, the last time Balotelli played for Italy was on 7 September 2018, against Poland in Bologna. It also happened to be Mancini’s first competitive game in his first spell in charge of the national team. So, could Balotelli play for Italy under Mancini again? “If I keep scoring, yes,” he replies emphatically.

Balotelli’s time in England remains a standout chapter in a career filled with highs and lows, especially the three years he had at Manchester City when he won the Premier League and FA Cup – under Mancini. “It remains one of the best memories of my career,” he says. “At that time, City wasn’t as renowned as it is today. We joined the team that took the first steps for City to become what it is today. That gives you a special feeling. It means a lot more, actually.”

View image in fullscreen Mario Balotelli had an eventful three years at Manchester City, where he won the Premier League and FA Cup. Photograph: Matthew Peters/Manchester United/Getty Images

As he navigates the twilight of his career, Balotelli’s focus is clear. “I’m feeling good,” he states. “I’m recovering from a slight leg issue but I’m training, and it’s going well. It’s hot, which makes it a bit difficult to give 100%, but if you pace yourself and use your head, you can manage to play quite well. The heat is definitely a drawback, however.

“On the pitch I want to play as long as I feel good. Playing is what I love doing, so as long as my body doesn’t say: ‘Enough,’ I’ll keep going. Off the pitch, once I finish my career, I definitely want to manage my businesses and focus on my kids. I’d prefer tranquillity, though. I’ve had a very hectic career, so a sedentary lifestyle wouldn’t be a bad thing.”

If Balotelli could offer one piece of advice to his 16-year-old self, what would it be? “I’d tell him not to make certain choices,” he says, “and to listen to certain people at specific times.”

Sports.title: Lionel Messi’s ‘footballing beauty’ hailed as Miami crush Montreal; MLS roundup
Sports.content:
Inter Miami interim coach Guillermo Hoyos ran out of superlatives for Lionel Messi after the ⁠Argentine playmaker scored four goals in a Major League Soccer match for the first time in his career to ⁠inspire a 7-1 thrashing ⁠of CF ​Montreal on Saturday.

Messi’s four-goal haul and an assist came at a crucial time for Miami, helping them snap a ⁠five-game winless run across all competitions.

The 39-year-old restored Miami’s advantage shortly before half-time, struck again in the 52nd minute, completed his ⁠hat-trick in the 83rd and capped his dazzling display with a free kick ​in stoppage time.

The former Barcelona forward ‌now tops the ‌MLS scoring charts with 18 goals this season.

“There are no words to describe ‌such footballing beauty,” Argentine Hoyos said. “So much is going on that words simply fall short.

“He is constantly looking for that goal, that play, that pass; I don’t think he’s an ordinary footballer. Analyzing him, both as a player and as a person, goes so deep that you run out of ‌words.”

Messi, who won the 2022 World Cup, also captained Argentina to this year’s World Cup final, where they lost to Spain.

“That’s ​what it means to have Messi on the team,” Miami midfielder Casemiro told Apple TV. “We have to enjoy these moments because he is a person, a player that makes history.”

Casemiro, 34, joined Miami in July after his contract expired at Manchester ⁠United. The Brazilian and Messi spent years on opposite sides of ​one of football’s fiercest ​rivalries, with Casemiro starring for ​Real Madrid and Messi for Barcelona, but are now teammates.

“We saw ​today that we ‌have to enjoy ​it, keep ​supporting and keep competing with him because he continues to be the best,” Casemiro added.

Joveljić scores twice on Sounders debut in 2-2 draw

View image in fullscreen Dejan Joveljic was traded from Sporting KC to Seattle this week. Photograph: Kevin Ng/Getty Images

Dejan Joveljic tallied twice in his Seattle Sounders debut in a 2-2 draw with the visiting Chicago Fire on Saturday ⁠afternoon.

Maren Haile-Selassie and Robert Lewandowski each had a goal and an assist for Chicago, who extended their MLS unbeaten run to ⁠five matches.

The Sounders have earned ​two straight draws after an eight- match losing streak in MLS matches.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Joveljic, acquired Tuesday from Sporting Kansas City in a $6m deal, opened the scoring in the 12th minute. Following a throw-in on the left side of the field, the Sounders switched and moved the ball down the right wing, with Kalani ‌Kossa-Rienzi sending a pass to Sebastian Gomez deep in the corner. Gomez’s low cross found Joveljic just outside the top of the 6-yard box ​and his one-timer skirted through the legs of Elliott and turned goalie Chris Brady into a pretzel as he crumpled to the turf.

The Fire tied it at 1-all in the 38th minute. Lewandowski took a pass from Andrew Gutman at the top left of the penalty area and fed ⁠Haile-Selassie, whose 17-yard shot from just left of center found the lower ​far corner of the net.

Joveljic scored ​again in the 48th minute. ​He took a pass from Rusnak just outside the top of the 18-yard ​box and lofted ‌a shot that ​Brady got his fingertips ​on but the ball went off the underside of the crossbar and into the net. Snyder Brunell was credited with a secondary assist.

Teenager Cavan Sullivan continues electric form in Philadelphia Union win

View image in fullscreen Cavan Sullivan scored again in Philadelphia’s win over New York Red Bulls. Photograph: Ron Smits/SOPA Images/Shutterstock

Cavan Sullivan scored in the second half to become the first 16-year-old in MLS history with goal contributions in four straight matches, and the Philadelphia Union beat the New York Red Bulls 3-1 on Saturday night to extend their unbeaten streak to seven.

Sullivan found the net for a second straight match and third time this season in 34 career appearances to give Philadelphia a 2-0 lead in the 50th minute. He is the third player in league history age 18 or younger with a scoring contribution in four straight matches.

The Union took the lead in the 21st minute on Milan Iloski’s career-high 11th goal. Indiana Vassilev and Danley Jean Jacques both picked up their first two assists of the season on the first two goals.

Teenager Neil Pierre scored in the 65th minute for a 3-0 advantage. It was the fourth goal in seven appearances for the 18-year-old rookie midfielder. Bruno Damiani and Iloski had assists.

The Red Bulls avoided a shutout in the 74th minute when Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting netted his third goal of the season after scoring 17 times last year.

Andre Blake saved three shots for Philadelphia, which posted a 3-0-2 record in August.

Ethan Horvath had one save for New York (7-10-5), which has gone 0-3-1 since a 3-2 victory over Orlando City to begin the month.

Minnesota scores three times in four minutes, but Orlando City gets last laugh in 3-3 draw

View image in fullscreen Antoine Griezmann assisted on Tyrese Spicer’s late equalizer. Photograph: Michael Turner/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock

Tyrese Spicer scored three minutes into second-half stoppage time and Orlando City salvaged a 3-3 draw with Minnesota United after blowing a two-goal lead on Saturday night.

Spicer used assists from newcomer Antoine Griezmann and Iván Angulo to score his career-high sixth goal for the equalizer.

Daryl Dike scored in the 28th minute to give Orlando City a 1-0 lead that stood through halftime. Dike’s first goal this season came in his first start and fourth appearance.

Griezmann took a pass from Justin Ellis in the 64th minute and scored his fourth goal in his seventh MLS appearance for a 2-0 advantage.

Minnesota United’s goals came in a four-minute flurry in the second half. The Loons got on the scoreboard in the 71st minute when Kelvin Yeboah and Kyle Duncan set up Marcus Caldeira for his second goal in his fifth appearance in the league. Defender Anthony Markanich scored his sixth goal three minutes later — with an assist from Joaquín Pereyra — to tie it 2-2. Yeboah found the net for the 11th time just one minute after Markanich scored to give Minnesota United a 3-2 lead.

Sports.title: Ruthless England's emphatic victory over Pakistan was a job well done after build-up dogged by more tales of drunken antics but there is still much work to do, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
It has taken them 630 days, but England were finally able to celebrate a series victory shortly after 5.45pm on the fourth evening of this second Test when Josh Tongue induced a thick edge from Mohammad Ali, and Harry Brook swallowed a sharp chance at second slip.

If celebrations were muted, it wasn’t simply because England might have forgotten how they work. Pakistan have provided as much resistance as a soggy napkin, and there is work ahead. Nothing less than a 3–0 whitewash at Edgbaston will suffice, at which point a testing winter trip to South Africa looms into view.

But victory by 194 runs, after being inserted under sepulchral skies on what has become English cricket’s least predictable surface, was a job well done by a team who had begun the game fending off yet more questions about drink. They were as ruthless as they were professional, and it hasn’t been often in the last year we have been able to say that.

In pursuit of a purely notional 389, Pakistan were dismissed for 194, their fourth sub-200 total in succession – and wouldn’t have got even as many as that but for a fighting 97 from Saud Shakeel that put some of his colleagues to shame.

England’s efforts were led once more by Ollie Robinson, who is enjoying a comeback summer like no other, and added four wickets to the four he collected on the second day. Match figures of 27–11–35–8 bore testimony to his metronomic menace, the kind on which the great Australian Glenn McGrath built a long career.

And they took his Test record to 99 wickets at an average of 19.53. The last England bowler to claim more wickets at a better average is the legendary SF Barnes, who won his last cap before the outbreak of the First World War.

England were ruthless in a crushing 194-win victory over Pakistan in the second Test at Lord's

For all the off-field nonsense that has dogged him ever since his debut five years ago, Robinson is building a CV that would be the envy of many. Making expert use of the wobble-seam delivery, and on surfaces that accentuate his skills, he has been all but unplayable.

Robinson it was who triggered the carnage in the fifth over, nipping one back into the left-handed opener Azan Awais, then bowling the right-handed Abdullah Shafique with a beauty that pitched on off stump and straightened.

Later, with England held up by a fourth-wicket stand of 97, he overturned an lbw decision to get rid of Shan Masood for 26, before removing Mohammad Rizwan in his next over when Pakistan’s wicketkeeper missed a sickening heave. Of Robinson’s 16 wickets in this series at 7.18 each, eight have been leg-before – a stump-to-stump threat, if ever there was one.

Throw in the Lord’s Test against New Zealand, and his summer’s work amounts to 23 wickets at 8.34. The only pity is that England – the version led by Brendon McCullum and Ben Stokes, at least – felt unable to trust him against the New Zealanders on a flat Trent Bridge pitch in punishing temperatures.

Yet he has become the glue of this attack, and the perfect foil to his three quicker colleagues, each of whom topped 90mph on the fourth day. Even factoring in Jofra Archer’s modest assertion on Friday evening that the Lord’s speed gun was faulty, there was no doubting the collective menace.

No vignette captured that better than the brute with which Archer removed Babar Azam, a 91mph bouncer that allowed Pakistan’s captain no time to think, much less to get himself into position for the pull. The ball looped off the bat’s top edge via his helmet and landed gently in the hands of Jordan Cox in the cordon. At 14 for three, there was no way back.

Shakeel fought hard, batting throughout the afternoon session, and later pulling Josh Tongue for six, six and four in five balls to move to 96, only to fall in Tongue’s next over when another pull shot was intercepted at deep backward square by Harry Brook.

Had Shakeel connected only slightly better, he would have become the second Pakistani of the day to etch himself on to the honours boards, after the relentless Mohammad Abbas ended a run of three successive Lord’s four-fors by completing figures five for 57 in the first 40 minutes of the morning.

Instead, Shakeel – utterly crestfallen – had to settle for a standing ovation. And with opener Imam-ul-Haq still unable to bat because of a calf strain, it was left to Tongue to mop up the tail and condemn Pakistan to their 10th defeat in 11 away from home.

Joe Root will be pleased with his side but knows there are much tougher challenges ahead

ROOT CHALLENGES QUICKS Joe Root called on England’s fast-bowling quartet to ‘write their own chapter in history’ after his side blew away Pakistan at Lord’s to clinch their first Test series victory in 20 months. Ollie Robinson led the way with four for 24 – and eight for 35 in the match – as England won the second Test by 194 runs to take an unassailable 2–0 lead to Edgbaston next week. And the result left Root purring about his four quicks, with the accuracy of Robinson complemented by the outright pace of Jofra Archer, Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson. ‘These guys have got the opportunity to create their own legacy,’ he said. ‘They’re all of an age where they can play together for a long period of time, and they’ve all got skillsets that travel around the world in different conditions. ‘If they keep working hard and performing in the manner they are currently, then there’s no reason why they can’t write their own little chapter in English fast-bowling history.’ Root also urged his team to celebrate in moderation after a string of unwelcome drink-related headlines. ‘It’s hard to win Test matches,’ he said. ‘So enjoy it and celebrate it, but in a sensible, grown-up way.’ Lawrence Booth

Only Atkinson, relegated to second change, failed to take a wicket, though he will bowl worse than this for better reward.

Excitement at the pace quartet has to be tempered by two factors. The pitch offered lavish assistance throughout, and remains a concern for MCC bosses, even as they do their best to seek solutions. And the Pakistan batting, Shakeel aside, was miserable.

But there is a tendency to hammer England when they struggle, and to explain their successes by diminishing their opponents. The evidence of the first two Tests is that Joe Root’s four-pronged seam attack are expertly exploiting helpful conditions against a team with little facility to resist them.

England have been excellent, Pakistan poor. Two things can be true at once. And one truth was undeniable: after all the sideshows, England have a winning Test team again.

Sports.title: Revealed: The rules loophole that led to Man United's second goal being given despite Harry Maguire handling the ball
Sports.content:
Harry Maguire's 'goal' against Ipswich Town at Old Trafford on Sunday left fans across the nation scratching their heads.

How could a goal, where the player seemingly handled the ball before shooting, stand?

Manchester United were left counting their lucky stars after an obscure rule allowed this, their second goal in a 5-2 mauling of Ipswich.

Despite the controversy, the goal was valid because, well, Maguire didn't actually score it.

The defender's original shot was slightly off target, but it deflected in after hitting Ipswich man Jacob Greaves, so it went down as an own goal.

Many felt Harry Maguire got lucky as Manchester United's second goal against Ipswich was allowed to stand after he handled the ball

Despite him seeming to handle the ball, because his shot wasoff target and it went in as an own goal, it stood

Had Maguire hit the target, the goal would have counted as his and been chalked off. But because he originally missed, it stands.

As the video assistant referee Jarred Gillett said to referee Craig Pawson during the match: 'It's an own goal and the accidental handball is not punishable, so we recommend you award the goal.'

The goal may have been disallowed had the officials felt that Maguire's handball was deliberate.

'It wasn't handball on purpose, that's for sure!' Maguire told Sky Sports. 'I don't know if it brushed my fingers. I actually dragged the shot a little bit wide so it's going to go down as an own goal!'

Opposition manager Gary O'Neil was gracious in defeat.

He told the BBC: 'It's a really tough rule to ref.

'Maguire's shot was missing by quite a way. But what if it's heading somewhere near the post and it's too close to tell?

'It doesn't feel like a goal. It feels like it should be chalked off but we accept that it isn't and that's the rule. We have to be ready for Liverpool on Friday.'

Ipswich boss Gary O'Neil said it 'doesn't feel like a goal' but admitted it was a tough rule for referees to apply

Pundit Darren Bent added to Sky Sports: 'It's one of those rules where I understand because it's there in black and white, but it still doesn't feel right.

'Harry Maguire directly impacts what happens to the ball and it ends up in the back of the net at a crucial time for Ipswich.

'If it hits your hand and he is the one that directly impacts it, it's not a nice one to take.'

Sports.title: Why Michael Carrick should be concerned despite Man United's thrilling comeback win over Ipswich as Bruno Fernandes comes to the rescue again, writes CHRIS WHEELER
Sports.content:
Why Michael Carrick should be concerned despite Man United's thrilling comeback win over Ipswich as Bruno Fernandes comes to the rescue again, writes CHRIS WHEELER

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

By the time the heavens opened over Old Trafford, the lightning flashed, the thunder rumbled overhead and the roof sprang another leak, the proverbial storm clouds gathering over Manchester United had long since passed.

But for 10 minutes before half-time, United were facing the unthinkable scenario of losing their opening two games of the season to newly-promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town.

The visitors from East Anglia led through a Leif Davis goal and were threatening to plunge Michael Carrick and his team into crisis before August is out and the transfer window has closed by winning here for the first time since 1984.

United deserve credit for responding to adversity so emphatically in a quite barnstorming game of football. They got a couple of lucky breaks, not least when Marcelino Nunez’s slip led to the equaliser and the second goal was allowed to stand after Harry Maguire wasn’t penalised for handball. Who thinks up these rules?

Having been given a nudge in the right direction, United took full advantage with a second-half onslaught that was as relentless as the deluge that battered this old place. Carrick wants his team to play on the front foot, and a total of 33 shots – their most in a decade – suggests he is on the right track, whatever concerns exist over his defence.

Once again, United were mightily grateful to their inspirational captain Bruno Fernandes for dragging them out of the mire. Fernandes scored a hat-trick – the third of his Old Trafford career – and got a first assist of the season after making a Premier League record 21 of them last term.

Not for the first time, it was captain Bruno Fernandes who rescued his team with a standout performance that ended with him claiming a hat-trick and another assist

Harry Maguire was allowed to get away with a handball in the build-up to the second goal

The scoreline certainly felt a little harsh on Ipswich given how they competed in the first half, but Gary O'Neil's men were simply swept away after half-time

At the end of a week in which he received the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award in recognition of his feat, Fernandes provided yet more evidence of his enduring importance to this team.

There hasn’t been quite the same level of speculation over his future as a year ago, but with 10 months left on a contract that includes an option for United to extend it by another year until June 2028, it still feels as though he is the one player that United simply can’t do without.

On the day Carlos Baleba was paraded on the pitch before kick-off, and other midfield signings Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos made their home debuts, here was Fernandes stealing the show again.

There were other big plusses for Carrick. Kobbie Mainoo was selected ahead of Santos and showed how important he will be if the £155million midfield rebuild is to be a success.

Marcus Rashford made his first United start for 626 days and showed the raw enthusiasm that turned him into a local hero before it all went wrong and he drifted away to Aston Villa and Barcelona on loan. We wondered how Old Trafford would react to his return, but there was genuine warmth from the stands.

There are still cracks that this win won’t paper over, in particular the issue at left-back which has lingered all summer and shows no signs of going away with two days to go until the window closes.

Luke Shaw was exposed at Hull and it took Ipswich less than half an hour to do the same. Shaw was left for dead by Abdul Fatawu who got away down the right and crossed to Davis who had had been left unmarked by Bryan Mbeumo and met it with a first-time effort.

Senne Lammens had already bailed United out with vital saves from Julio Enciso and Daizen Maeda, but he couldn’t prevent the ball going in off the underside of the bar.

Shaw looked vulnerable in the defeat at Hull, and he was left for dead in the build up to the Tractor Boys' opener

New £70million signing Carlos Baleba was paraded on the pitch before kick-off but might not make his debut until mid-October due to an ankle injury

Having failed to sign a left-back so far, surely United have to do so before Tuesday's deadline.

They were presented with a rather fortunate opportunity to level the scores in the 40th minute when Nunez slipped as he controlled a pass close to halfway, and Matheus Cunha guided an excellent early pass beyond Sasa Lukic and into the path of Fernandes.

Did United’s captain have the legs to get away from his opponent? Probably not so he took one touch and then lashed the ball past Kjell Scherpen.

After Mbeumo somehow hit the bar from point-black range early in the second half, United transformed the game with two goals in the space of five minutes.

The first felt very harsh on Ipswich after Maguire challenged Chuba Akpom just outside the penalty area and clearly used his hands to control the ball. The United defender advanced into the box and fired a low shot which was going wide until it hit Jacob Greaves, which not only diverted the ball past Scherpen but also negated the handball because it was an own-goal.

Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil accepted the ‘strange rule’ with good grace, but summed up the sense of injustice around it. ‘Sometimes you see a goal and think it shouldn’t stand, and that felt like one of them,’ said O’Neil, who also had the misfortune of losing record signing Emersonn to a knee injury at half-time.

It got worse for Greaves when he tripped Cunha as he raced onto Mainoo’s excellent throughball and Fernandes scored from the spot.

Then after Mainoo and Mbeumo both had efforts blocked, the ball ran kindly for the Portugal star to slot home for his hat-trick.

As the storm raged overhead, Fernandes sent Mbeumo through to lob Scherpen for the fifth, before Enciso picked Lisandro Martinez’s pocket and squared for Akpom to score.

It mattered not, but was another reminder that United still have work to do despite the scoreline.

Sports.title: Man United 5-2 Ipswich PLAYER RATINGS: Which star was badly exposed despite victory? Who put in a 'gem' of a performance? And how did Marcus Rashford fare on return to starting XI?
Sports.content:
Man United 5-2 Ipswich PLAYER RATINGS: Which star was badly exposed despite victory? Who put in a 'gem' of a performance? And how did Marcus Rashford fare on return to starting XI?

Manchester United sent an emphatic response to their critics with a 5-2 demolition job of Ipswich Town in the pouring rain.

Michael Carrick cut a concerned figure in his technical area when Leif Davis fired the newly-promoted side into the lead at the Stretford End.

But, with a the help of Bruno Fernandes’ hat-trick, United have got their season up and running, and still had time to put the gloss on it with a lovely chip from Bryan Mbeumo.

Daily Mail Sport's NATHAN SALT was in position at a soaked Old Trafford to run the rule over both sets of players...

Manchester United hit Ipswich Town for five as Bruno Fernandes settled a seven-goal thriller

MAN UNITED (4-2-3-1)

Senne Lammens - 7.5

Week by week you just cannot understate just how important Senne Lammens is to Manchester United. He was let down by his team-mates at Hull and had to bail out more mistakes ahead of him here when he denied Julio Enciso one-v-one with his left knee, and then denied Daizen Maeda full stretch to his left after he was set clear by Davis. Looks an even greater transfer market steal with every game.

Diogo Dalot - 6

Drew a fine save out of Ipswich goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen 13 minutes in on his left foot after a brilliant cut-back on the edge of the box. But Ipswich got in far too many times down his side. Makes a lot of good runs in attacking areas but needs to shore up the right side with tougher games ahead.

Harry Maguire - 7

His experience and composure under pressure really goes a long way to helping United navigate storms that continually seem to come their way. United were rocked by Ipswich’s opener and an unruffled Maguire was key to turning it around. He helped shift the momentum with a low strike that went in via Jacob Greaves’ right heel and made some crucial defensive headers when Ipswich looked to counter. Well worth the new deal he inked in the summer.

Lisandro Martinez - 6

Had a lot of the ball as he came into the starting line-up in place of Ayden Heaven and did his best to try and split the lines as he so often does here. Shook his head when a lapse in concentration saw him robbed of possession in stoppage time as Ipswich added a late consolation. Felt like a night where he was just getting some rhythm back and will only get better as the games go on.

Luke Shaw - 5.5

An afternoon which badly exposed Luke Shaw’s lack of pace and exactly why United have spent all summer scouring the left back market. He was bailed out by Lammens first time when Enciso went past him but didn’t get the same fortune when Abdul Fatawu breezed beyond to tee up Davis for the opening goal. His body cannot compete with the league’s fastest wingers - but he’s being hung out to dry this season if they don’t get another left back.

Luke Shaw (left) got exposed multiple times for a lack of pace and United need another option

Youri Tielemans - 6

A lovely footballer who showed glimpses here that he can pass through the eye of a needle. But the frenetic first half highlighted that to get the very best version of Tielemans, Carrick and his staff need to put legs and runners around him, just as Aston Villa did, so as not to expose his lack of pace. Play to his strengths, don’t make him cover acres of space and thus highlight his weaknesses.

Kobbie Mainoo - 8

A gem of a performance. This was the type of front-footed, physical performance that had fans screaming all sorts of obscenities at former head coach Ruben Amorim for not picking Mainoo, and why so many fans were perplexed he didn’t kick a ball at the World Cup. After United were so poor at Hull, Mainoo showed why he simply has to be in a first-choice XI moving forward.

Bryan Mbeumo - 6

Capped the rain-soaked day off with a brilliant goal, chipping 6ft9’ Scherpen and deserves credit for that. But he should still expect some unimpressed glances from team-mates when this game is reviewed. Gave up on his defensive responsibility to allow Davis to be unmarked to score his first Premier League goal since November 2024. Didn’t track Davis again for another, but got away with it. Was left aghast when he missed from two yards out as Marcus Rashford’s cross was kneed up onto the crossbar. Has moments of quality - as he showed with the goal - but cannot neglect the basics. Booked.

Bruno Fernandes - 9.5

Laughable really that the fact he won last season’s PFA Players’ Player of the Year was even a discussion point and here was another example of just how brilliant he is. His first was empathic on the breakaway. His second came from the penalty spot and the third he ghosted in to convert a blocked Mbeumo shot. He even had time to produce a stunning clipped cross over the top which Mbeumo converted to finish with three goals and an assist. Where would Manchester United be without their Portuguese genius?

Fernandes is unquestionably the Premier League's best player and he showed it again here

Marcus Rashford - 7

Starting for Manchester United for the first time in 626 days, he’d have been forgiven for having some reservations about the reception he’d get back at Old Trafford. He need not have worried. Rashford worked hard at both ends and deserved a goal for his contribution down the left. An enormous upgrade on Patrick Dorgu’s display at Hull.

Matheus Cunha - 7.5

Constantly busy and never wants to give players a moment’s rest, which is what United need. Not sure he’s best suited to playing through the middle but he works hard and his expertly played pass through for Fernandes after Nunez’s costly slip in the United half was one of the plays of the game.

MANAGER: Michael Carrick - 8

Had to face a barrage of criticism after the abject. Nature of the defeat at Hull City and this would have felt particularly sweet on the back of it. Was vindicated with his changes as Dalot, Rashford, Mainoo and Martinez all improved a United side that went for the jugular here.

Ipswich (4-2-3-1)

Scherpen 6.5; O’Shea 4, Diop 5, Greaves 3, Davis 7; Núñez 5 (Palacios 65, 6), Lukić 5 (Ouattara 73); Fatawu 7 (McAteer 83), Enciso 6.5, Maeda 6 (Furlong 73); Emersonn 5 (Akpom 46, 6.5)

Goals: Davis (29), Akpom (90+1)

Booked: Lukic, Fatawu, Greaves

Manager: Gary O’Neil 6

Sports.title: Jed York's prostitute sting shame laid bare: Billionaire family's stunning response as cruel whispers spread among locals about the scandalized San Francisco 49ers' boss
Sports.content:
Jed York's prostitute sting shame laid bare: Billionaire family's stunning response as cruel whispers spread among locals about the scandalized San Francisco 49ers' boss

The parents of disgraced San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York have insisted their son's humiliating prostitution sting arrest has now been 'resolved' - but it hasn't done anything to quell the scathing gossip spreading like wildfire among locals, the Daily Mail can reveal.

York's father, John York, was dismissive of the scandal that has rocked the billionaire family ever since police arrested Jed at a trailer park in Ohio over the weekend for allegedly trying to hire a prostitute.

Days later, the NFL bigwig secured a plea deal that ultimately saw a prostitution charge dropped - allowing him to plead no contest to misdemeanor charges of disorderly conduct and possessing a criminal tool.

'That’s been resolved,' the elder York, 77, told the Daily Mail this week after being approached at the headquarters of the family's DeBartolo Corporation in Youngstown, Ohio.

Jed’s mom, Denise DeBartolo, 75, also ducked just moments later when she stopped by the offices.

Their 46-year-old son, meanwhile, remained out of sight with the windows to his house just around the corner shuttered.

An armed security guard parked in the driveway, who was hired from the Columbiana County Sheriff’s Office, shooed visitors away.

But in a community that reveres the billionaire family behind one of the greatest franchises in NFL history, the scandalous episode remains an epic subject.

San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York, 46, was arrested at a mobile home park in East Palestine, Ohio last weekend after cops said he was attempting to pay $140 for sex with a woman he believed to be a prostitute. That charge was later dropped in a plea deal

York's father, John York, 77, was dismissive of the scandal that has rocked the billionaire family, telling the Daily Mail that his son's arrest had been 'resolved'

When the Daily Mail approached at the family's DeBartolo Corporation in Youngstown, Ohio, on Tuesday, York's mom, Denise DeBartolo, 75, declined to speak to the reporter

As Jed York and his family hunkered down in Youngstown, a half mile away, locals at a shopping mall built by the DeBartolo family scratched their heads and mocked the DeBartolo scion.

At the center of the mockery is not just the allegations he tried to nab a prostitute - but also the circumstances that led to his bust.

York had allegedly responded to an online , rented a car and drove to Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community last Sunday morning to meet up with a $140-an-hour ‘prostitute’ who turned out to be an undercover detective, according to a police report.

He was arrested at the trailer park in East Palestine, which was the site of the disastrous 2023 freight train derailment, roughly 15 miles away from Youngstown.

‘What is it with East Palestine?’ 72-year-old Diane quipped as she sipped tea with elderly friends at the Southern Park Mall. ‘First we had the train wreck, and now this.’

‘He’s male - what else do you need to know?’ she continued.

But as Diane and her circle of friends’ laughter echoed through the food court, she dialed it back a bit given her respect for York’s family.

'I will say for that family - they’ve done a lot of good. Everything you see here.’

A giant mural in the entryway pays homage to the DeBartolo family, which built the mall and has owned the San Francisco 49ers now for nearly half a century.

In the wake of the sting at the Wheat Hill Home Community (pictured above), York was initially charged with engaging in prostitution but prosecutors later amended that to disorderly conduct

Jed York and his family have been hunkering down at their sprawling home in Youngstown in the wake of the saga. Locals, meanwhile, have been gossping about the scandalous episode

An armed security guard, who was hired from the Columbiana County Sheriff’s Office, was spotted parked in the driveway of the family's home and shoed visitors away

The mural traces the roots of the family from 1977 through 2020, when the ‘49ers increased their ownership in Leeds United soccer club to 37%.’ It ends with the all-caps declaration ‘MORE GREAT THINGS TO COME.’

‘LEGACY: The DeBartolo Commons at Southern Park,’ another sign reads, marking a 4-acre sports complex just outside.

The family is so revered and influential around town that nobody inside would allow their last names to be used for this article. Several had gone to high school locally with members of the DeBartolo family.

But given the relative anonymity, residents didn’t bite their tongues.

‘Guess he thought nobody would recognize him,' said 32-year-old Sue, who was eating a sandwich with her boyfriend John.

‘I saw it on TikTok,’ John explained. ‘It’s on brand for the area, not the person. So nasty. They should just fire him.’

Sandra, 70, and her boyfriend Jim, 77, seemed equally unforgiving.

’The fact he’s getting divorced is not an excuse,’ Sandra told the Daily Mail. ‘He should know better. He’s got to be more careful.'

‘He comes from a good family,’ she continued. ‘It’s shameful that he’s bringing disgrace to his family including himself.’

York had allegedly responded to an online , rented a car and drove to Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community on Sunday morning to meet up with a $140-an-hour ‘prostitute’ who turned out to be an undercover detective, a police report stated

York has spent most of the summer in Ohio where he grew up near Youngstown. The NFL issued a statement in the wake of his arrest saying the league will review he ordeal under the personal conduct policy

He pleaded no contest to misdemeanor disorderly conduct and possession of criminal tools on Monday - resulting in a one-day jail sentence with credit for time already served. The tool referred to in the charges was his cell phone

York, who has two sons with his wife Danielle, filed for divorce in May, citing irreconcilable differences.

‘Maybe he’s sad because of the dissolution of his marriage,’ Jim, whose late wife went to high school with Denise DeBartolo, reasoned.

Sandra wasn’t having it.

’This is his grandpa right here!’ she exclaimed, pointing to a portrait on the wall of Edward J. DeBartolo Sr.

At another table of a dozen senior citizens, Glyn, 77, decried, ’It’s a shame.'

'He’s rich and can afford whatever he wants,’ she said. 'He doesn’t have anything better to do?’

Her friend Bonnie, 80, sniped at York’s plea deal in the wake of the sting.

York was initially busted on a charge of engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors later dropped that charge and amended that to disorderly conduct.

He pleaded no contest to misdemeanor disorderly conduct and possession of criminal tools in relation to his cell phone on Monday - resulting in a one-day jail sentence with credit for time already served.

York, who has two sons with his wife Danielle, filed for divorce in May, citing irreconcilable differences

’The big thing that ticks me off is that they lowered the bar from the prostitution charge,’ Bonnie told the Daily Mail.

'If it was anybody else, I think that charge would stick.

‘Honestly, I still can’t understand - why would he go to a trailer park in East Palestine?’ she continued, while shaking her head.

'At least take her to a hotel room.'

Sports.title: Tottenham agree £60m deal for Everton star Iliman Ndiaye - with Richarlison in line for £35m return to the Toffees
Sports.content:
Tottenham agree £60m deal for Everton star Iliman Ndiaye - with Richarlison in line for £35m return to the Toffees

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tottenham have a deal in place with Everton forward Iliman Ndiaye and have proposed Richarlison to go the other way.

Tottenham are set to pay £60m for Iliman Ndiaye and Everton will pay £35m for Richarlison.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport last week, Tottenham opened discussions last week when it became apparent that Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo would opt to join Manchester City should the Anfield club agree to sell.

Ndiaye has turned down multiple contract offers in the last 12 months.

Man City have also been looking at a deal for Ndiaye. Everton are looking into a return deal for Man City winger Jack Grealish.

Everton have also made a £9million offer to Fulham for right back Kenny Tete.

Tottenham have a deal in place to sign Everton forward Iliman Ndiaye

Spurs have proposed Richarlison to go the other way and complete a return to Everton

Ndiaye has scored 17 goals and provided four assists in 74 appearances for Everton, since joining in a £15m move from Marseille in 2024.

Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi had been appointed as Marseille's head coach just days before Ndiaye was sold, with the winger never playing a match under the Italian.

Ndiaye, who has 44 caps for Senegal, had previously been an integral to Sheffield United's Championship promotion season in 2023.

De Zerbi revealed following Tottenham's 2-0 loss to Newcastle on Saturday that Richarlison was one of three players to have asked to leave the club.

'Richarlison he said too many times that he wanted to leave,' De Zerbi said.

'[Kevin] Danso came to me two days ago and said he wanted to leave. [Pape Matar] Sarr the same but he also suffered a small injury but he is almost ready to train.'

Richarlison has scored 32 goals in 134 matches for Tottenham since signing from Everton in a £60m deal.

The Brazilian previously scored 53 goals in 152 games for Everton.

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez LEFT OUT of Chelsea squad to face Brighton: Wantaway star dropped by Xabi Alonso for second-straight match - as Blues boss insists he is doing what's 'best for the club' amid Man City's £100m interest
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernandez was omitted from Chelsea's matchday squad for the second time in just four days, as speculation over his future at Stamford Bridge intensifies amid Manchester City's interest with transfer deadline day looming.

The 25-year-old is wanted by City before the transfer window closes on September 1 - with the Etihad outfit preparing a £100million bid, as reported by Daily Mail Sport. Even if that offer does come it is set to be rejected, with Chelsea wanting £120m.

And with Fernandez's future remaining uncertain, Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso opted not to include the midfielder for Sunday's Premier League 4-3 win at home to Brighton and Hove Albion.

Asked pre-match about his decision to not include the Argentina international, the Spaniard told Sky Sports: 'We think what is best for the team and the club. Sometimes we need to make tough calls; we don't know what will happen in the future.

'But today it was better that we have this squad, and in the future we don't know what is going to happen.'

Fernandez's exclusion comes days after he was dealt the same fate during Thursday's League Cup second-round 2-0 win over Luton Town.

Enzo Fernandez was left out of Chelsea's matchday squad for a second-straight match - with Premier League rivals Manchester City keen to sign him in a £100million transfer

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso says the midfielder's omission is what is 'best for the club' currently

In the build-up to that tie, which Chelsea won courtesy of Danny Welbeck and a Hakeem Odoffin own goal, Alonso insisted that Fernandez would be involved against their League One opponents.

However, when the team news came out on Thursday evening, Fernandez's name was nowhere to be seen in the 20-man squad.

Asked about Fernandez's absence from the squad against Luton, Alonso said pre-match: 'We assessed situations, individual and collective and we have decided he is not in the squad for today.'

However, speaking post-match the Spaniard was a lot more open, revealing that the decision was made by himself and the club hierarchy.

'It was a decision from myself and from the club,' Alonso said. 'We had other players that needed minutes and it was that way. It's a decision that I took. He's a good professional. He's training well. I have nothing to say about him.

'It was just a decision that we had to take, thinking about the game that we're playing tonight and we'll see for (Brighton on) Sunday.'

Speaking on Wednesday, Alonso was adamant to see his No 8 involved, saying: 'Yes, so we expect that he's involved.

'He's trained, he's training really well, he's a good professional and he will be involved.'

When pressed on whether he wants Fernandez to remain a Chelsea player after this window, Alonso added: 'We want to have the best team possible. We know his qualities. He has shown it. We have to wait, but we will think about tomorrow and let's see how things develop.

'We assess the whole squad as a unit and in that squad, we want good balance in terms of quality, in terms of positions, in terms of personalities, so we are aware of everything and we are prepared for whatever.'

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan

Play-off Path A:

Semi-final: Italy vs Northern Ireland

Semi-final: Wales vs Bosnia and Herzegovina

Final: Wales/Bosnia and Herzegovina vs Italy/Northern Ireland - Tuesday, 7.45pm kick-off

Play-off Path B:

Semi-final: Ukraine vs Sweden

Semi-final: Poland vs Albania

Final: Ukraine/Sweden vs Poland/Albania

Play-off Path C:

Semi-final: Turkey vs Romania

Semi-final: Slovakia vs Kosovo

Final: Slovakia/Kosovo vs Turkey/Romania

Play-off Path D:

Semi-final: Denmark vs North Macedonia

Semi-final: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland

Final: Czech Republic/Republic of Ireland vs Denmark/North Macedonia - Tuesday, 7.45pm kick-off

Sports.title: Coleman: Ireland's new generation not scarred by past World Cup play-off pain
Sports.content:
Seamus Coleman insists the Republic of Ireland's new generation will not be scarred by the bitter pain of World Cup play-off defeat as they attempt to book a ticket for this summer's finals.

Ireland face the Czech Republic at Prague's Fortuna Arena on Thursday evening attempting to go one better than they did in 2009 against France and in 2017, when Denmark shattered their dreams with a 5-1 demolition job in Dublin.

However, Everton defender Coleman, who was not in the squad on that fateful night in Paris and was injured for the game with the Danes, is confident there will be no hangover, with the Czechs standing between Heimir Hallgrimsson's men and a winner-takes-all match with either Denmark or North Macedonia in Dublin on Tuesday.

Asked if the pain of those near-misses was fuelling the latest bid to make it to the finals for the first time since 2002, the 37-year-old said: "It's difficult to say if it's fuelling the players, they're all so young.

"Obviously the nation was hurt massively, but in terms of the current group of players I don't think they're dwelling too much on that hurt.

"To be honest, we're just riding the wave of the confidence we've got as a group - which I think this young group deserves - from the last two games and we're looking forward to Thursday night and then see what comes after that.

"But to see how the nation is feeling now is incredible and we've got a duty to try and make them even happier."

Image: Troy Parrott's goals inspired Ireland to stunning wins over Portugal and Hungary that secured a play-off spot
