A dispute has emerged between Poland’s government and the office of opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki over whether Poland would be willing to host allied nuclear weapons. Deputy defence minister Paweł Zalewski announced on Thursday that Poland wants to participate in the US-led NATO nuclear sharing programme, but without actually hosting warheads. That prompted criticism from Nawrocki’s senior foreign policy aide, Marcin Przydacz, who says Poland should host such weapons. Jedno zdanie wiceszefa MON wystarczyło, by wywołać polityczną burzę wokół kwestii broni jądrowej w Polsce. Paweł Zalewski stwierdził w Kwaterze Głównej NATO w Brukseli, że Polska nie chce głowic nuklearnych na swoim terytorium. Kilka godzin później zareagował szef MON Władysław… pic.twitter.com/EqjTPKqidg — OficjalneZero (@OficjalneZero) August 28, 2026 Zalewski met on Thursday with Elbridge Colby, US under secretary of defence for policy, at NATO’s headquarters in Brussels. Afterwards, he was asked by reporters if an expanded future US military presence in Poland might include nuclear weapons. “No. I would like to say this very clearly and openly: Poland does not want nuclear warheads on its territory,” replied Zalewski, quoted by broadcaster TVN. The minister added that Poland still wants to be part of NATO’s nuclear deterrence programme. However, he said that this could be achieved without hosting the weapons themselves. Those remarks triggered criticism from the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), Poland’s main opposition party. Former PiS defence minister Mariusz Błaszczak said that refusing to host warheads “in practice means renouncing participation in nuclear sharing”. “Poland should strive for full participation in nuclear sharing,” added Błaszczak. “This is not a matter of Poland possessing its own nuclear weapons, but of strengthening NATO’s nuclear deterrence on the eastern flank.” Criticism also came from other sources, including retired Brigadier General Stanisław Koziej, who served as head of the National Security Bureau (BBN) of former President Bronisław Komorowski, who is an ally of the current government. Koziej called Zalewski’s announcement “an incomprehensible strategic mistake in the field of deterrence”. He said that, to deter Russia, Vladimir Putin must know that there is the possibility Poland could host nuclear weapons. Chęci nie odstraszają. Odstraszają realne zdolności – własne i sojusznicze. A przede wszystkim takie, o jakich użyciu sami decydujemy. To elementarz, który warto przypomnieć https://t.co/Nc3xXnA7bU — Paweł Zalewski (@ZalewskiPawel) August 27, 2026 Late on Thursday, Zalewski commented on the controversy. He rejected Błaszczak’s claim that refusing to host warheads would effectively exclude Poland from nuclear sharing. “We want to participate in NATO’s nuclear deterrence programme without wanting the stationing of nuclear weapons in Poland,” he wrote. “Thanks to our efforts, NATO has opened up precisely such a possibility.” In response to Koziej, Zalewski argued that “intentions do not deter, real capabilities do…above all, those whose use we ourselves decide upon”. Meanwhile, defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz also weighed in, declaring that “Poland remains strongly interested in participating in the NATO nuclear sharing programme” and is also “conducting talks regarding the proposal for participation in a European nuclear protective umbrella”. Kosiniak-Kamysz did not, however, comment on the issue of Poland potentially hosting warheads. Rozwiewając wszelkie wątpliwości: Polska jest niezmiennie zainteresowana udziałem w programie NATO Nuclear Sharing. Prowadzimy także rozmowy na temat propozycji uczestnictwa w europejskim nuklearnym parasolu ochronnym. Stanowisko naszego rządu jest w tych kwestiach… — Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz (@KosiniakKamysz) August 27, 2026 On Friday morning, Przydacz, who is the head of President Nawrocki’s International Policy Bureau (BPM), joined the criticism of Zalewski, calling his comments “bizarre, absurd and completely inconsistent with what Poland has been saying so far and what the policy of the Polish state is”. “Both the presidential palace and the executive branch of the government have so far supported Poland joining the nuclear sharing programme as part of its deterrence policy,” he continued. Przydacz added that “it is not true” the country wants to participate without actually hosting warheads. “Poland also wants to have warheads on its territory,” he said. Nawrocki, who is a close ally of President Donald Trump, has made clear his support for Poland seeking a nuclear sharing arrangement with the United States. But it remains unclear exactly what the government’s plans are. Earlier this year, Poland entered discussions with France over the extension of the French “nuclear umbrella” over Europe. Later, however, Prime Minister Donald Tusk indicated that Poland would not want to actually host French nuclear-armed aircraft. Both last year and this year, Tusk has also hinted that Poland could seek to develop its own independent nuclear deterrent. However, Colby made clear that the US would “strenuously oppose” European countries such as Poland, Germany or the Scandinavian states seeking to develop their own nuclear weapons. Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition, has regularly clashed with the government, including vetoing a record number of laws. However, the two sides have sought to present a more united front on issues of national security. The United States would “strenuously oppose” Poland, Germany or the Scandinavian countries seeking to develop their own nuclear weapons, says a senior Pentagon official. His comments come amid discussions in Poland and Europe over nuclear deterrence https://t.co/e9J8tNxcc9 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 5, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Kraków withdraws fireworks ban after negative court ruling
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A ban on the use of fireworks that was introduced last year by Kraków, Poland’s second-largest city, has been withdrawn after the local authorities decided not to appeal against a court decision revoking it. Kraków had argued that the ban would boost the safety and health of both humans and animals. However, opponents of the measures, including the provincial governor, who launched the legal challenge against it, argued that it was excessive and undermined constitutional freedoms. Kraków bez zakazu fajerwerków. Miasto nie zaskarży wyroku WSAhttps://t.co/rPEYNhEMAQ — Fakty RMF FM (@RMF24pl) August 25, 2026 In November 2025, Kraków’s city council adopted a resolution banning fireworks, firecrackers, sparklers and other pyrotechnic materials being set off “for entertainment purposes”. The ban, which carried an exemption for last year’s New Year’s celebrations, applied in public spaces as well as private properties where the use of fireworks was deemed to impact public places. The city said the ban aimed to “protect the life, health and peace of residents” and “ensure public safety”, adding that the discharge of pyrotechnics created noise and air pollution and could pose a threat to the health and life of humans and animals. Some councillors also argued that a ban would benefit residents suffering from trauma, including World War Two veterans and Ukrainian refugees. The city’s then mayor, Aleksander Miszalski, cited a city poll finding that 67.5% of respondents supported a year-round ban on fireworks and 31.2% opposed it. However, the measures were criticised by the head of the Association of Pyrotechnic Importers and Distributors, Marta Smolińska, who told news service Puls Krakowa that the ban was an “extreme solution” that would hurt local businesses. She called instead for “promoting the responsible use of pyrotechnics”. In December, Krzysztof Klęczar, the government-appointed governor of the Małopolska province, of which Kraków is the capital, announced that he would challenge the ban in the Provincial Administrative Court. Klęczar argued that the measures may “violate the principle of proportionality of limiting constitutional freedoms and rights as well as the freedom…to conduct business activity”. National parks in Poland have appealed to revellers to refrain from using fireworks this New Year’s Eve to avoid awakening wild animals from their winter slumber. A number of cities have also called on residents to abandon the tradition to protect petshttps://t.co/T6RQHdsF9P — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 29, 2022 His arguments were endorsed by the court, which, in a ruling in late June, deemed the resolution introducing the ban “invalid” and ordered that the city of Kraków pay legal costs. The court said the ban “went beyond the competence of the city council” and “violated the principle of proportionality of the protection of constitutional freedoms and rights”. It added that it “was not necessary to protect health, life or public order”. While Kraków could have appealed against the ruling at the Supreme Administrative Court, it has decided not to take that step. An appeal “would probably have little chance of upholding the resolution,” spokeswoman Dominika Jaźwiecka-Bujalska told the Polish Press Agency (PAP). Poland's largest opposition group has proposed a law banning fireworks, arguing that they cause distress, and even death, among domestic pets and wild animals https://t.co/UVzFMv3IEn — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 23, 2021 At the national level, in 2021, Civic Coalition (KO) – which was then the largest opposition party and is now Poland’s main ruling party – proposed a law that would have banned the use of most fireworks and firecrackers to protect domestic and wild animals. While that legislation did not proceed beyond a parliamentary commission, two further bills seeking to limit the use of fireworks to protect animals are currently proceeding in parliament, reports local news service Portal Samorządowy. Several Polish cities have introduced their own restrictions, which in some cases have also faced legal challenges. Wrocław, Poland’s third-largest city, also introduced a ban in January, which was likewise revoked in an administrative court after facing opposition from the provincial governor, reports PAP. Year-round bans remain in place in the Baltic resort town of Sopot, where there is an exemption for 31 December and 1 January, and the southern mountain resort town of Zakopane, a popular destination for New Year’s revellers, where the New Year period is included. The president of the Polish Olympic Committee (PKOl), Radosław Piesiewicz, has been detained as part of a criminal investigation into Zondacrypto, a cryptocurrency firm that collapsed earlier this year and was a major sponsor of Poland’s Olympic team. The development comes a day after Waldemar Żurek, Poland’s justice minister and prosecutor general, revealed that prosecutors are investigating possible crimes relating to Zondacrypto’s financing of various individuals and organisations, including PKOl, Piesiewicz, and figures from Poland’s right-wing opposition. Dziś w ramach śledztwa w sprawie ZondaCrypto zatrzymany został Radosław P. Prokuratura będzie przekazywała dalsze informacje po zakończeniu czynności z jego udziałem, prowadzonych w Śląskim Wydziale PZ PK. — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) August 27, 2026 On Thursday afternoon, Żurek announced that Piesiewicz had been detained and would be charged. He said he was unable to reveal what the charges would be, but confirmed that prosecutors are investigating a €40,000 watch reportedly given to Piesiewicz by the former head of Zondacrypto, Przemysław Kral. Under Piesiewicz’s leadership, PKOl signed an agreement in 2025 with Zondacrypto that made the crypto firm the main sponsor of the Polish team at this year’s Winter Olympics in Italy. However, in April, Zondacrypto began to come under scrutiny after customers began reporting being unable to access their funds. The firm subsequently collapsed and Kral went into hiding abroad. Prosecutors estimate losses to its clients of at least 350 million zloty (€81.4 million). At a press conference today, Żurek confirmed that Piesiewicz had been detained in connection with the investigation into Zondacrypto, which concerns suspected large-scale fraud and other criminal activity. The development comes days after two leading media outlets, Wirtualna Polska and TVN, published a joint investigation in which they alleged that Piesiewicz received a watch worth €40,000 and other gifts from Kral. The gifts were allegedly given in exchange for Piesiewicz intervening on behalf of Zondacrypto with Poland’s consumer protection authority, UOKiK. Piesiewicz denies the allegations and says he bought the watch with his own money, with Kral simply helping facilitate the purchase. 🔴Szef Zondacrypto, prezes PKOl i złoty zegarek za 40 tysięcy euro Prezes Polskiego Komitetu Olimpijskiego Radosław Piesiewicz dostał od szefa Zondacrypto Przemysława Krala zegarek Patek Philippe wart 40 tysięcy euro oraz inne prezenty – wynika z ustaleń wspólnego śledztwa… — Wirtualna Polska (@wirtualnapolska) August 24, 2026 Piesiewicz, who became head of PKOl in 2023 under Poland’s former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, has long been a controversial figure. In 2024, after PiS had lost power, he publicly clashed with Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s new government following Poland’s poor performance at the Paris Olympics, where the Polish team finished with its lowest medal haul since 1956. This year, as Zondocrypto fell into crisis, it emerged that the company had failed to provide promised bonuses to Polish athletes following the Winter Olympics. In May, 82 of the 106 members of the Polish Olympic Committee supported a motion calling for an extraordinary meeting at which the sole item on the agenda was the dismissal of Piesiewicz from his position. He has so far refused to convene the meeting. Poland has finished @Paris2024 with just one gold and 10 medals in total – its worst result since 1956. Poland has formally requested that the European Commission fine Meta, the owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, €250 million (1.1 billion zloty) for failing to tackle fraudulent advertising on its platforms. Its decision follows a high-profile campaign by Rafał Brzoska, the billionaire owner of Polish delivery giant InPost, over scam adverts on Facebook that exploit fake images of him and other prominent Polish public figures, including President Karol Nawrocki. Platformy cyfrowe muszą ponosić pełną odpowiedzialność za swoje działania i dlatego zawnioskowałem o nałożenie na Metę kary w wysokości miliarda złotych. Po analizie materiałów, w tym tych otrzymanych od Meta, a także kolejnych doniesień medialnych o braku kontroli nad… pic.twitter.com/1zSZg8MGf4 — Krzysztof Gawkowski (@KGawkowski) August 27, 2026 On Thursday morning, digital affairs minister Krzysztof Gawkowski announced that he had sent a request to the European Commission to take action against Meta, including fining it €250 million. “Inaction and ineffectiveness in combating harmful s and fraudulent content targeting Poles will not be tolerated,” wrote Gawkowski. “I expect the European Commission to conduct the proceedings swiftly and impose the fine. There is more than enough evidence.” The minister also called on Meta itself to “immediately introduce effective tools to eliminate scams, fake s, and the promotion of illegal applications. This Wild West on the platform must come to an end”. Gawkowski shared an image of the first page of a letter he had sent to Henna Virkkunen, the European commissioner for technological sovereignty, security and democracy, in which he argued that Meta’s failure to combat fraud may violate the EU’s Digital Services Act. He pointed to a study by CERT Polska, a Polish state IT security body, which found that, of 122 adverts reported to Meta as being fraudulent, in 106 cases the company rejected requests to remove them. Gawkowski noted that the European Consumer Organisation has reported similar concerns to the EU. On Wednesday, Gawkowski also shared copies of correspondence he had exchanged with Meta earlier this month. In response to the minister’s concerns, the tech firm had argued that it “does not seek to profit from” fraudulent advertising and outlined steps it was taking to address the problem. Meta disclosed that, between July 2025 and June 2026, it had, in Poland alone, removed 380,000 examples of content and 137,000 adverts for violating its policies on fraudulent practices. It noted that the vast majority were removed before users even reported them. Meta przesłała odpowiedź o działaniach związanych ze zwalczaniem scamów i wskazuje, że niektóre dane przekazuje z zachowaniem ścisłej poufności. W państwie szanującym obywatela takie dane muszą być jawne i dlatego podjąłem decyzję o ujawnieniu treści pisma. W piśmie Meta… — Krzysztof Gawkowski (@KGawkowski) August 26, 2026 Gawkowski’s intervention follows a high-profile campaign by Brzoska, one of Poland’s richest people and who, along with his wife, former TV presenter and businesswoman Omenaa Mensah, is a prominent public figure. Brzoska and Mensah have long complained about the unauthorised use of their likenesses in fraudulent social-media advertising, especially on Facebook. In 2024, Poland’s data protection authority ordered Meta to stop displaying adverts that featured false reports of Mensah’s death to promote scams. Earlier this month, Brzoska renewed his campaign, highlighting an example of a scam on Facebook that used a fake image of him being handcuffed by police in his home. Tak działa koncern @Meta w Polsce-nieustająco tolerując fake newsy na mój i wiele innych publicznych osób temat… Może innym to nie przeszkadza, ale jeśli moje małoletnie dzieciaki wysyłają mi te screeny pytając "o co chodzi Tato?", to jak się polskiemu zarządowi tej gównianej… pic.twitter.com/rp4CUscah1 — Rafał Brzoska (@RBrzoska) August 14, 2026 Brzoska – who also pointed to examples of Facebook running fake adverts featuring other prominent Polish figures, including President Nawrocki – launched a petition calling for platforms that run scam adverts to be fined 150% of the revenue they received from them. The petition – which, at the time of writing, has been signed by almost 91,000 people – cited leaked data, reported by Reuters last year, indicating that Meta estimated 10% of its sales in 2024, around €16 billion, came from advertising scams or illegal products and services. In comments to Reuters, Meta said at the time that the estimate was “rough and overly inclusive” and that the actual figure was lower. But it declined to provide an updated figure. Nowy dzień i nowy scam serwowany bez żadnych oporów przez @Meta z Prezydentem @NawrockiKn w roli głównej. Ale to managerowie Meta (Robert Bednarski, Jakub Turowski,Tomasz Parfjanowicz i Ewa Tumanow) mówią,że nic nie mogą w tej sprawie. Jeśli chcemy temu powiedzieć stanowcze… pic.twitter.com/ZVZl04yYY1 — Rafał Brzoska (@RBrzoska) August 24, 2026 This week, Brzoska welcomed Gawkowski’s moves against Meta. He also noted that, while the minister’s letter to Meta had been addressed to Jakub Turowski, Meta’s director of public policy for Central and Eastern Europe, the firm’s response to him was unsigned. “First-class cowardice,” declared Brzoska, who has repeatedly published the names of four of Meta’s senior Polish managers, including Turowski. World.title: Czechia Spent CZK 19 Billion on COVID Vaccines and Used Less Than Half
World.content:
The Czech Republic has spent roughly CZK 19 billion on COVID-19 vaccines since 2020, but fewer than half of the 41 million doses supplied under its pandemic-era procurement agreement were ultimately used in the country.

More than 18 million doses expired and had to be destroyed, representing a value of about CZK 8 billion.

A further four million doses were donated to other countries, according to information provided by the Czech Ministry of Health in response to a request from the Czech Technical Committee.



For the 2026-27 vaccination season, around 900,000 doses will be available in the country. By comparison, fewer than one-third of that number was administered during the previous season. The vaccination season runs from September through the end of August the following year.

Demand for COVID-19 vaccination has fallen sharply since the initial rollout. More than 15 million doses were administered during the first year vaccines were widely available. A year later, demand had fallen to roughly one-fifth of that level. Between 2022 and 2023, interest dropped by more than 80 percent, followed by further declines of about one-third in subsequent years.

Only about 1,500 doses had been administered by July 26 this year. Most vaccinations, however, take place during the autumn months.

The low demand has contributed to substantial vaccine waste. When the original purchases were made, authorities faced considerable uncertainty over how the pandemic would develop, how many booster doses would be required and how many people would seek vaccination.

Maintaining sufficient supplies was considered necessary in case the epidemiological situation deteriorated.

The Czech Republic is now considering a different approach to future procurement. The Ministry of Health is negotiating with vaccine manufacturers, health insurance companies and medical organisations over supplies and financing for the 2027-28 season. The talks are taking into account both the expected demand and the cost-effectiveness of vaccination.

World.title: Foreign Pupils on the Rise in Czech Schools — Nearly One in Five in Prague
World.content:
Of the nearly one million pupils attending Czech primary schools last academic year, almost 8% were foreign nationals, most commonly from Ukraine.

According to the Czech Statistical Office (CSO), Prague recorded the highest proportion, with foreign pupils making up 18% of all children in its primary schools.

Compulsory education is mandatory for Czech citizens as well as citizens of other European Union member states who reside in the Czech Republic for more than 90 days. The requirement also applies to foreign nationals with long-term residence permits.

Their children therefore have the same rights as Czech children, including access to free education, school meals and extracurricular activities.



The number of foreign pupils increased significantly after Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, nearly doubling that year. Their numbers have continued to rise ever since. Today, children from Ukraine account for 5% of all pupils in the Czech Republic.

The trend is similar in secondary schools, where the proportion of foreign pupils reached its highest level in the past 10 years, at almost 5% of the total.

Although the number of children in primary schools has remained relatively stable at just over one million in recent years, a sharp decline is expected in the coming years due to the falling birth rate, according to Vendula Kašparová of the CSO’s Social Development Statistics Department. The office said the birth rate has been falling continuously for the fifth consecutive year.

The decline is already visible at the kindergarten level. The number of children enrolled in kindergartens fell below 350,000 in the 2025/2026 academic year, the first time this has happened since 2013. Over the past three years, enrolment has dropped by more than 21,000 children, or around 5.8%.

Fewer Children Receiving Deferrals From Starting School

Kašparová identifies another clear trend: fewer children are being granted deferrals from starting compulsory school. Since the 2021/2022 academic year, the proportion of six-year-olds whose school entry was deferred has fallen from 24.1% in September 2021 to 17.7% in September 2025, representing just under 21,000 pupils.

Furthermore, an amendment to the Education Act is expected to reduce the number of deferrals even further. Under the new rules, deferrals will only be granted when justified by a medical condition that prevents a child from attending school.

This could include a serious medical condition following surgery, cancer treatment or a moderate intellectual disability.

World.title: Czechia, the Land of Burgers. More Fast Food Chains Enter the Market
World.content:
The Czech fast food market is expanding beyond its established players, with new international brands entering the country and existing chains opening restaurants in smaller cities.

McDonald’s and KFC continue to build their networks, while brands from Germany, the United States and Poland are looking for opportunities in the Czech Republic.

The expansion is increasingly moving beyond Prague and other major cities, with retail parks becoming an important location for new restaurants.



Burgermeister prepares Czech debut

One of the newest international brands preparing to enter the Czech market is Germany’s Burgermeister. The Berlin-based burger chain plans to open its first restaurant on Wenceslas Square at the beginning of next year.

The company already sees its Prague location as more than a single restaurant. It is also considering further locations across the country.

Popeyes and Burger King continue expanding

Burger King entered the Czech market 18 years ago and now operates around 70 restaurants. Popeyes arrived much later but has expanded quickly, opening 19 locations during its first three years in the country.

The companies are building a network that stretches from smaller regional towns to central Prague. In Králův Dvůr, a town of around 11,000 people, both Burger King and Popeyes operate at the Litavka Retail Park.

Popeyes is preparing additional restaurants at the Eden shopping centre and in the Budějovická area of Prague. The chain is also expanding into regional cities, with planned locations in Klatovy and Písek.

Five Guys adds another international brand

The Czech burger market gained another major international name last December when U.S. chain Five Guys opened its first Prague restaurant.

The restaurant is located in the former Máj department store on Národní Street. Five Guys is known for burgers prepared to order and a wide range of toppings, allowing customers to customise their meals.

Its prices, however, are generally higher than those of traditional fast food chains.

Another U.S. brand, Dave’s Hot Chicken, is also expected to enter the Czech market this year, according to consulting firm Cushman & Wakefield.

The chain specialises in spicy fried chicken and will therefore compete directly with established players such as KFC and Popeyes.

Czech chains are looking beyond their home cities

The expansion is not limited to international companies.

Czech burger chain Mama’s Burger is also developing its network. Originally based in Ostrava, the company has expanded into several larger Czech cities and operates a restaurant at Prague’s Arkády Pankrác shopping centre.

The company is also seeking franchise partners as it looks to increase the number of locations.

World.title: Slavia Prague to Face Bayern Munich, Arsenal and Porto in Champions League
World.content:
Slavia Prague have learned their eight opponents for the 2026/27 UEFA Champions League league phase following Thursday’s draw in Monaco.

Slavia will play four matches at home at Eden Arena and four away.

At home, Slavia will welcome Arsenal, Aston Villa, Villarreal and Lens. Their away fixtures will take them to Bayern Munich, Porto, Fenerbahçe and Sabah Baku in Azerbaijan.



The most high-profile home fixture will be against Arsenal, the reigning Premier League champions. Slavia also faced the London club in last season’s Champions League campaign, making the return meeting at Eden Arena particularly notable.

The toughest away assignment is likely to come in Munich, where Slavia will face six-time European champions Bayern at the Allianz Arena. The team will also travel to Portugal to meet Porto and to Istanbul for a match against Fenerbahçe.

The longest trip of the league phase will be to Baku to face Azerbaijani champions Sabah, who are making their debut in the Champions League league phase.

How the Champions League league phase works

The 2026/27 competition is being played under UEFA’s new league-phase format for the third consecutive season. Instead of a traditional group stage, all 36 teams are placed in one league table.

Each club plays eight matches against eight different opponents, with two opponents drawn from each of the four seeding pots. Every team has four home and four away games.

The top eight teams in the final standings will advance directly to the round of 16. Teams finishing ninth to 24th will enter a knockout playoff for the remaining eight places, while clubs finishing from 25th to 36th will be eliminated.

The league phase begins on September 8–10, with six rounds taking place before the end of 2026. The final two matchdays will be played in January, with the league phase concluding on January 27. UEFA will announce the exact dates and kick-off times for each individual match later.

World.title: MINT Market Returns to Prague’s Náplavka with More Than 130 Local Brands
World.content:
MINT Market returns to Prague’s Rašín Embankment on Sunday, September 6, bringing more than 130 independent brands and makers to the Vltava riverbank.

From 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., visitors can browse a wide selection of independent fashion, jewellery, ceramics, natural cosmetics, illustrations and original accessories, with many of the products made by small Czech and Prague-based businesses.



The popular design market is also known for its relaxed atmosphere, food stalls and chill-out area. Admission is free, and the riverside venue is fully accessible. The event is suitable for visitors of all ages.

MINT Market has been supporting independent and local creators since 2010.

Over the past 16 years, the project has grown from a small market into a nationwide platform, hosting more than 450 events in over 20 Czech cities and bringing together a community of more than 1,500 designers and makers.

For visitors, the September event offers a chance to discover products that are often made locally and in small quantities, while meeting the people behind the brands directly.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by The best design markets in CZ (@mintmarket.cz)

“Supporting small and local brands has been one of the core ideas of our project from the very beginning,” says MINT Market organizer Lenka Šašková.

“We provide creators with a place where they can showcase their products and meet their customers, because nothing can replace a personal meeting.”

The full list of vendors and further information about the September market can be found on the MINT Market website. Updates are also available through the Facebook event and Instagram.

World.title: Historic Invalidovna Building in Prague Begins Major Reconstruction
World.content:
The long-awaited reconstruction of Prague’s Invalidovna has officially begun.

The Baroque complex in Karlín will undergo a major renovation costing CZK 2.15 billion, with work scheduled for completion in 2030.

The project is the largest investment in the history of the National Heritage Institute (NPÚ). Alongside the restoration of the historic building, two new extensions will be constructed on the southern side of the complex.



One will provide facilities for the Prague Philharmonic Choir, while the other will house technical infrastructure needed to operate the site.

Much of Invalidovna will remain open to the public

Once the reconstruction is complete, the NPÚ will use part of the complex for restoration workshops, laboratories, archives and study rooms.

An underground garage with space for 50 vehicles is also planned.

Around 80 percent of the complex is expected to remain accessible to the public. The restored site will include exhibition and conference spaces, visitor routes through the Baroque interiors, a café and facilities for children’s groups operated by Prague 8.

A new multi-purpose hall in one of the extensions will be suitable for concerts, conferences and other events. The modern section will also contain technical facilities that cannot be accommodated inside the protected historic building.

The courtyard and gardens will be opened through the original entrances.

A Baroque complex with a long military history

Invalidovna was built between 1731 and 1737 based on plans by Kilián Ignác Dientzenhofer, one of the leading architects of the Czech Baroque. The institution provided accommodation and care for war veterans and their families until 1935.

The original complex was designed at a time when European armies were beginning to develop more systematic forms of care for soldiers who had been wounded or disabled in war.

Military campaigns were often accompanied by outbreaks of diseases such as cholera and typhus, which could kill even soldiers whose battlefield injuries were not life-threatening. Separate psychiatric institutions were later established for veterans suffering severe mental trauma after their military service.

World.title: Tisza government official resigns after just two months; opposition Fidesz reacts immediately
World.content:
A deputy state secretary at Hungary’s Ministry of Rural and Settlement Development has resigned after only around two months in the position, citing personal reasons. The announcement immediately triggered a political exchange, with Fidesz MP Miklós Panyi suggesting the departure points to problems within the new Tisza government.

Rural and Settlement Development Minister Dr Viktória Lőrincz announced the resignation on Sunday afternoon, stressing that there was nothing extraordinary about the decision.

Deputy state secretary cites personal reasons

According to Lőrincz, the deputy state secretary submitted their resignation because of a change in their personal circumstances.

“There is nothing extraordinary about this; we will soon arrange for the departing colleague to be replaced,”

the minister said in a Facebook post.

Lőrincz also rejected speculation that internal disagreements at the ministry were behind the resignation. She accused Fidesz of attempting to build conspiracy theories around the departure and said the ministry would not comment on what she described as baseless claims, out of respect for its employees’ private lives.

She also called on opposition politicians not to spread what she described as false information about people working in public administration.

Fidesz MP claims leaders are already leaving

The minister’s comments came shortly after Fidesz MP Miklós Panyi published his own post about the resignation.

Panyi claimed that the official had started working at the ministry at the end of June and that their departure would take effect on 1 September. He described the ministry as one of the “most incompetent” departments of the Tisza government and suggested that the resignation reflected wider problems within the new administration.

The Fidesz politician also claimed that several government officials, including chiefs of staff and deputy state secretaries, had left their positions after only a few weeks. Panyi characterised the latest departure as a sign that officials were already “fleeing” what he called the “Tisza government’s authoritarian government”.

He also questioned why a supposedly committed and competent senior official would leave a well-paid position so soon after taking it up.

If you missed it: Tisza government takes back EUR 276 million in state assets as KEKVA system is dismantled

Minister rejects claims of a crisis

Lőrincz, however, said the resignation should not be interpreted as evidence of a crisis within the ministry. She maintained that the official’s decision was based on personal circumstances and reiterated that a replacement would be appointed shortly.

The departure comes roughly two months after the official joined the ministry. The resignation is expected to take effect on 1 September. At this stage, neither the identity of the departing deputy state secretary nor further details about the personal reasons cited for the resignation have been publicly disclosed.

World.title: Debrecen stabbing tragedy: 23-year-old man dies after being stabbed in the heart
World.content:
A 23-year-old man has died after being stabbed in the heart during an attack in Debrecen in the early hours of Saturday morning. According to eyewitness accounts cited by RTL Híradó, the two young men had confronted the alleged attacker after seeing him assaulting a woman in the street.

As previously reported, two young men were stabbed by a 64-year-old man on Múzeum Street in Debrecen at around 3 AM on 30 August. Police said the attack was preceded by a verbal altercation, after which the man pulled out a knife and stabbed both victims.

Both men were taken to hospital by paramedics. Police arrested the suspect approximately two hours after the incident.

Young man stabbed in the heart dies

The 23-year-old victim from Létavértes was stabbed in the heart and suffered life-threatening injuries. RTL Híradó has now reported that he died from his injuries despite efforts to save his life.

His 24-year-old friend was stabbed in the abdomen. He also suffered serious injuries but was able to reach a nearby tobacconist’s shop and ask for help. His condition is reportedly stable.

A third member of the group escaped the attack unharmed. According to the report, he tried to stop the bleeding from his friend’s chest wound with both hands while waiting for help to arrive.

The injured 23-year-old was still able to communicate at the scene, but paramedics were unable to save his life.

Young men allegedly confronted attacker over woman

RTL Híradó reported, citing eyewitnesses, that the incident began after the 64-year-old man allegedly assaulted a woman while shouting at her in the street.

The two young men reportedly approached him and told him to stop and leave the woman alone. The man allegedly then pulled out a knife and approached the two victims, who were sitting on a bench. The precise circumstances of the confrontation are still being investigated.

Police previously said that the 64-year-old suspect was arrested after officers searched the surrounding streets for approximately two hours. He was questioned as a suspect, taken into custody, and prosecutors were asked to order his detention.

The Hajdú-Bihar County Police Headquarters’ Criminal Directorate is investigating the case on suspicion of causing life-threatening bodily harm. Following the victim’s death, the legal classification of the alleged offence may now be subject to change.

World.title: World’s most liveable cities ranking is out: here’s how Budapest performed
World.content:
Budapest has slipped four places in the latest Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) Global Liveability Index, ranking 36th out of 173 cities. While Copenhagen remains at the top, Asia is gaining ground and several Middle Eastern cities have suffered sharp falls amid worsening security conditions.

Copenhagen remains the world’s most liveable city

The overall picture of global liveability has not changed dramatically in 2026, but significant shifts are taking place beneath the surface. The EIU assessed 173 cities across 30 indicators, grouped into five broad categories: stability, healthcare, culture and environment, education and infrastructure. The resulting score is measured on a 100-point scale.

The average score this year was 76.1 points, unchanged from 2025.

However, individual categories moved in different directions. The average stability score fell by another 0.5 points, while culture and environment also deteriorated slightly. Healthcare, meanwhile, improved by an average of 0.7 points, with smaller gains also recorded in education and infrastructure.

At the top of the ranking, Copenhagen retained first place, followed by Vienna and Melbourne.

The top 10 remains dominated by cities in wealthy, developed countries, with Australia, Canada, Japan and Switzerland all represented.

Asia is catching up with Europe

Western Europe remains the strongest-performing region overall, but it has stopped extending its lead. The region’s average liveability score remained broadly unchanged, while Asian cities continued to improve. As a result, nine Asian cities and seven European cities now feature among the world’s 20 most liveable cities.

The EIU attributed some of the progress made by Chinese cities to improvements in healthcare indicators. New York also recorded a stronger stability score, helped by declining crime figures in recent years and a lower perceived risk of a major terrorist attack, Pénzcentrum writes.

If you missed it: Budapest lifts energy restrictions as normal operations return on 1 September

Budapest falls four places

Budapest ranked 36th out of 173 cities, with a liveability score of 91 points. That represents a four-place drop compared with last year, while the Hungarian capital’s overall score declined by one point.

Budapest was therefore among the cities experiencing one of the more noticeable falls in the ranking. Its four-place drop was the same as those recorded by Luxembourg, Portland, Abu Dhabi, Dubai and Saipan, although their starting positions and scores differed considerably.

Despite the setback, 91 points remains a strong result.

Photo: Anadolu Agency

For comparison, Zurich scored 96 points and ranked fifth, while Auckland and Luxembourg both scored 95 points, placing 12th and 15th respectively. Athens, meanwhile, ranked 88th with 78 points, meaning Budapest’s absolute liveability score remains considerably higher than that of the Greek capital.

The ranking does not simply measure how enjoyable a city is to live in. It also considers its stability, healthcare and education systems, cultural and environmental conditions and the quality of its infrastructure.

Middle Eastern cities suffer major setbacks

The most dramatic deterioration in this year’s ranking was recorded in the Middle East. In previous years, stability scores had been particularly affected in Europe by the war in Ukraine, terrorist attacks and protests. In 2026, however, the focus shifted towards the Middle East.

According to the EIU, the war involving Iran that began in February, Israeli and US strikes on Iran and subsequent regional responses significantly damaged perceptions of security across the region. The 18 Middle Eastern and North African cities included in the index fell by more than three places on average.

Muscat experienced the sharpest decline, falling 14 places to 123rd, with a score of 68. Kuwait City dropped 12 places, Amman 11 and Manama 10. Doha fell seven places, while Tehran entered the 10 least liveable cities in the world.

For Budapest, the four-place fall is a setback, but the Hungarian capital remains firmly within the upper tier of the global rankings, despite losing ground compared with last year.

World.title: Cold front to sweep across Hungary as September begins: but summer is not over yet
World.content:
A cold front will reach Hungary on Monday, bringing a slight drop in temperatures as September begins. However, forecasters say genuinely autumnal weather is still some way off, while the country’s drought is unlikely to ease significantly.

Cold front arrives on Monday

Hungary will see a change in the weather on the final day of August, as a cold front reaches the country on Monday, 31 August, according to HungaroMet.

The front will bring somewhat fresher mornings in early September, but temperatures will remain relatively high. In the afternoons, temperatures could still approach 30°C in many parts of the country. So while the calendar is about to turn to autumn, the weather will not be making a dramatic seasonal switch just yet.

Rain may finally reach a wider area

The cold front could also bring the most widespread rainfall of the week. Current forecasts suggest that rain could fall in several parts of Hungary by Tuesday morning. However, HungaroMet warned that there remains considerable uncertainty in the forecasts, with some models still pointing towards a considerably drier scenario.

This means that although the front could provide some much-needed rainfall, it is unlikely to deliver a major breakthrough in the country’s persistent precipitation deficit.

Drought set to continue

HungaroMet’s weekly precipitation outlook indicates that the drought is unlikely to ease significantly during the coming week. The lack of rainfall has remained a major concern after an exceptionally hot and dry summer, and the start of meteorological autumn is not expected to bring a substantial change in conditions.

The coming days will therefore bring a combination of fresher mornings and relatively warm afternoons, rather than the sustained cool weather many people associate with September.

No real autumn just yet

For those already looking forward to autumn, there is still a little longer to wait. The cold front will lower temperatures by a few degrees, but HungaroMet says genuinely autumnal weather is not yet on the horizon.

Instead, September will begin with moderately warm conditions, while the rainfall situation is uncertain and the country’s drought could persist. In other words, summer may be taking a small step back, but it is certainly not ready to disappear just yet.

World.title: Tisza government takes back EUR 276 million in state assets as KEKVA system is dismantled
World.content:
The liquidation of Hungary’s public interest asset management foundations has been completed, with assets previously transferred to the foundations returning to the state. Transport and Investment Minister Dávid Vitézy says four foundations alone have returned around HUF 100 billion (EUR 276 million) in state assets to the budget.

HUF 100 billion returned to the state

The liquidation of Hungary’s public interest asset management foundations (KEKVAs) was completed at the end of August, meaning assets previously transferred to the foundations have now returned to state ownership.

Dávid Vitézy, Minister for Transport and Investment, said the process had been carried out over the past two months by liquidators appointed by the government. The ministries concerned will now take over the management of the assets and the functions previously performed by the foundations.

In the case of the Transport and Investment Ministry, four foundations were involved:

the Millenáris Scientific Cultural Foundation,

the Central European Foundation for the Preservation of Built Heritage,

the Hauszmann Foundation, and

the Central European Education Foundation.

According to Vitézy, taking over these four foundations has brought around HUF 100 billion worth of assets back under state control.

Government says public services will not suffer

Vitézy stressed that the restructuring would not negatively affect the day-to-day operation of the institutions or the services they provide. He argued that the new system would eliminate unnecessary positions while making the use of significant amounts of state property more transparent and subject to public oversight.

“There will be no public task or service whose quality will deteriorate under the new system,” Vitézy said, adding that numerous positions he described as unnecessary “pay-outs” had been eliminated.

The minister also portrayed the move as a major change in how public assets are managed, saying assets originating from public funds were now returning to the state.

KEKVA system was a long-running EU dispute

The foundations were originally established under the previous Fidesz government, but Vitézy has strongly criticised the system, arguing that it allowed state assets and public funds to be managed in an insufficiently transparent manner.

He claimed that the governing boards of the foundations were largely made up of Fidesz politicians and that the system was designed to keep control of the assets in the hands of people linked to the former governing party even after a possible change of government.

The KEKVA system has also been at the centre of a long-running dispute between Hungary and the European Commission. The Commission had criticised the presence of politicians on the foundations’ governing boards and their management of state assets, with reforms to the system becoming one of the conditions linked to the release of EU funding.

Vitézy argued that the previous government had refused to dismantle the system despite the consequences for Hungary’s access to EU funds.

World.title: Hungarian passenger changes his mind three times – Wizz Air actually let him fly home for free
World.content:
A passenger travelling from Budapest to Crete reportedly changed his mind about flying just before boarding, changed it back moments later, and then decided mid-flight that he wanted to return to Budapest immediately. What happened next sounds too bizarre to be true, but Wizz Air has confirmed the story.

From Budapest to Crete and back again

According to 444.hu, the extraordinary story was shared in the Hungarian Facebook group Wizz Air, Ryanair és egyéb fapados károsultak (“Wizz Air, Ryanair and other low-cost airline victims”) by a passenger who had booked a flight from Budapest to Heraklion on 25 August.

Everything appeared to be going smoothly until boarding. As he was about to board the aircraft, the man suddenly became unsure whether he actually wanted to travel. He walked out onto the apron, waited while the other passengers boarded and eventually sat down on a set of steps.

A member of the ground staff approached him and tried to reassure him, but the passenger ultimately decided not to travel. He was escorted back to the gate, where staff removed his name from the passenger list.

Then, while walking back through the terminal, he changed his mind again. He reportedly got as far as the piano when he suddenly decided that he did want to go to Crete after all. He ran back to the gate and asked to board.

There was a problem: he had already been removed from the passenger list. Staff explained that they needed special permission from the captain before he could return to the aircraft. After some coordination, permission was granted, and a ground staff member escorted him back to the plane.

The lake of Agios Nikolaos, Crete, Greece. Photo: depositphotos.com

Then he wanted to come straight home

You might think that was the end of the story, but it wasn’t. During the flight to Heraklion, the passenger apparently reconsidered the purpose of his trip and decided that he no longer wanted to stay in Crete. Instead, he wanted to fly straight back to Budapest on the very same aircraft.

There was just one small problem: he had no ticket for the return flight. He had no booking, no boarding pass and, according to his account, no return ticket for any other day either.

He approached the senior cabin crew member and explained his unusual request. The crew member told him they would try to help, but that the situation would require coordination with the airline, the captain and the ground staff in Heraklion. The passenger was moved to the first row while the crew worked on a solution.

Wizz Air arranged a free return

When the aircraft landed in Heraklion, the passenger did not leave the plane. Instead, he waited on board while the other passengers disembarked and the aircraft was prepared for its return flight to Budapest. Around ten minutes later, a member of the ground-handling team arrived carrying something rather unexpected: a boarding pass for the passenger’s return flight to Budapest.

He did not have to leave the aircraft, go through security again or purchase a ticket. And, most remarkably, he did not have to pay for the return journey.

The passenger said he was subsequently able to remain on the same aircraft and even speak briefly with the captain before the Budapest-bound passengers boarded.

“Surely this must be made up?”

The story was so extraordinary that even 444.hu’s journalist who reported it initially assumed it was a hoax. The passenger’s account appeared almost too perfect: an indecisive traveller who repeatedly changed his mind, managed to board after being removed from the passenger list, then convinced the airline to let him fly back to Budapest for free without having a return ticket.

There was even speculation that the story could be some kind of Wizz Air PR stunt, but then the airline’s communications agency responded.

Wizz Air confirmed that the airline really did arrange the passenger’s ticket home.

The passenger also praised the crew for their patience and helpfulness throughout the bizarre ordeal, saying that staff never made him feel like he was causing a problem or behaving foolishly. He acknowledged that the situation was highly unusual and that the airline was under no obligation to go to such lengths to help him.

World.title: Budapest lifts energy restrictions as normal operations return on 1 September
World.content:
Budapest is set to return to normal operations from 1 September after the capital’s energy supply was restored. Decorative lighting, fountains and the Gellért Hill waterfall will also be switched back on following weeks of energy and water-saving measures.

Budapest’s restrictions to end

Budapest’s municipal companies will return to their usual operating schedules from 1 September, Mayor Gergely Karácsony announced on Sunday. The temporary restrictions were introduced during a period of extreme summer heat, severe drought and pressure on the country’s energy system.

According to Karácsony, the measures can now be gradually withdrawn after energy supplies have been restored. The mayor said the capital had adapted to the exceptional circumstances while trying to keep public services running with as little disruption as possible.

Among the measures introduced were reduced energy consumption in public transport and at municipal companies, more economical watering of Budapest’s trees and lower overall water use. The city’s decorative lighting was also temporarily switched off, along with fountains and the Gellért Hill waterfall.

From September, these measures will come to an end, and Budapest will once again operate under its usual arrangements.

Public transport also cut energy use

The measures produced significant energy savings across the capital during August. According to information released by the Mayor’s Office, BKK and BKV vehicles accelerated and braked less intensively, saving more than 661 MWh of electricity in the tram network and over 355 MWh on the metro system.

BKK also reduced the energy consumption of escalators at metro stations and cut electricity use at its office building by around 20 per cent. The city said these steps demonstrated that Budapest could respond collectively and responsibly to the increasingly extreme effects of climate change.

Nearly 20 MWh saved by switching off city lights

Budapest’s public utility company, BKM, saved almost 20 MWh of electricity by temporarily switching off the capital’s decorative lighting. Its peak electricity demand was also reduced by almost 4 MW, while total energy savings at the company exceeded 120 MWh.

The city compared this figure to roughly half an hour of full production by one unit of the Paks Nuclear Power Plant. Meanwhile, Főkert saved around 25,000 cubic metres of water by temporarily shutting down the city’s fountains. BKM is also continuing to install solar power systems, with its installed generation capacity expected to reach 1 MW by the end of the year.

Have you heard? Relief for drivers as Budapest traffic becomes easier with important flyover now finished

Gellért Hill waterfall and fountains return

For Budapest residents and visitors, one of the most visible changes will be the return of the city’s decorative features. The Gellért Hill waterfall and fountains, which were switched off as part of the emergency water-saving measures, are expected to resume operation.

Karácsony said that although the immediate conservation measures are ending, the lessons learned during the crisis should remain. He said the capital would continue working towards a more sustainable, energy-independent and resilient Budapest, while thanking residents for their patience and cooperation.

The city is also consulting with MOHU Budapest, which operates the Capital’s Waste Recovery Facility, about temporarily reducing heat intake during critical periods. This could allow additional electricity to be fed into the national power grid when the system is under particular pressure.

World.title: Bucharest Stock Exchange-listed tech company AROBS posts 121% higher net profit in H1
World.content:
AROBS Transilvania Software (BVB: AROBS), one of the largest entrepreneurial technology companies listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange, recorded consolidated turnover of RON 292 million in the first half of 2026, up 36% compared to H1 2025, EBITDA of RON 40 million, a 29% increase, and net profit of approximately RON 23 million, up 121% compared to the same period of last year.

The first six months of 2026 represented the AROBS group’s best first half of the past three years in terms of turnover, EBITDA, operating profit, and net profit. The positive momentum accelerated in the second quarter, when the group generated turnover of approximately RON 148 million, EBITDA of RON 22 million, and net profit of over RON 15 million, twice the level recorded in Q1 2026 and almost four times higher than in Q2 2025.

“In 2024 and 2025, we increased the scale of the group and added capabilities through the acquisitions we completed. In 2026, our focus is on integrating these capabilities through One AROBS and transforming this structure into an organization that operates as one, both commercially and operationally,” stated Voicu Oprean, founder and CEO of AROBS.

Of the consolidated turnover recorded in H1 2026, RON 242 million, representing almost 83% of the total, was generated by activities classified as organic, while RON 50 million came from companies included in the M&A scope.

At business segment level, Software Services generated turnover of approximately RON 186 million, up 31% compared to H1 2025. Software Products recorded turnover of RON 54 million, 17% above the level reported in the comparable period, while the segment’s gross margin increased from 52% to 54%.

The fastest growth was recorded by Integrated Systems, where turnover advanced by 88% to RON 52 million, mainly as a result of the implementation of projects for the National House of Public Pensions and the Ministry of Health. Furthermore, after the end of the first semester, AROBS Systems signed a contract with the Agency for Payments and Intervention for Agriculture (APIA) with a total value of approximately RON 70 million, excluding VAT, of which approximately 61% is attributable to the company.

In the first half of the year, AROBS achieved 53% of the turnover, 49% of the EBITDA and 65% of the net profit envisaged in the 2026 Consolidated Revenue and Expense Budget, which provides for turnover of RON 552 million, EBITDA of RON 82 million and net profit of RON 35 million. The budget approved in April was prepared based on prudent estimates regarding the contributions of GESS and QUEST, companies acquired by AROBS in November 2025 and January 2026, respectively, and does not include contracts signed after its approval, including the contract concluded by AROBS Systems with APIA in August.

“The results for the first half of the year provide the first financial confirmation of this model. For the second half of the year, our objective is for the increase in turnover to translate to a greater extent into EBITDA. Looking ahead to 2027-2030, the group’s development will be supported by expansion in international markets, the organization of our activities around the verticals in which we have expertise, the development of proprietary products and the integration of AI into the solutions and services we provide,” he added.

World.title: Romanian digital education infrastructure provider Ascendia posts 50% higher net profit in H1
World.content:
Ascendia (BVB: ASC), a Romanian benchmark and provider of critical learning infrastructure, announced its financial results for the first half of 2026. According to the press release, the company recorded the best first half in its history, marking accelerated growth supported by the completion of previous projects, its own product portfolio, and efficient capital management.

“The first half of 2026 was the best first half in the company’s history. After the very good results recorded in H1 2025, we managed to achieve significant growth both in terms of revenue and net profit. We have a solid financial position, with cash of around RON 25.8 million. This flexibility allows us to consider the possibility of early repayment of the ASC27 bonds to reduce financing costs,” said Cosmin Mălureanu, CEO and co-founder of Ascendia.

As of June 30, 2026, equity doubled to RON 37.95 million, representing 71% of total assets of RON 53.45 million. The current liquidity ratio strengthened to 4.56, giving the company the capacity to finance future expansion stages without the pressure of an immediate need for external financing.

World.title: CTP delivers 3,000 sqm of built-to-suit temperature-controlled warehousing in Bucharest
World.content:
Developer and operator of logistics and industrial real estate CTP has delivered nearly 3,000 sqm of built-to-suit temperature-controlled warehouse space to Frigonet Logistics at CTPark Bucharest South, according to a press release published on Friday, August 28.

Frigonet Logistics provides integrated cold chain logistics services, including refrigerated warehousing and handling, national dual-temperature distribution for chilled and frozen goods, picking, and cross-docking. The company selected CTPark Bucharest South for its strategic location and excellent connectivity to Bucharest and key regional hubs, enabling more efficient distribution routes and supporting the continued expansion of its operations.

Frigonet Logistics has signed a long-term lease for its new facility, which it will use to expand its temperature-controlled storage operations for refrigerated and frozen food products, supporting its growing logistics network across Romania.

CTPark Bucharest South is strategically located with direct access to Bucharest’s ring road and major national transport corridors, providing excellent connectivity to the capital, the A0, A1 and A2 motorways, and key destinations across Romania and Southeastern Europe. The park comprises nearly 140,000 sqm of built space across a nearly 37-hectare site.

“Beyond the operational advantages, the location at CTPark Bucharest South provides excellent connectivity to Bucharest and our key regional hubs, helping us optimise distribution routes and improve logistics efficiency. This investment gives us the capacity and flexibility required to support our continued growth and to provide our customers with temperature-controlled transport and logistics services that meet the highest standards,” explained David Stoian, Executive Director of Frigonet Logistics.

The facility incorporates dedicated frozen storage operating at -20°C, a 0-4°C buffer area, a refrigeration plant, and the infrastructure required to safely handle and store temperature- sensitive products while maintaining an uninterrupted cold chain.

“We are pleased to welcome Frigonet Logistics to CTPark Bucharest South and to support the company’s next stage of expansion,” said Cristina Manea, Business Developer at CTP in Romania.

World.title: Mastering the Music Business brings over 100 speakers to Bucharest
World.content:
The 11th edition of the Mastering the Music Business (MMB) conference will take place at Hotel Caro in Bucharest from September 1 to 3. More than 100 speakers from 16 countries will participate in 27 panels, workshops, and discussions on building careers in the music industry.

The lineup includes Romanian artists and industry figures such as Grasu XXL, Nicole Cherry, Marius Moga, AFO, Bean of Subcarpați, and television host Cătălin Măruță, who also manages singer Andra.

They will be joined by professionals representing European festivals, booking agencies, record labels, and music organizations. Speakers include European Music Exporters Exchange president Corinne Sadki, ESNS junior booker Janneke de Boer, SoAlive Music Conference founder Ruth Koleva, Music Glue business development head Marion Sosnowicz, and Future Echoes festival director Peter Åstedt.

For the first time, the conference will host representatives of music export offices from 11 European countries: Poland, Latvia, Lithuania, Switzerland, Belgium, France, Italy, Ukraine, Austria, Greece, and Germany. Discussions will focus on festivals, touring, and the professional networks that could help Romanian artists reach European markets.

The program will cover topics including artificial intelligence in the creative process, independent music economics, ticket fraud, songwriting, artist selection by European bookers, mental health, fan communities, copyright, and crisis management.

AFO and Bean will discuss Subcarpați’s development on the opening day, while Marius Moga will participate in a panel about how brands choose music projects. The final day will feature a conversation with Măruță about managing Andra and a keynote address by Grasu XXL.

The conference will also include three small-group accelerators focusing on music marketing, booking, and music business fundamentals. They are open to ticket holders through separate registration, subject to availability.

Each conference day will be followed by concerts at Club Expirat as part of the MMB Showcase Festival. Twelve acts from Romania and elsewhere in Europe will perform during the three evenings, with admission free, subject to venue capacity.

World.title: Romania’s population drop slowed by migration but still ongoing
World.content:
Romania’s resident population reached 19.041 million people on January 1, 2026, 1,829 fewer than a year earlier, according to provisional data published Friday, August 28, by the National Institute of Statistics.

The decline was largely limited by migration. The number of immigrants exceeded that of emigrants by 102,200, but the difference did not fully offset the natural decrease of 104,100 people.

Overall, the positive international migration balance increased compared with previous years and covered almost the entire difference between the number of deaths and the number of births.

Among people who left Romania, men accounted for 57.9% of the total. They were also the majority among those who came to the country, with a share of 58.6%.

The urban population reached 9.792 million people at the beginning of 2026, up 0.2% from the same period in 2025. The female population stood at 9.744 million people, down 0.1%.

Beyond the decrease in the number of inhabitants, INS data indicate an intensification of demographic aging. People aged at least 65 accounted for 20.5% of the population on January 1, 2026, compared with 20.3% a year earlier. At the same time, the share of children aged 0 to 14 fell from 15.4% to 15.1%.

The demographic aging index therefore rose from 131.3 to 135.9 elderly people for every 100 young people. In other words, at the beginning of 2026, Romania had almost 136 people aged at least 65 for every 100 children under 15. The demographic dependency ratio fell slightly, from 55.6 to 55.2 young and elderly people for every 100 working-age adults.

INS included foreign citizens in the resident population, as well as stateless people, who usually live in Romania for a period of at least 12 months. During the war in Ukraine, the statistics also include Ukrainian citizens benefiting from temporary protection in Romania.

World.title: Tour of Romania brings together 23 cycling teams from 16 countries
World.content:
The 2026 Tour of Romania will bring together approximately 150 cyclists from 23 teams representing 16 countries between September 9 and 13. Italian Olympic champion Elia Viviani will also attend the race as manager of Italy’s national team.

The five-stage competition will cover more than 800 kilometers, beginning in Chișinău, Moldova, and ending with a final circuit in Bucharest. This will be the first edition of the race to start outside Romania.

“The presence of 23 teams from 16 countries confirms the growing interest in the Tour of Romania,” Romanian Cycling Federation president Cătălin Sprinceană said. “We are pleased that the public will be able to see athletes from so many countries at the start.”

The lineup includes ten UCI continental teams, eight club teams, and five national teams. The participating countries are Albania, Austria, Belgium, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Greece, Hungary, Italy, Moldova, Monaco, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Romania, Turkey, and the United States.

The national teams of Romania, Italy, Moldova, Albania, and Bosnia and Herzegovina will compete in the race.

Elia Viviani won the Olympic omnium title at Rio 2016 and is a three-time Olympic medalist and three-time track world champion. He has also won stages in all three Grand Tours and claimed the European road race title in 2019. After a 16-year professional career, the Italian cyclist is beginning a new role as manager of his country’s national team.

The participating teams will be officially presented in Chișinău on September 8. The first stage, from Chișinău to Ungheni, will take place the following day.

The race will then continue in Romania with stages from Iași to Piatra Neamț on September 10, Piatra Neamț to Băile Balvanyos on September 11, and Brașov to Ploiești on September 12. The final stage will be held on a circuit in Bucharest on September 13.

The race will be broadcast live by Prima Sport and on the official Tour of Romania and Auchan Romania Facebook pages, while TVR Sport will air daily highlights. Further details can be found here.

World.title: NASA Space Apps Challenge opens registration for Bucharest, Cluj-Napoca events
World.content:
NASA Space Apps Challenge, the world’s largest hackathon, will return to Romania on November 14-15, with simultaneous events in Bucharest and Cluj-Napoca. Registration for the 48-hour international event is open until November 13.

Under the theme The Next Frontier!, participants will form teams of up to six members and use NASA’s open data to develop solutions to challenges related to Earth and space exploration. The challenges will be announced on September 17.

The competition is open to programmers, scientists, engineers, designers, students, storytelling specialists, and other people interested in technology and innovation, regardless of their age, experience, or professional background.

“Romania has people with ideas and skills who can compete at the highest international level, and this competition is an extraordinary opportunity to bring them together and connect them to one of the most innovative global communities,” said Diana Iosu, founder of DiFine PR and organizer of the Bucharest edition.

The Bucharest event will be held at the Romanian-American University, while the Cluj-Napoca competition will take place at ClujHUB. Registration for Bucharest is available here, and for Cluj here.

Two winning teams will be selected from each city to advance to the global competition and compete against thousands of teams worldwide. Global winners will be invited to visit a NASA center or facility, attend an event celebrating their projects, and meet representatives of the US space agency.

Participants will also receive free access to the Google AI Professional Certificate course offered through Coursera.

People under 18 may participate only with the consent of a parent or legal guardian, who must accompany them throughout the event.

The 2025 edition attracted 200 registrations in Romania. Winning projects included an algorithm assessing the environmental effects of business decisions, a visual platform for learning about physics and astrophysics, and an AI solution that converted air-quality data into real-time information.

Launched globally in 2012, the NASA Space Apps Challenge has brought together more than 487,000 participants from 190 countries and territories. The Romanian editions are organized by ROTSA and DiFine PR.

World.title: IKEA opens first Plan and Order Point in Iași
World.content:
IKEA will open its first Plan and Order Point in Iași on Monday, August 31. Located in Egros Shopping Center, the studio will be the retailer’s sixth such facility in Romania.

The location will offer personalized planning services for kitchens, wardrobes, and storage solutions. Customers will be able to work individually with IKEA specialists to select configurations, products, and finishes suited to their homes and budgets, the company said.

The studio will feature three kitchen layouts, three wardrobe solutions, two planning desks, and more than 1,400 IKEA products. Around 50 everyday products will also be available to purchase directly.

Customers can collect their orders free of charge from the location, arrange home delivery, or use another IKEA pick-up point. Furniture assembly services will also be available.

The new facility replaces IKEA’s existing pick-up point at Egros Shopping Center, with collection services integrated into the expanded format.

IKEA opened its first Romanian Plan and Order Point in Constanța in 2024. More than 4,500 planning sessions have since taken place across its locations over the past year, with kitchens attracting the most interest.

The company’s other Plan and Order Points operate in Constanța, Bucharest, Cluj-Napoca, and Brașov.
