World.title: US dollar exchange rate drops against Iraqi dinar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar experienced a decline on Sunday in both Baghdad, the capital of Iraq, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate dropped in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,537.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,540 Iraqi dinars on Sunday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,542.5 Iraqi dinars and 1,532.5 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate fell, fluctuating between 1,537.5 and 1,537 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq’s central bank freezes assets of senior officials in anti-graft sweep
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) has ordered the immediate freeze of moveable and immovable assets for political figures, parliamentarians, and former officials as part of a comprehensive judicial anti-graft effort.

Following security operations, the CBI asked all licensed commercial banks to restrict transaction flows, confiscate properties, and disclose accounts associated with the targeted individuals in accordance with Anti-Corruption Investigative Court guidelines.

Financial institutions must compare client account activity to official monthly government salaries to identify abrupt asset increases or excessive wealth buildup.

Monitoring procedures apply directly to bank accounts held by spouses, intimate family members, and close business partners to prohibit the use of third-party front businesses for asset concealment.

This step is part of a countrywide anti-graft campaign led by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government. The campaign, known as “Operation Dawn,” aims to expose deeply rooted financial corruption among Iraq’s crucial ministries.

The Iraqi prime minister’s legal advisor, Munir Haddad, revealed in early July that more than $2 trillion have been stolen from Iraq since 2003.

According to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Haddad stated that the number of suspects continues to increase as investigations with the arrested ones are ongoing.

The countrywide anti-corruption campaign resulted in the arrests of several lawmakers and senior officials, as well as the recovery of millions of dollars, gold, luxurious cars, and real estate.

World.title: Iraq to speed up construction of strategic oil pipeline network
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi stated on Saturday that the oil export pipeline project is important to the country since it would diversify export routes and increase export capacity.

During a meeting with senior officials in the oil industry and representatives from the project’s implementation company, al-Zaidi emphasized the importance of moving quickly with the implementation of the oil pipeline network, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

Al-Zaidi directed the Oil Ministry to provide the best possible conditions for the implementing companies to ensure the project’s completion according to the highest standards as it serves Iraq’s economic and developmental interests.

The prime minister reviewed the project’s technical and economic specifics, as well as its long-term developmental implications, export routes, and estimated oil quantities through the Basra-Haditha-Fishkhabur and Haditha-Baniyas pipelines.

Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair met last week with officials from Qatar’s UCC Holding in Baghdad to discuss the oil pipeline projects that aim to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

The discussions addressed establishing technical frameworks, project schedules, and contractual structures for the Basra-Haditha-Fishkhabur pipeline to Turkey and the Haditha-Baniyas pipeline to Syria.

Iraq is prioritizing this oil pipeline network to build alternate export routes to the Mediterranean to minimize its longstanding vulnerability and reliance on maritime shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

Qatar-based UCC Holding is leading the consortium that includes Chevron, TI Capital, and TotalEnergies to carry out the project.

The project is a network of pipelines that will be extended to the Turkish port of Ceyhan and the Syrian port of Baniyas, providing two additional outlets to enhance export flexibility.

The Basra-Haditha pipeline project is an Iraqi venture estimated at $4.6 billion aiming to transport crude oil from the southern Iraqi province of Basra to Haditha in the western Iraqi province of Anbar.

Reaching Haditha opens up three distinct offshore export routes: the Turkish port of Ceyhan, the Syrian port of Baniyas, and Jordan’s port of Aqaba.

Iraq’s proposed oil pipeline network indicates an anticipatory initiative to lessen reliance on Gulf maritime routes, which are prone to interruptions.

World.title: Iraq’s foreign reserves hit $79.2 billion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The financial adviser to Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, Mazhar Saleh, confirmed on Sunday that Iraq’s foreign reserves remain at relatively safe levels.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated Iraq’s total reserves at approximately $79.2 billion for 2026, according to Saleh.

The reserve efficiency index considers covering more than six months’ worth of imports to be a generally safe level.

According to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), the reduction in reserves this year needs more care, not because they have reached a critical level, but because there is worry that the loss will continue and negatively impact the safety buffer in the future.

Foreign reserves play a crucial role in maintaining the stability of the Iraqi dinar’s exchange rate and protecting against pressures on the national currency. The capacity of the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) to meet the genuine demand for US dollars is essential for ensuring economic stability and growth.

The heavy dependence on oil revenue is one of the most apparent sources of risk. A decline in oil revenues leads to lower government revenues and reduced foreign currency inflows, which further strains reserves and undermines exchange rate stability.

Saleh emphasized the need to maintain the CBI’s monetary policy independence and not to use foreign reserves to finance the budget deficit, as these measures may lead to reserve depletion and a spike in inflation.

World.title: New intellectual biography explores life and legacy of Iraqi sociologist Ali Al Wardi
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A new intellectual biography examining the life and critical scholarship of Iraq’s founding father of sociology, Ali Al-Wardi, has been released by the American University of Iraq, Baghdad (AUIB) Press.

Authored by Iraqi philosopher and translator Ali Hakim Saleh, the 300-page volume—titled Ali Al-Wardi: An Intellectual and Social Biography — traces Al-Wardi’s transformation into an urban modern intellectual (effendi), his systemic deconstruction of official state narratives, and the subsequent censorship and institutional marginalization he faced.

The biography structures Al-Wardi’s life and academic legacy across several defining phases:

The Rise of the “Effendi” and the Public Intellectual: Tracing Al-Wardi’s emergence from traditional quarters to Western academia (earning his Ph.D. from the University of Texas at Austin in 1950) and his creation of a broad reading public outside elite scholarly circles.

Theorizing the Iraqi Persona: Examining his foundational sociological frameworks, notably the dialectic between nomadism (Badawa) and urban civilization (Hadara), and the concept of psychological duality (Izdawajiyya) within Iraqi society.

Direct Critique of Political Power: Analyzing Al-Wardi’s rigorous critique of state structures and his disruption of official historiography, most prominently captured in his multi-volume opus, Social Glimpses from Modern Iraqi History.

State Friction, Censorship, and Disillusionment: Documenting the political suppression, academic sidelining, and personal disillusionment that followed his confrontation with authoritarian state narratives.

The publication has generated significant interest across Iraqi cultural and academic circles. Prominent author and University of Basra professor Louay Hamza Abbas praised the work as a major cultural milestone:

World.title: U.S. crude oil imports from Iraq drop to zero
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Official data released by the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) on Sunday, August 30, 2026, shows that United States imports of Iraqi crude oil fell back to zero barrels per day (bpd) during the past week, down from an average of 6,000 bpd recorded the previous week.

The fluctuation follows an extended summer lull where direct crude shipments from Iraq to U.S. refiners remained largely suspended amid ongoing maritime transit adjustments in the Gulf.

Canada maintained its dominant position as the primary foreign crude supplier to American refineries, while Latin American and West African exporters filled the bulk of remaining import volume:

Rank Exporter Country Volume (bpd) 1 Canada 3,526,000 2 Venezuela 662,000 3 Brazil 348,000 4 Mexico 196,000 5 Saudi Arabia 165,000 6 Colombia 141,000 7 Libya 89,000 8 Nigeria 50,000 — Iraq 0 — Ecuador 0

Note: The EIA recorded zero crude imports during the same reporting week from Algeria, Angola, Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Kuwait, Norway, Russia, Trinidad and Tobago, and the United Kingdom.

World.title: Iraq recovers 1.35T dinars in anti-corruption drive
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi federal government has successfully recovered public funds, financial assets, and real estate valued at over 1.359 trillion IQD (approximately $1.04 billion) during its anti-corruption campaign, “Sawlat al-Fajr” (Dawn Assault), government spokesperson Haider Al-Aboudi announced on Saturday, August 29, 2026.

In a statement delivered to Al Iraqiya News and reported by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Al-Aboudi revealed that the Federal Commission of Integrity has received more than 26,000 formal corruption reports, reflecting heightened institutional activity and public reporting.

Key Operational Milestones & Asset Recovery Figures

Total Asset Value Recovered: Surpassed 1.359 trillion IQD in seized liquid funds, frozen financial instruments, and confiscated real estate properties.

Integrity Commission Reports: Over 26,000 tips and corruption filings registered with the Federal Commission of Integrity during the ongoing enforcement phase.

Whistleblower Financial Incentives: In accordance with the Informants Law (قانون مكافأة المخبرين), individuals who submit verified information leading directly to the recovery of stolen public funds are entitled to financial rewards of up to 5% of the total recovered sum.

Al-Aboudi outlined that the government’s anti-corruption strategy balances punitive judicial enforcement with systemic preventive reforms:

Judicial Safeguards: Emphasized that the Iraqi judiciary stands as the core guarantor supporting the legitimacy, evidence verification, and success of anti-corruption actions.

Direct Prime Ministerial Oversight: Highlighted the Prime Minister’s recent field visit to the Commission of Integrity, confirming direct executive backing for specialized investigative judges and investigators.

Preemptive Contract Auditing: Instituting mandatory advance audits on high-value public procurement contracts to identify irregularities before fund disbursements take place.

Digital Transformation and Automation: Accelerating the digitization of state transactions and public registries to minimize arbitrary human interference, extortion, and bribery opportunities across ministries.

Al-Aboudi characterized systemic corruption as a deeply entrenched web linking financial schemes, administrative loopholes, and political influence that drains public wealth and stalls infrastructure projects.

He reiterated that there will be no halt or political compromise in the government’s anti-corruption drive, noting that institutional transparency, automated governance, and aggressive asset recovery remain long-term priorities.

World.title: Sanad: Iraq targets simultaneous nationwide 5G rollout
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi federal government is actively working to coordinate a simultaneous rollout of next-generation 5G telecommunications services across all Iraqi governorates and the Kurdistan Region, Minister of Communications Mustafa Sanad announced on Saturday, August 29, 2026.

Speaking to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Sanad stated that existing technical and administrative differences between the federal ministry and the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) are manageable, emphasizing that bilateral discussions are progressing toward unified protocols.

Key Discussion Tracks & Technical Files

Synchronized 5G Commercial Launch: Noting that the Kurdistan Region had taken earlier exploratory steps toward 5G deployment, the federal ministry is coordinating with regional authorities to synchronize spectrum allocation and commercial launches nationwide.

Transit Fiber-Optic Backbone (Basra to Europe): Coordinating agreements regarding the strategic international transit fiber cable routed from Basra through the Kurdistan Region onward to European hubs, requiring unified commercial terms with operators operating in the region.

Unified International Representation: Sanad underscored Baghdad’s position that Iraq must engage as a unified entity before international telecommunications bodies and multilateral organizations, with the federal Ministry of Communications serving as the sovereign representative.

Regulatory Coordination & Operator Oversight: Addressing regulatory discrepancies stemming from the KRG’s direct ministerial oversight over regional mobile operators (including Korek Telecom), in contrast to the federal model where licensing and sector oversight are managed through an independent communications and media commission.

Sanad confirmed his intention to lead an official delegation to Erbil following a formal written invitation extended by KRG Prime Minister Masrour Barzani during Sanad’s first week in office, which was reaffirmed during a visit to Baghdad by the KRG Minister of Transport and Communications.

The upcoming ministerial meetings aim to finalize an integrated operational framework for cross-border fiber traffic, harmonize telecom licensing standards, and establish joint technical committees to oversee spectrum readiness for 5G network integration.

NHAI has made Automated and Intelligent Machine-Aided Construction compulsory for highway projects longer than 20 km (AI generated image)

NEW DELHI: National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has made Automated and Intelligent Machine-Aided Construction (AI-MC) compulsory for all highway projects longer than 20 km in length and costing over Rs 500 crore, in whatâs a move aimed at addressing quality issues, which have become a major concern for govt.As per an NHAI circular issued on Friday, contractors will have to use the AI-MC system while building the road from the ground up and continuously across the entire spatial footprint of the project. The technology will be used for every major layer of highway, including embankment (raised earth foundation), subgrade (compacted soil base) and Granular Sub-Base (GSB) â the first layer of crushed stone, sand and gravel laid over the compacted soil before the road surface is built.The move is aimed at improving construction quality and ensuring roads are built with greater accuracy and uniformity. AI-MC is a construction technology with on-board computers and sensors on heavy machinery such as graders, pavers, compactors and dozers. Deployment of AI-MC aims to improve the quality, durability and transparency of road construction by replacing manual monitoring with technology-driven, real-time execution and quality control.TOI has learnt that though AI-MC was first deployed during construction of Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway, it was not used on the entire stretch and at all grades.Officials said the move is designed to minimise human errors, ensure uniform construction standards and generate digital records of every stage of construction, from earthwork to pavement laying. âThe new norms make it mandatory to share real-time data with NHAI officials.This is good for contractors and for us as well. Once the contractor gets real-time data, there will be hardly any scope for sub-contractors to cut corners,â said an official.Some of the industry players in AI-MC segment said that contractors are reluctant to share real-time data with NHAI and other highway construction agencies as this makes them accountable. âUnless NHAI and other agencies get the data in real time, the impact of using the technology will be negligible. It must not be used in a piecemeal way if govt is serious about putting things in order,â said one of them.

World.title: 'Oldest trick in RSS playbook': Owaisi attacks Mohan Bhagwat over Hindu-Muslim remarks
World.content:

NEW DELHI: AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi on Sunday criticised RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat over his remarks on Hindu-Muslim unity, alleging that the RSS projects a different image of itself to the world while the writings of its key thinkers reflect a different view of minorities.Owaisi's remarks came a day after Bhagwat, speaking at at event in New York, said that a Hindu who believes Muslims should not live in India would not remain a Hindu.Reacting to the remarks, Owaisi said, âThis is the oldest trick in the RSS playbook: some words are for the world, and some are for its own members. The RSS has never disavowed its key thinkers and writers. What do they say about Muslims and other minorities?âOwaisi referred to a biography of RSS founder K B Hedgewar, published by the RSS, to claim that Hedgewar had opposed the Congress's emphasis on Hindu-Muslim unity.Quoting from the biography, Owaisi said, âGandhiji worked constantly with one eye on Hindu-Muslim unity... But Doctorji sensed danger in that move. In fact, he did not even relish the newfangled slogan of 'Hindu-Muslim Unity'.âThe AIMIM chief also cited former RSS chief M S Golwalkar's writings, referring to his book Bunch of Thoughts and its chapter titled 'Internal Threats'.âGolwalkar's 'Bunch of Thoughts' has a long chapter titled 'Internal Threats', in which Muslim and Christian citizens of India are described as threats number one and two, respectively,â Owaisi said.He also referred to Golwalkar's statement that the Sangh was âinspired by one flag (saffron), one leader and one ideologyâ.Owaisi alleged that the RSS did not contribute to India's freedom struggle and claimed that Hedgewar left the Congress because he opposed the participation of different religious communities in the anti-British movement led by Mahatma Gandhi.Owaisi also invoked the 2002 Gujarat riots while criticising the RSS, asking, âShould we forget what happened to the Muslims of Gujarat under the RSS's proxy rule?âHe alleged that Muslims and Christians continued to face discrimination and claimed that Muslims were being subjected to Hindu law in the name of the Uniform Civil Code, while Christians were being targeted through âdraconianâ anti-conversion laws.The AIMIM chief also raised concerns over the alleged misuse of laws such as the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).Earlier on Saturday, addressing the âOne World One Humanityâ event in New York, Bhagwat said different religions may follow different paths, but humanity and truth remain one. âWe come from a society that believes humanity is one,â he said.âIf any Hindu thinks that there should be no Muslim in Bharat, he will not remain Hindu. If you want to call yourself Hindu, you must believe that all paths are leading to the same goal and that every human has dignity. There is no difference between human beings,â Bhagwat had added.Bhagwat also used the occasion to speak about perceptions of the RSS. He said the organisation was often viewed through narratives that, in his view, did not reflect its work on the ground."There are many perceptions created by wrong narratives. But when you come and see us from inside, all those will be disbelieved in the day."The RSS chief was speaking in New York as he began a three-nation global outreach tour covering the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom. The visit has been organised as part of the organisation's centenary year celebrations, following invitations from overseas local organisations.

World.title: IISc eco-friendly foam moves from lab to market; TOI story drew industry
World.content:
BENGALURU: An eco-friendly bio-based foam developed by researchers at the Indian Institute of Science (

), is moving from the laboratory towards commercialisation, with Absolute Cold LLP working on its use in cold-chain and temperature-controlled packaging.

The foam, developed by Prof Suryasarathi Bose and Prof Subodh Kumar, along with the team comprising Sampath Parasuram, Akshay Sunil Salvi, Supriya H, Sandeep Kumar Singh and Amit Malakar, is an alternative to conventional polyurethane (PU) foam, which is widely used for insulation but is difficult to recycle after use.

The IISc material was designed to combine the properties needed for insulation with a more sustainable approach to what happens to the material at the end of its life.

The journey from laboratory to industry also had a link to TOI.

Bose said a report on the development published by TOI on Nov 11, 2024, helped bring a potential industry partner on board. âYour [TOI] article brought in a potential licensee on board and helped take the technology to market. Absolute Cold director saw your story and reached out to us,â he said.

The original IISc work involved making the foam using epoxidised fatty acids derived from non-edible oils and polyphenol-based materials derived from tea leaves.





The researchers also incorporated a chemical structure that allows the material to be reprocessed, rather than simply being discarded after use.

Absolute Cold, which works in the cold-chain and temperature-controlled logistics sector, subsequently became interested in the technology. The company is now working towards translating the laboratory material into a product for applications where maintaining temperature during storage and transport is critical.

This could include packaging used to transport pharmaceuticals and other temperature-sensitive products. Such packaging needs to provide insulation while also being lightweight and strong enough to withstand handling and transportation. Its environmental impact after use is an increasing consideration as well.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The move is the latest step in Boseâs broader work on more sustainable polymeric materials. His research has included efforts to find ways of reusing or upcycling plastics that are otherwise difficult to recycle, with the aim of keeping materials in use for longer rather than sending them to waste.

For IISc, the foam's progress also shows the less visible part of academic innovation: getting a material developed in a laboratory into a form that industry can manufacture and customers can use. The licensing and scale-up process can require changes to the formulation, manufacturing process and product design even after the underlying research has been demonstrated.

The next test, therefore, is whether the foam can be produced at commercial scale while retaining the insulation, strength and durability demonstrated during development. Its performance in actual cold-chain applications will ultimately determine whether the IISc innovation can become a practical alternative to conventional foams.

For a material conceived around the problem of what happens to foam after its useful life, that commercial journey is as important as the laboratory breakthrough itself.

Addressing an event in Lucknow, CM Yogi Adityanath said, "There are narrow lanes, but Lucknow also has smart roads and roads developed under the CM Grid scheme. Alongside the narrow streets, Lucknow has also received an outer ring road, similar to the Kisan Path. If Lucknow has the heritage of Uda Devi Pasi and Maharaja Bijli Pasi, it has also emerged as a centre for modern defence technologies such as BrahMos missiles, contributing to India's defence needs and self-reliance.

"

World.title: U.S. forces strike Iranian rocket launchers on the Strait of Hormuz in first military action in weeks
World.content:
U.S. forces have struck Iranian rocket launchers on the Strait of Hormuz in the first military action in a month, a U.S. official said Sunday.

Semiofficial news outlets in Iran reported sounds of explosions near Larak island on the strait.

Forces with the Revolutionary Guard Corps were observed preparing to launch rockets with sea mines into the strait, according to the official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to detail sensitive military movements.

The U.S. military last week completed clearing sea mines from the strait’s international shipping routes.

World.title: Should the CJP be a political party?
World.content:
A glimpse at India’s recent history suggests that while some protest movements became successful political parties, others did not. The success of the recent youth movement started by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) should not be judged by whether it would become a successful political party nor by its forcing the former Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign. Rather, the success of the CJP movement should be judged by the enthusiastic participation of young students for a cause which concerned them; the success of which has raised confidence in them.

They now believe that they can make the government hear their voices even if it is raised from a non-political platform.

Movements to parties

Very often the success of a movement is judged by not only what the movement was able to achieve but whether it was able to become a successful political party or not. The 1979 student’s agitation in Assam led by the All Assam Students Union transformed into a successful political party, the Asom Gana Parishad (AGP), which formed the government in 1985 in Assam. The India against corruption movement also transformed into a political party — the Aam Adami Party (AAP) which came to power in Delhi for the first time in 2013. Not only did the India against corruption movement draw large support, the AAP also enjoyed massive electoral gains; it won 67 and 62 seats out of a total of 70 Assembly seats in Delhi with a 54.3% and 53.5% vote share during the 2015 and 2020 Assembly elections respectively.

The AAP also formed a government in Punjab in 2022.

In the success story of both the AGP and AAP, the youth played an important role. During the 2015 Assembly elections, the AAP’s vote share among young voters (18-22 years of age) was 63%, almost 10% higher compared to its average vote share. The AAP went on to draw 60% of the votes among young voters (18-22 years) during the 2020 Assembly elections as well — 7% higher compared to its average vote share.

If the CJP does turn into a political party, there is hardly any doubt that the new party will attract young voters, as has been the case with other newly formed parties. The newly formed Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), led by actor-turned politician C. Joseph Vijay, formed the government in Tamil Nadu in the very first election it contested in 2026, replacing the two established formations mainly the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam. The youth played a very important role in the victory of the TVK. While the overall vote share of the TVK was 34.9%, its share among young voters (18-22) was significant at nearly 70%.

Nationally, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has an advantage among young voters, its vote share being 4% higher amongst voters in the age group of 18-22 years. Therefore, the rise of the CJP may affect the BJP more than any other party.

But the question remains, can the CJP attract young voters across the country?

Strong challengers

There have also been successful social movements which have failed as political parties. The movement for a separate State of Uttarakhand resulted in the formation of a new State and a new political party, the Uttarakhand Kranti Dal (UKD). However, it failed to make an electoral impact. During the 2002 election, which was the first election held after the formation of Uttarakhand, the UKD polled only 5.4% votes and won just four Assembly seats. There have been similar groups which have led protest movements, demanding Statehood and the like, but most of them could not become successful political parties.

However, there have been movements led by the youth, with the participation of larger social communities, which resulted in a change of the national government. The Jayaprakash Narayan led anti-emergency movement of 1977 dethroned the powerful Indira Gandhi-led government. Similarly, the anti-corruption movement led by Anna Hazare contributed to the defeat of the Congress-led coalition government in 2014.

It should be of no concern whether the CJP becomes a political party or not as the movement has already been able to achieve some noticeable milestones. It emphasised that issues take importance and not leaders as this movement was largely leaderless without the active support of any political party.

It also gave a large number of people the hope that their voices can be heard if they come together in a sustained manner.

Sanjay Kumar is Professor and election analyst. Views expressed are personal.

World.title: Boy ‘assaulted’ at day care in Delhi; principal, 3 others booked under POCSO; 1 arrested
World.content:
The Delhi police on Sunday arrested an employee of a private day care and playschool in north-east Delhi’s Jaffrabad, two days after the father of a three-year-old boy filed a complaint alleging that the child had been physically assaulted and sexually harassed at the facility, a senior police officer said.

A case was registered against the staff member, the school director, the principal and a teacher on August 28 under Sections 115(2) and 126(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Sections 75 and 82 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, and Section 12 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Efforts are under way to arrest the other three accused, the officer said, adding, “Appropriate legal action will be taken after reviewing the CCTV footage and other evidence.”

According to the father’s complaint, the child had been refusing to go to school for several days and was having difficulty using the washroom. On August 18, he began vomiting, following which his parents took him to an ENT specialist, who found severe swelling in both his eardrums. “The doctor said he had been beaten. We asked the facility to give us access to the CCTV footage. The school director made us pay ₹1,500 to access it,” the father stated in the complaint.

The CCTV footage from August 16 to 18, which the father received on August 25, purportedly showed the child being tied to a chair, slapped, having his ears pulled and the chair being kicked by the teacher and the support staff member.

“This was happening inside the classroom where all the other children were present. During playtime, when the other children were playing, he was always kept with the teachers, tied to the chair,” the father told The Hindu, adding, “He is still having difficulty hearing.”

On August 27, the child was medically examined at GTB Hospital. The medico-legal case (MLC) report recorded “physical assault” and noted swelling on his left thigh and an abrasion near his left eye.

‘School ignored abuse’

The father said when he confronted the school director, he was told, “Aise to bachche roz pit te hain (Children are beaten like this every day).”

“I could only access the footage for three days. I don’t know for how long they had been torturing my child like this,” the father said. “He immediately starts crying at the mention of using the washroom,” he added.

World.title: 100 acres freed from legacy waste at three landfill sites, says Delhi Chief Minister
World.content:
Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta has said her government has taken several scientific measures to tackle the Capital’s legacy waste problem and reclaimed approximately 100 acres across the Okhla, Bhalswa and Ghazipur landfill sites so far.

She said 70 lakh metric tonnes of waste had been processed at the Okhla landfill and about 35 acres reclaimed. At Bhalswa, 102 lakh metric tonnes had been processed and about 45 acres reclaimed, while at Ghazipur, 44 lakh metric tonnes had been processed and about 20 acres reclaimed.

The inert material generated during waste processing is being used for road construction and to fill low-lying areas, the Chief Minister said. “The lifestyle of those who live around it has improved and property rates in the area surrounding the landfills have also gone up,” Ms. Gupta said in a video.

To prevent garbage from piling up again, the government is introducing four new waste-to-energy plants to ensure that waste generated in the city is processed immediately, she said.

The Okhla and Bhalswa landfills have a December 2026 deadline for clearance, while the Municipal Corporation of Delhi aims to clear the Ghazipur landfill by the end of 2027, Delhi Mayor Pravesh Wahi had announced last month.

Development works

The Chief Minister also announced a series of works to mark Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday on September 17, covering sanitation, water and sewerage systems, traffic, education, power and civic facilities.

“Our government is resolved to ensure that the benefits of development reach every area and every section of Delhi,” Ms. Gupta said.

World.title: State of exception: On India, the UN CERD report
World.content:
In its first review by the U.N. Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination (CERD) since 2007, India has elicited an expression of “grave concern” about reports of the law enforcement apparatus resorting to violence — physical and otherwise — against minority ethnic and ethno-religious groups, Dalits, and non-citizens over the years. The Committee also noted that India, which ratified the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination in 1968, has not provided detailed and updated information about the state’s inquiries and sanctions arising from allegations of such violence. While the government has told CERD that caste bias falls outside Article 1 of the convention because caste is not synonymous with race, CERD has allowed all forms of discrimination based on inherited status. The Committee’s concerns also span the practice of manual cleaning of sewers despite a law banning it; hate speech against, poor living conditions of, and the mass refoulement of Rohingya Muslims; the mass deprivation of citizenship via the National Register of Citizens; large-scale deletions from the Special Intensive Revisions of electoral rolls; the government’s use of the FCRA, UAPA, AFSPA, and PMLA instruments to hamper the work of civil society organisations; the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita not expressly criminalising racist hate speech; and the Forest (Conservation) Amendment Act exempting “national security” projects from consultative decision-making.

Given these issues and the fragmented recourse available, the lack of suitably disaggregated data on disenfranchised communities, including due to a much-delayed Census and the slow release of NCRB data, has transcended the bounds of administrative lethargy to actively impeding independent checks of India’s claims about fighting caste- and faith-based discrimination. In fact, India has been implementing “special measures” based on 2011 Census data, which could mask a regression in the socioeconomic status of Scheduled Tribes and Adivasis. Together with the Global Alliance of National Human Rights Institutions recommending the downgrade of the NHRC last year, following the government appointing police officers to investigative roles and a lack of pluralism, CERD is effectively stepping into a vacuum. The road ahead remains clear, from restoring the NHRC’s independence and criminalising hate speech to supportive affirmative action, collecting and publishing disaggregated data, and improving the transparency of the electoral roll revisions, and strengthening enforcement overall. But if the government’s attempted use of a technicality to keep the issues of 200 million Dalits a “domestic matter” and avoid international accountability — and its dismissal of CERD’s concerns as politically motivated — is any guide, the task continues to fall to civil society to exert influence in multilateral fora and sustain political, legal, and administrative resistance to government choices that normalise India’s sadly widespread culture of discrimination of all sorts.

World.title: Congress will quit Vijay Cabinet if Rahul is not accepted as PM candidate, says Minister
World.content:
Tamil Nadu Tourism Minister S. Rajesh Kumar on Sunday (August 30, 2026) warned that he and his Congress colleague Viswanathan (Higher Education Minister) will quit the C. Joseph Vijay-led Cabinet if the TVK continued to push the narrative projecting Mr. Vijay as a Prime Minister candidate for the 2029 parliamentary elections.

“If Mr. Rahul Gandhi [Congress leader] is not accepted (by the TVK) as the Prime Minister candidate of the 2029 Parliamentary election, both the Congress Ministers in the Tamil Nadu Government will immediately resign their posts and pull out from the Cabinet,” Mr Rajesh Kumar said while addressing in a party meeting held at Marthandam on Sunday (August 30) night.

Also Read | Congress will return to power at Centre in 2029, says K.C. Venugopal

Mr. Kumar said the Congress was gaining popularity among the people from all walks of life after Mr. Gandhi was relentlessly fighting against the Narendra Modi-led BJP Government and its “anarchic anti-people and anti-youth policies”. He had been accepted as the Prime Minister candidate by the voters across the nation and the Congress.

Also Read | Rahul Gandhi seeks FIR over ‘purification’ ritual in Haldwani after Kharge’s address, calls it ‘untouchability’

“If the TVK takes a contradictory decision that it would not accept Mr. Gandhi as the Prime Minister candidate, the two Congress Ministers in the Tamil Nadu Cabinet will immediately resign their post,” Mr. Kumar said amidst thunderous applause from the party cadres.

His warning comes against the backdrop of some TVK Ministers and functionaries openly seeking to present CM Vijay as the Prime Minister candidate.

World.title: Neelakurinji-like bloom adds charm to Kudremukh Hills
World.content:
Adding a distinctive charm to the beauty of the Western Ghats, a rare blue-violet flower resembling Neelakurinji has bloomed big along some trekking trails in the Kudremukh region of Chikkamagaluru district recently, attracting more trekkers and nature enthusiasts.

According to the Forest and Tourism Department officials, these flowers were seen in greater abundance in some of the hill regions of Kudremukh during 2022–23, earlier. They have appeared in limited numbers again this time. The blue-violet blooms scattered across the green hills are adding a unique attraction to the natural landscape of Kudremukh.

Sampath, owner of Namma Mane homestay near Kalasa in Chikkamagaluru, said that the bloom in 2022-23 had attracted big crowds to the region and they were expecting a similar jump in tourist traffic this season too.

Ram Prasath Manohar, Secretary, Tourism Department, said that the limited blooming of these blue-violet flowers in Kudremukh this year has generated special interest among trekking enthusiasts and nature tourists. “There is a need to present such natural phenomena through environmentally responsible tourism. Instructions have been given to the district Tourism Department officials to provide visitors with the necessary information, guidance and facilities without causing any harm to the flowers or their habitat,” he said.

He urged the visitors not to pluck the flowers and only watch them. “If they are plucked, then it disturbs the blooming cycle of these flowers. We have requested visitors not to damage the plants or litter the surroundings and help us preserve the natural environment,” Mr. Manohar said.

Tourism Minister K.J. George said blue-violet flowers like neelakurinji blooming in the hills of Kudremukh showcase the exceptional beauty of Karnataka’s natural wealth. “While visiting such natural attractions, tourists must adopt eco-friendly travel practices. Visitors should not only enjoy the beauty of nature but also understand their responsibility towards protecting it.”

World.title: Two held over hoax bomb threat in Kochi
World.content: The Kadavanthara police took two migrant workers from Idukki into custody on Sunday (August 30, 2026) following a hoax bomb threat. This followed a complaint from a woman who received the bomb threat over the phone late on Saturday (August 29, 2026) night.

World.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye to hold first meeting under Makkah pact in Istanbul on Monday
World.content:
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye will hold their first meeting under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in Istanbul on Monday, the Foreign Office (FO) confirmed.

In a statement, FO said the “inaugural meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee established under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (Makkah Accord)” will be held in the Turkish capital.

Pakistan will be represented at the meeting by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, and Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir.

The meeting will also be attended by the respective foreign and defence ministers, as well as the chiefs of general staff, of Turkiye and Saudi Arabia, according to FO.

“Pakistan’s participation in the meeting signifies Pakistan’s historic bonds of friendship with the brotherly countries of Turkiye and Saudi Arabia, as well as its desire for lasting regional peace and stability,” the statement highlighted.

Chief of the Army Staff Munir arrived “in Turkiye on an official visit”, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a brief statement issued in the evening.

In its statement, Turkiye said FM Hakan Fidan, Defence Minister Yasar Guler and Chief of Turkish General Staff Gen Selcuk Bayraktaroglu will participate in the meeting.

‘Continued strengthening’ of Pak-Turkiye ties

Earlier in the day, FM Dar reached Istanbul after concluding his visit to the United Kingdom.

He then held a meeting with FM Fidan, with both sides expressing “satisfaction at the continued strengthening and expansion of bilateral relations in the political, economic, security and cultural domains”, FO said on X.

The foreign ministers welcomed the progress achieved under the framework of the Pakistan–Türkiye High-Level Strategic Cooperation Council (HLSCC) and agreed on the early convening of its next session.

“The two sides also exchanged views on issues of regional and international importance and reaffirmed their commitment to continue working closely for regional peace and stability,” the statement read.

Special Secretary (United Nations) Nabeel Munir, Director General (UN) Umar Siddique, First Secretary Qazi Saleem, and Deputy Director to the Foreign Minister Agha Hunain also joined Dar for the meeting.

Upon his arrival in Istanbul, Dar was received by Turkish Deputy Chief of Staff for Administration Brig. General Senol Varol, Pakistan’s Ambassador to Turkiye Dr Yousaf Junaid, Ambassador Cihad Erginay of the Turkish foreign ministry, and other senior officials of the Turkish government, FO said.

The deputy premier later visited the shrine of Hazrat Abu Ayyub Ansari (RA) to pay his respects. He offered prayers for the peace and prosperity of Pakistan and its people, as well as for the Muslim community’s unity, FO said.

Earlier this month, Turkiye’s Fidan had also invited Dar to the Regional-4 meeting in Istanbul, which includes the three countries part of the defence pact, along with Egypt.

Dar had confirmed his participation in the meeting, which was scheduled to take place in August, FO had said.

The R-4 group has been focused on regional security and emerged in March amid efforts for mediation between the US and Iran.

The last R-4 meeting was held on August 5 in Amman, where the ministers “reaffirmed the importance of continued consultation and close coordination among the four countries in advancing regional stability”, according to FO.

Prior to that, a Cairo meeting held in June welcomed the signing of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding between the US and Iran. The first and second R-4 meetings — both held in March — took place in Riyadh and Islamabad, respectively.

UK visit wrapped up

In an earlier statement, FO said DPM Dar “concluded a successful official visit to the UK”.

During his trip, Dar met several officials, including UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, Minister of State for Pakistan Stephen Doughty, National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell, International Maritime Organisation (IMO) Secretary General Arsenio Dominguez and Commonwealth Secretary General Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey.

The deputy premier also interacted with British parliamentarians of Pakistani origin and the Pakistani diaspora in the UK.

World.title: Islamabad, Riyadh agree to boost Pakistani agri and food exports to $3bn
World.content:
Islamabad and Riyadh have agreed to boost Pakistani agricultural and food exports to Saudi Arabia up to $3 billion, the countries said in a joint statement on Sunday.

The statement, shared by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), said the agreement was reached after “successful” talks between Saudi Arabia’s agriculture ministry and Pakistan’s food security ministry, at the initiative of PM Shehbaz Sharif.

At the invitation of the Pakistani government, a Saudi delegation led by Minister of Environment, Water and Agriculture Engineer Abdulrahman Al-Fadley visited Islamabad from August 26 to August 28.

The delegation included senior officials from Riyadh’s Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture, the General Food Security Authority and other relevant institutions.

PM Shehbaz met the Saudi delegation and discussed potential areas of cooperation in detail, the joint statement said, referring to Friday’s meeting.

“The two countries expressed their shared commitment to increase Pakistan’s agricultural and food exports to Saudi Arabia to $3bn, with efforts to be made to achieve the target over the next two years,” it read.

“For this purpose, rice, red meat, fruits and their concentrates, green fodder and water-efficient agricultural technologies were identified as priority sectors in collaboration with the Saudi private sector.”

During the visit, the two sides held briefings on the Pakistan-Saudi Arabia Agriculture and Food Strategic Plan and meetings with the Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC), Fauji Foundation and the Pakistan-Saudi Arabia Agri-Business Forum.

The Saudi delegation also visited the National Agricultural Research Centre (NARC).

Reaffirming their deep and historic ties, the two sides highlighted the strong alignment between Saudi Arabia’s food security priorities under Vision 2030 and Pakistan’s agricultural and food export sector.

The delegations noted that Pakistan supplied around 169,000 tonnes of rice worth about $163 million to the Saudi market in 2025. The Saudi team expressed interest in further increasing bilateral rice trade in the coming years, according to the joint statement.

Furthermore, the Saudi delegation expressed interest in gradually doubling imports of red meat from Pakistan, as both sides reviewed Islamabad’s annual supply of around 30,000 tonnes of red meat worth approximately $167m.

Regarding fruits and fruit concentrates, the two sides highlighted significant potential to further increase Pakistan’s share of the Saudi market. They encouraged measures to facilitate business-to-business linkages and matchmaking between the private sectors of the two countries, as well as the mutual recognition of quality certifications.

The Saudi side identified green fodder as a promising area for expanding trade and establishing long-term supply partnerships, the joint statement said.

Both countries welcomed the successful completion of the first phase of a water-efficient irrigation programme in Punjab’s Bhakkar and expressed interest in a proposed second phase targeting small farmers.

The Saudi delegation also encouraged Pakistan to join the International Dates Council, a proposal welcomed by the Pakistani side.

The two sides also reviewed investment proposals put forward by Pakistan’s private sector in livestock, agri-food processing and the rice value chain, and agreed to maintain coordination to pursue cooperation in these areas.

“Both countries reaffirmed their broader strategic partnership,” the statement read.

Pakistan also welcomed an invitation to participate in the 43rd Saudi Agriculture Exhibition, scheduled to be held in Riyadh from October 19 to 22.

Both sides expressed satisfaction with the outcomes of the visit and agreed to maintain coordination to translate the understandings reached into practical cooperation.

The Pakistani delegation was led by Minister for National Food Security and Research Rana Tanveer Hussain and included its Secretary Aamir Ali Ahmed, Commerce Secretary Jawad Paul, PM’s Coordinator for Agriculture and Food Security Ahmed Umair, and private-sector representatives from Pakistan’s rice, red meat, processed food/fruit concentrate and green fodder sectors.

Prior to the Saudi delegation’s visit this week, Assistant Minister of Investment of Saudi Arabia Ibrahim Al-Mubarak had toured Islamabad in February, when he expressed interest in investing in corporate farming in Pakistan’s rice sector.

World.title: Trump says NBC journalist should face 'punishment' from broadcast regulator
World.content:
United States President Donald Trump on Sunday threatened a prominent NBC broadcast journalist with possible punishment by US media regulators as the Republican expressed disappointment with coverage of his candidate endorsements ahead of November’s midterm elections.

Trump took to his Truth Social platform to attack Kristen Welker as the “unpopular ‘hostess’ of the once great Meet the Press” talk show.

He objected to her having said the president had had “mixed results” on his endorsement of political candidates in party primaries, insisting the races had gone his way 98 per cent to 100pc of the time.

Welker, speaking early Sunday to a local NBC affiliate, said Trump would “loom large over these midterms”.

When it came to endorsements, she added, he “had some mixed results, but most recently, his pick of Senator Darline Graham… was successful in her primary battle”.

Trump, in his comments, said that “because of this purposeful inaccuracy, she will be reported to the FCC for rebuke or punishment”. The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) assigns and oversees licenses for radio and television broadcast frequencies.

“Unfortunately, she is not the only one,” he added. “The Radical Left News is going out of their way to harass, demean, and libel anything ‘TRUMP’.”

Welker is an award-winning journalist who earned bipartisan praise after moderating a 2020 presidential debate featuring Trump and Joe Biden, the Democrat who won that year’s election.

An NBC News spokesperson, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, defended Welker on Sunday, telling AFP that “Kristen is one of the best in the business and we stand by her”.

Billionaire Trump used American media to his advantage over the years as a provocative real estate developer in New York. But as president he dramatically turned against the press and what he called “fake news”.

He has sued several newspapers including the Wall Street Journal and New York Times, and ordered federal funding slashed for public media.

His administration has ramped up restrictions and attempts to intimidate journalists, and the FCC — headed by a close Trump associate — has pressured broadcasters to toe the line.

“I hope that Chairman Brendan Carr, and the fine people of his Commission, will take this Threat to our Country very seriously,” Trump said.

The latest attack is part of the Trump administration’s months-long offensive against media outlets it deems overly critical.

Such efforts are facing growing resistance from news organisations and major broadcast networks. Several of them have filed lawsuits against the FCC, arguing such pressure constitutes political retaliation that violates the First Amendment of the US Constitution, which protects freedom of speech.

Relations between Trump and Welker have been under pressure for months. In June, the president abruptly cut short an interview with her following a tense exchange, during which he grew irritated by Welker’s questioning, particularly on the war against Iran.

Experts argue the FCC lacks the legal authority to punish broadcasters or reporters for their viewpoints.

According to a 2025 paper by the Yale Journal on Regulation, the US Supreme Court has confirmed that US law “does not grant the FCC the power to ban controversial speech”.

World.title: England clinch series win over Pakistan with thumping 194-run victory in second Test
World.content:
Ollie Robinson led the way once more as England clinched a series win over Pakistan with a thumping 194-run win in the second Test at Lord’s on Sunday despite Saud Shakeel’s fine 97.

Pakistan were dismissed for 194, having been set an improbable victory target of 389, to give England an unbeatable 2-0 lead in a three-match series.

This was England’s first multi-match Test series win since a 2-1 success in New Zealand more than a year ago.

Robinson finished with figures of 4-24 in 14 overs following his sensational 4-11 in 13 during Pakistan’s meagre first-innings 110 all out.

The Sussex seamer produced a pair of double strikes Sunday either side of Shakeel and Shan Masood, checking England’s progress with a fourth-wicket partnership of 97.

Robinson took two wickets in four balls to leave the tourists 7-2, before express quick Jofra Archer dismissed Pakistan captain Babar Azam.

But from the dire position of 14-3 before lunch, Shakeel and fellow left-hander Masood kept England at bay.

Robinson, however, had Masood lbw from around the wicket for a gritty 26 off 72 balls, although it needed a review to reverse umpire Allahuddien Paleker’s original not out decision.

And 111-4 became 115-5 when Mohammad Rizwan was lbw to Robinson carelessly slogging across the line.

Shakeel, 78 not out at tea, went to 86 by hooking Tongue for six and, two balls later, another superb hook off another the fast bowler saw him into the 90s.

Shakeel pulled the fifth ball of the over to go to 96 only to hole out soon afterwards when he swung Tongue straight to Harry Brook at deep square leg.

A crestfallen Shakeel received a standing ovation from MCC members in the pavilion as he walked back in after the end of a 122-ball innings also featuring 13 fours.

Pakistan were now 169-7, although they were effectively eight wickets down with Imam-ul-Haq still sidelined by the calf problem, meaning he was unable to bat in Pakistan’s first innings.

Tongue then cemented his reputation for polishing off the tail by bowling Khurram Shahzad before ending the match when he had Mohammad Ali caught in the slips by Brook.

Pakistan had looked to Masood and Azan Awais to see off the new ball on a still seam-friendly pitch.

Awais, however, was lbw to Robinson and, three balls later, Abdullah Shafique was bowled for a duck by a superb delivery from the paceman that angled in and moved away late to hit off stump.

Archer’s brute of a bouncer then had Azam in a horrible flap, with the ball looping to Jordan Cox at second slip.

Abbas on the honours board at last

Earlier, Mohammad Abbas finally achieved a coveted place on the Lord’s honours boards with a return of 5-57 as England were dismissed for 208.

Cricketers who take at least five wickets in an innings or 10 in a match or score a century in a Test at Lord’s have their feats recorded on one of the honours boards in the home and away dressing rooms at the ‘Home of Cricket’.

Abbas, 36, had come close before with a trio of four-wicket hauls, including his 4-73 in England’s first-innings 290 of this match.

But he went one better Sunday after starting the day with 3-48.

Dan Lawrence had added just four runs to his overnight 50 not out when he was bowled by Abbas before the veteran seamer had Robinson edging to wicket-keeper Rizwan, who held a fine catch standing up to the stumps.

An elated Abbas was mobbed by his teammates before kissing the turf in celebration.

World.title: At least 8 die, more missing, as ferry capsizes off Northern Cyprus
World.content:
A passenger ferry capsized and sank off Northern Cyprus on Sunday, killing at least eight people and leaving more than a dozen missing, officials and media reports said, as police took the captain and seven crew members into custody.

Several rescued passengers told local media a blast had gone off at the bow of the ferry before it rolled over, and said the boat had an insufficient supply of life-vests.

The vessel capsized 6.5 kilometres off the coast of Cyprus, shortly after leaving a Northern Cyprus port bound for Turkiye’s mainland.

Images broadcast by Turkish television showed the upside-down ferry in the water, with people wearing life vests atop its orange hull.

“Some people had to jump without lifebuoys or life jackets,” one young man, Efe Multici, told CNN Turk. “It was literally a fight for survival.”

The ferry had been carrying a total of 267 people, according to authorities, of which 161 were rescued and taken to hospital and 76 have returned home.

The official Cypriot news agency TAK, however, said 17 were missing.

The ferry had departed from the Northern Cyprus port of Kyrenia — called Girne Kepuveia in Turkish — heading to the Turkish port of Tasucu.

Captain arrested

Unal Ustel, prime minister of the self-proclaimed Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC), said the ship’s captain and seven crew members had been arrested.

The TRNC, which is recognised only by Turkiye, controls the northern third of the island of Cyprus, which has been divided since 1974. The territory is served with regular air and sea links to Turkiye.

The TRNC’s transport minister Erhan Arikli said the ferry had “completely sunk to a depth of 514 metres (1,686 feet)”.

“Efforts to find the missing are continuing tirelessly,” Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said during a public ceremony. “We hope to receive positive news from these efforts.”

The TRNC is dependent on Turkiye, and Turkish Vice President Cevdet Yilmaz said on X: “We are providing all necessary assistance to the search and rescue operations.”

One rescued passenger who spoke of a blast on board told local TRNC television after he was taken back ashore: “The front part exploded, they tried to turn around. And the side windows blew out. The boat started taking on water.”

The man, aged in his 50s and not named, said he spent an hour and a half in the water before being rescued. He said many people had been inside the ferry when it started taking on water.

“Those who could, got out,” he said, adding that he saw the captain among the first to abandon ship “without organising anything”.

Another witness, in his thirties, corroborated reports of an explosion. He said he had reported water leaks to the captain.

“The seats started to float, the captain kept going, and the bow exploded,” he said.

Many inside

Many boats, including private ones, were involved in the rescue operation. Turkiye’s interior ministry said on X that six Turkish navy ships had also been dispatched.

“All necessary preparations are being made for a swift response from rescue and health services,” the TRNC’s health ministry said in a statement.

Hospitals in the territory had been alerted, to provide any needed medical attention, it added.

Pakistan extends condolences

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Deputy PM Ishaq Dar both said they were “deeply saddened by the tragic” incident in the Mediterranean Sea.

“I extend my heartfelt condolences to my dear brother President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, the Turkish government and the bereaved families,” PM Shehbaz wrote on X.

He prayed for the swift and safe recovery of those missing, affirming that the people of Pakistan stood in solidarity with the Turkish nation “at this difficult time”.

Expressing his condolences to the families of those who lost their lives, Dar wrote, “Our thoughts and prayers are with all those affected and with the missing persons and their loved ones.”

He also prayed for the success of search and rescue operations.

World.title: Armed clash between two clans claims 8 lives in Sindh's Dadu
World.content:
HYDERABAD: Eight individuals were killed while two others were injured in an armed clash between two groups of the Chandio clan in Dadu district in the early hours of Sunday.

According to a police report, the feud between the two sides was the result of an “ongoing blood feud and disputes regarding the use of a common passage and other land-related matters”. The incident took place in the jurisdiction of the Jhallo police station.

Hyderabad Range Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Tariq Dharejo confirmed the incident, adding that the deceased were wanted in some criminal cases by police as well. Out of eight deceased, two belonged to Sikandar Chandio’s group, and six belonged to Ali Akber Chandio’s side.

He said that efforts had been underway to bring about reconciliation between the two sides, but in vain.

The deceased from Sikandar Chandio’s group were identified as Usman Chandio’s son Deedar Ali and his brother, Gul Bahar. Usman’s son Mumtaz and Kehar Khan Chandio’s son Ghulam Qadir were injured from the group.

Meanwhile, the deceased from Ali Akbar Chandio’s side included Gahi Khan’s son Fida Hussain; Zulfiqar alias Watani, son of Mohammad Waris Chandio; Mohammad Bachal, son of Mohammad Bux Chandio; Akbar Chandio’s sons Sultan and Manzoor; and Arshad alias Hajjan, son of Usman Chandio.

The deceased and injured were shifted to the Dadu District Headquarters Hospital.

DIG Dharejo said that the two sides had exchanged gunshots on several occasions in the last three years because they were at loggerheads. These clashes had earlier also caused the deaths of two persons each from both sides. Nine others had received injuries, while their cases were pending in court.

He noted that among the deceased, Gul Bahar was involved in eight cases, Fida Hussain in one, Zulfiqar in seven, Bachal in 11, Manzoor in five and Arshad alias Hajjan in one case as per police record. Injured Ghulam Qadir was involved in two cases.

Dadu Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Mir Saddam told Dawn that the incident took place Sunday morning when Ali Akbar Chandio’s men attacked Sikandar Chandio-Khan Mohammad Chandio side, leading to a fierce clash and ending up in multiple deaths.

He added that some arrests have been made by police and weapons were recovered. The bodies from both sides were unburied as of Sunday evening.

SSP Saddam disclosed that Ali Akbar Chandio wanted to avenge the killing of his school-going nephew because Ali Akbar’s brother had not agreed to the reconciliation proposal involving Khan Mohammad Chandio.

He said that the area where casualties took place was mostly a riverine area.

“Police have been deployed there to control the situation from escalating any further,” he said.

World.title: Nepal-China flood death toll rises to nearly 800, with over 3,000 missing
World.content:
Devastating floods near the border with China killed at least 781 people in Nepal, its disaster authority said on Sunday, with 2,502 people missing as rescue efforts continued for a fifth day.

Chinese state media earlier confirmed 16 dead in Tibet and 546 people missing following Wednesday’s disaster, taking the overall toll to 797 dead and 3,048 unaccounted for.

Nepal’s missing list includes 592 foreigners unaccounted for. It also includes 933 workers on hydropower projects along the river which the torrent crashed through, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.

Nepal’s disaster agency listed 1,910 missing citizens in an update on Sunday. That includes 562 unaccounted for in the hardest-hit district of Rasuwa.

In India, authorities said they had recovered seven bodies from rivers flowing from Nepal, believed to be flood victims. However, they are not included in the toll.

The Red Cross has estimated that more than 90,000 people are likely to have been affected by the disaster, which China has linked to the effects of climate change.

Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi told his Nepalese counterpart during a Saturday telephone call that the mudslide was their “most severe cross-border disaster” in recent years and that rescue operations had risen to an unprecedented level of difficulty and complexity, state broadcaster CCTV reported.

On the Chinese side, authorities said 16 people were killed in Gyirong County, and 546 were missing. Beijing said 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries were unaccounted for in Tibet, near a key border crossing with Nepal.

The scale of the disaster has complicated rescue efforts across the rugged Himalayan terrain.

Local police in Nepal told Reuters that residents and rescue workers had moved to higher ground after the Trishuli River’s water levels rose in recent hours following fresh rainfall, raising fears of additional flooding.

Rescue operations have been suspended several times since Friday because of bad weather and concerns that a lake formed across the Nepal-China border by the disaster could trigger fresh flooding after it began overflowing into Nepal’s Lhende Khola and Trishuli Rivers.

CCTV reported that the lake threatening downstream areas had been largely drained by Saturday evening. But drones detected a landslide late on Saturday that is 2.8 kilometres downstream of the lake, forming a new dam and a fresh pool of water.

In Nepal, rescue efforts have become more focused on hundreds of people believed to be trapped inside tunnels at hydropower plants damaged by the floods.

Lok Bahadur Chhetri, a spokesperson for Nepal’s foreign ministry, said Nepal required international assistance in specialised areas, including tunnel rescue operations, DNA testing, refrigerated storage for bodies and forensic identification of decomposed remains.

Indian and Chinese experts were already working to help open tunnels and support rescue operations, Chhetri said.

Mass burials of decomposing bodies

Days after desperate relatives moved between hospitals, morgues and relief centres searching for loved ones, authorities in Nepal began mass burials of hundreds of unidentified victims whose bodies had started to decompose.

In Chitwan district, which escaped the direct impact of the disaster, bodies swept downstream from the flood-hit Rasuwa region have been carried by the river system into the Narayani River.

Authorities are photographing the bodies, collecting DNA samples and recording identifying details in the hope that families may still be able to identify relatives after burial.

“Of the bodies we have recovered so far, more than half are beyond recognition,” police officer Anil Thapa told Reuters.

“Many have no visible faces. In some cases, only hands or legs remain; in others, only parts of the body are available. In many cases, more than half of the head is missing.”

After burying more than 100 unidentified bodies on Saturday, authorities were digging additional graves on Sunday for hundreds more.

Link to ‘long-term effects of climate change’

The flood was “caused by glacier instability under the long-term effects of global warming”, CCTV reported, saying it was a “new and prominent feature of cryosphere disasters” on the Tibetan plateau.

The mudslide from the Nepalese side took six to seven minutes to reach the Gyirong border crossing, CCTV said, citing the findings of Chinese scientists. Dramatic surveillance footage shared worldwide showed torrents of water and debris engulfing buildings while people tried to flee.

The state-run TV channel reported China has mobilised more than 2,100 rescue workers and allocated at least 220 million yuan ($32.7m) to support relief efforts and has been airdropping equipment and supplies to frontline rescuers, while its soldiers used life-detection equipment to look for the missing.

World.title: 'They can come to Pakistan today': Khawaja Asif disputes claim by Imran's sons of expired Nicops
World.content:
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on Sunday said that PTI founder Imran Khan’s sons — Qasim and Sulaiman Khan — could visit Pakistan “today if they wished”, citing the validity of their National Identity Cards for Overseas Pakistanis (Nicop).

The government has consistently maintained that Imran’s children can enter the country based on their Nicops with no visa required. However, the sons claimed earlier this month that their Nicops have expired and accused the government of denying them visas.

In a post on social media platform X, the defence minister recalled that the ex-premier’s sons had last travelled to Pakistan on their Nicops in November 2022, when the PTI founder got injured in an assassination attempt.

“They can visit Pakistan today if they wish. Both Nicops are valid,” Asif stated.

He also shared partially censored Nicop numbers for both Kasim and Sulaiman, stating that the document was valid until Nov 8, 2032 for Kasim and Jan 6, 2030, for Suleman.

The minister dismissed the perception that the government was denying them visas as “incorrect”, accusing Imran’s family and PTI of concocting the narrative.

“Holders of Nicops can travel to Pakistan whenever they wish. There is no need for a visa,” he maintained.

A day earlier, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MOIB) had addressed the potential arrival of Imran’s sons, noting that they may enter the country through their Nicops, but that access to the country may not guarantee access to prison visitation.

Zulfi Bukhari, adviser to Imran on foreign media, responded to the government’s stance on his recent CNN interview with a lengthy statement. He reiterated his claims of the PTI founder being kept in “solitary confinement” and detailed medical concerns raised in a doctor’s assessment submitted to the Supreme Court.

Sons want to meet their father

As Kasim and his older brother Suleiman live in London with their mother and Imran’s former spouse Jemima Goldsmith, they will have to travel to Pakistan to meet Imran, who is imprisoned at Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail.

In December 2025, Kasim had said that he and his brother had applied for their visas. However, in February, Kasim claimed that the government was “deliberately” refusing to process his and his brother’s visas.

The next month, Goldsmith made a “direct appeal” to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to grant her sons visas.

In response to the appeal, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said that Imran’s children were welcome to visit Pakistan on their Nicops.

Meanwhile, Goldsmith alleged that the government was recommending that her sons travel to Pakistan on Nicops as they would have “no British protection”, expressing fear that they may be arrested on arrival.

In her statement, Goldsmith had claimed that the government was refusing her sons’ visas and held that they also did not have their renewed Nicops.

Imran was sent to jail on August 5, 2023, in the Toshakhana case. However, he is also serving a 14-year sentence in a £190 million corruption case , was convicted in another Toshakhana case in December 2025 and also faces pending trials in terrorism cases related to the May 9, 2023 riots .

The ex-premier’s sons, along with his party and family, have been protesting against the lack of meetings and phone calls with him despite court orders for the same.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels.
